title: Devotion to God
text: After getting ready in the evening, Swamishri arrived at the Wangara sabha hall to walk. After finishing his walk, he arrived to our mandir situated in Double View at 6:35 PM. He did darshan of Thakorji with love and then performed arti. Then remembering old smrutis he said, “I have done many kathas here.” The haribhakto present there did darshan of the small Harikrishna Maharaj situated there and replied, “Swami! In 1998 you had performed pujan of this murti and then sent it here. This murti was going to come here from India in a sealed container. You said, ‘How will Thakorji breathe?’ Saying this you had the container changed.” Such was Swamishri's parabhakti and attention to Thakorji’s needs."

title: Attention to Details!
text: Swamishri did abhishek of Ghanshyam Maharaj in the abhishek mandapam. Soon after, Shrijiswaroop Swami was called near. Behind Ghanshyam Maharaj, there is a peepal tree with a murti of Ghanshyam Maharaj looking west. Situated on different parts of the tree, Ghanshyam Maharaj's friends are all looking at him. Pointing at one child situated in the front, Swamishri said, "There are many wrinkles on his cheeks. They should be removed." Thereafter, as he offered pradakshina to the murti, he said "It bothers me every day." Only after Swamishri mentioned it, did everyone see it. They started to talk amidst each other, "We have done darshan for many years. Thousands and Millions have come here, but this did not come to anyone's attention." As per Swamishri's #Agna the wrinkles were removed from the boy's face. The next day, when Swamishri was shown, he gestured and said "Finally! He is now laughing."

title: Importance of Ekadashi
text: While giving blessings on 'Yogi Vani' in the morning, Swamishri said, "One should not sleep on Ekadashi. We stop for many things when compelled, so similarly we should also stop as the great sadhu tells us. We will get a thousand times the fruits. They tell us with love. They are not forcing us or behaving hypocritically. By any means, we must stay awake on Ekadashi. We should put in our efforts to follow Maharaj's orders."

title: An Eagerness for Devotion
text: After having darshan of Thakorji, Swamishri left for Mumbai from Nashik. The car started moving towards the airport. On the way, Hariprakash Swami started an impromptu goshti and asked, 'Swami! What time did you wake up this afternoon?' Swamishri said, '2 o'clock.' Hariprakash Swami asked, 'Aren't you feeling sleepy?' Swamishri said, 'No no...' Hariprakash Swami asked, 'If you wake up early in the morning and early in the afternoon, don't you feel tired?' Swamishri said tired from what? Hariprakash Swami said, 'When you get older, you feel tired more and sleep more. So what is the reason behind feeling less sleepy?' Swamishri replied, 'I have an eagerness to do bhajan.'

title: Coloring our Hearts
text: During the evening Pushpadolotsav sabha, Swamishri gave ashirwad: "If we keep devotion in our life, Bhagwan comes to us. If we do pure devotion, then our hearts become more and more pure. And it has happened – thousands of devotees have become ekantik in Shriji Maharaj's time. The happiness there is in becoming ekantik, is nowhere else. In any situation, there will only remain happiness. We do these festivals for this very reason: to make our hearts pure. These festivals are here to color our hearts. We need to color our hearts in such a way so that nothing besides Bhagwan remains."

title: What Swamishri likes?
text: Swamishri finished his morning breakfast at 8:37 AM and then went to rest. Once Swamishri woke up, he sat down to write letters. Swamishri has a unique interest in homeopathic medicine and a doctor called during that time regarding a similar medicine. The doctor began to ask Swamibapa questions regarding Swamishri's homeopathic treatment. There, the doctor asked Swamishri, "Since you have taken on such a large responsibility, do you feel that you ever worry about it?" Swamishri simply responded with a clear 'no.' The doctor then asked another question, "What do you like to do?" Swamibapa said, "Bhajan and meeting the haribhakto." Swamishri's mind is constantly absorbed in God and bhajan of God. Due to this, there is no worry or tension in Swamibapa's mind.

title: Four Values to enter Akshardham
text: After finishing his dinner, Swamishri returned to his place of residence. At that time, P. Atmaswarup Swami asked Swamishri, "Swami! Kishores from London have asked a question, 'Which four values or qualities must be required to go to Akshardham? And if we have those qualities, will you give us the stamp to enter Akshardham?'" Swamishri was pleased and began responding to the kishores' question, "One is to eliminate abhav-avgun from our roots, we can not even touch that. Yes, then there is divyabhav; and then there is mahima; and to become das na das."

title: Tranquility through Bhakti
text: After Pramukh Swami Maharaj's 97th Birthday Celebrations, Swamishri started eating his dinner. Gunvatsal Swami said, "Today, you sat for three and a half hours during Swamibapa's birthday celebrations. You did not even get up to use the restroom or drink water." Swamishri said, "I did 300 malas." All of the sadhus nearby went, "Oh!" The sevak sant asked, "Did you remember Bapa?" Swamishri replied, "Who else should I remember?". He added, "I only did mala in one way." Gunvatsal Swami then asked, "Even with so much going on?" Swamishri replied, "Bapa's virtues were being praised, what's that have to do with everything else going on?" Gunvatsal Swami responded, "Are you not worried about the kitchen and parking facilities since so many people have come?" Swamishri squinted his eyes and said, "I was not worried, I was relaxed." This is the calm and relaxed state of the Gunatit Satpurush.

title: A Strong Desire
text: Early in the morning at 2:00 AM, Swamishri woke up wanting to take a bath. After completing his daily rituals, he was all ready at 3:45 AM. Now? Swamishri came with his own solution. He sat to read his favorite scripture, 'Purushottam Bolya Prite' for almost an hour and a half from 3:45 to 5:10! His sevak Munichintan Swami was asked, "So why did Swamishri not come outside early at 5:00?" Munichintan Swami replied, "He was so engrossed in his reading that he lost track of time."

title: My Mistake
text: At exactly 8:16 PM, Swamishri arrived in Sarangpur. After doing mandir darshan, he sat down to eat his dinner. During that, Kothari Bapa and Doctor Swami fed Swamishri laadus and Swamishri fed them laadus. All of a sudden, Swamishri gave samip smruti to Aksharcharan Swami sitting on the ground and threw a laadu at him, but the laadu fell a little bit in front of Aksharcharan Swami. Aksharcharan Swami collected the laadu after it bounced once. Swamshri immediately said, "My mistake." The nearby santo then said, "No Swami, what mistake did you make?" Aksharcharan Swami said, "Swami! I was supposed to extend my arm and collect the laadu." But Swamishri remained firm in asserting that it was his own mistake.

title: The Importance of Bhajan
text: During lunch, Apurvapurush Swami, one of the main santo leading the creation of the Paramanand Show, asked Swamishri, "Swami! The theme for the Paramanand Show is 'Bhajan Karvu ne Karavvu (To do bhajan and have others do bhajan)' We have kept Bapa's slogan. Is that alright?" Swamishri emphasized, "That is the main thing. All other activities will go on."

title: The Blessings of a Child
text: Doctor Vismay's little child Mitransh was also seated for Swamishri's bhojan darshan at night. After the meal was over, Swamishri called the little boy closer to him with love. And out of nowhere, Swamishri bowed his head to Mitransh and beckoned him to bless him. Mitransh extended his hand with childlike innocence. Just as the boy's hand reached Swamishri's head, the santo started to call him back. Mitransh pulled his hands back, but Swamishri's humility touched everyone. "Such a big guru wishes for even the blessings of a child!" It may seem normal, but try to put it in practice by bowing your head to a child.

title: Following Agna Directly
text: After departing from sabha, Swamishri returned to his place of residence. As he was waiting for his meal, P. Atmaswarup Swami remembered a 9 year old balak from Wellington, New Zealand and spoke to Swamishri, "You came to this balak's dream and gave him agna to observe tap and he took this agna to heart and did a 40 day liquid fast." Hearing this, Swamibapa became very happy with the 9 year old balak and responded, "He even obeys agna from his dreams." In Swami's response, the suggestive message was echoed that '...then we must obey agna directly!'

title: Das na Das
text: During Kishore Din, Swamishri was asked, "What is your name?" They had placed 4 options in front of him: 1) Aksharbhrama, 2) Sadhu Keshavjivandas, 3) Bhagwanna Akhand Dharak, and 4) Das na Das. All of these options were correct, but since he had to choose, he picked, "Das na Das. Everyone's das, Sadhu Keshavjivandas."

title: Enthusiasm for Seva
text: At 8:50PM, Swamishri had sat down in his dining room. At that time, P. Anandjivan Swami said, "Years ago, we had an old mandir in Sankari where if we crossed the road, there was a building there. There was a field behind the building and a shibir was to be held there. Mahant Swami Maharaj arrived and said that there were used dantan sticks laying all over the field. For many years, people would come to this field and throw their used dantan sticks there. You (Swamishri) immediately took on the seva. You found a bucket by yourself and began to pick up the used dantan sticks. We all ran to you when we say this and tried to stop you by saying, 'we will take care of it,' but you replied to us, 'No, you do it and we will do it as well.' And you stayed to help us till the very end."

title: Love for Bhakto
text: Swamishri had arrived for mulakats with haribhakto. Just like usual, the mulakats quickly started. There, an elder around the age of 66 arrived. He started asking something. The local volunteers knew from experience that there was no substance to his questions and it also disrupted the flow of the mulakats, so the volunteers guided him forward but how does Swamishri let this go? Immediately, Swamishri called the elder man back and asked using his hands, "What was the question? Do tell." The uncle then pointed to his white hair and asked Swamishri, "Should I dye my hair black or should I shave my head?" Everyone laughed and Swamishri smiled and responded, "Shave it."

title: Mala na Manka
text:
During the Yuva Din sabha in the evening, the yuvaks performed the "Mala na Manka" drama. After the drama, the yuvaks approached Swamishri with an iPad.

A question was displayed on the iPad: "We would also like to become "Mala na Manka" (the beads of His mala). How can we achieve that?"

There were four options listed under the question:
(1) Washing the kitchen utensils (2) Cleaning seva (3) Doing katha-varta (4) Decoration seva

Swamishri had to select one from these options. But he had something different altogether in his mind. He asked for the microphone and revealed his thoughts, "Whatever you do, even if it just a little, if you keep divyabhav, then you can become a bead on His (Bhagwan's) mala."

title: Heartfelt Prayers
text:
Today was Swamishri's Bhagwati Diksha din. On this occasion, Swamishri was requested to write a message to his guru Yogiji Maharaj. Swamishri wrote a wonderful message:

"Always, forever, I have only one prayer that may I always have divyabhav in everyone, and may that divyabhav always increase."

title: The Taste of Prapti
text:
During Swamishri's breakfast, Chaitanyamurti Swami narrated the prasang as follows: In the year 2000, Swamishri was having lunch. There were children from abroad sitting across him for darshan. Their eyes were on Swamishri's plate. Swamishri was joyfully eating. Reading the children's mind, Swamishri asked, "Do you want to try it?"

The children wanted to know, "What does Swamishri eat?". Swamishri gave them parvar nu shak and rotlo as prasadi. The balaks tasted it and immediately expressed, "Yuck…yuck, We did not like that." One balak even asked, "How do you even like this?" "I experienced the joy of having met Yogiji Maharaj," Swamishri responded

title: A Sea of Humility
text:
Adarshjivan Swami entered the room. Seeing him, Swamishri immediately folded his hands. "You shouldn't fold your hands," Adarshjivan Swami said.

"Hands automatically fold," Swamishri responded. Swamishri naturally folds his hands, bows down, and performs danvats (prostrations). Similarly, once after puja in Atladara, Swamishri folded his hands to the haribhaktas for 16 minutes and 2 seconds. "Don't you get tired," Swamishri was once asked regarding him folding his hands all the time.

"I don't get enough of it," Swamishri replied. Everyone realized the joy Swamishri derives from folding his hands and bowing to others (dasbhav).

title: A Life Full of Love
text: During Swamishri's puja, balks were reciting mukhpath. One balak stood up and recited a verse by Yogiji Maharaj written in the Yogi Gita, "When Shastriji Maharaj would call me by 'Yogi', I would get very excited." Then the balak continued, "Swami! Just like that, when you call me 'Tilak', I feel joy." Immediately, Swamishri looked up and called Tilak closer and lovingly called out 'Tilak' twice. Upon hearing this, the balak became very happy and returned to his seat. Our guru makes so much effort to please us. Whatever we ask him to do, he does it. In reality, we should be doing as he says.

title: The Himalaya of Humility
text:
Swamishri has so much mahima for everyone. Even though Narayanmuni Swami urged him not to, Swamishri still placed the charanraj (the dust) of all the site seva volunteers on his head. Dasbhav is so deep-rooted in Swamishri that he even has dreams about it.

Once, during a dream, Swamishri did dandvats to all the Sadguru santo while holding onto their feet. He has also had dreams where he did danvats to the sevak santo, and also to yuvaks who did mukpath of the Satsang Diksha. Swamishri is able to have dreams like this because of his innate humility.

title: The Arti of Arti
text:
After finishing his morning rituals, Swamishri arrived at the mandir. He did darshan of the Guru Parampara and the deities. He performed arti in the central shrine. As he was leaving, he returned to Ghanshyam Maharaj's shrine for darshan again. "Did you sing arti?" Swamishri asked the devotees seated nearby. "Yes," they responded. "Arti should be sung at a slower pace," Swamishri explained, while moving both his hands from top to bottom.

Swamishri has an intense liking to perform all ahniks properly and peacefully.

title: Devotion to the Divine
text: At 10:20 AM, they arrived to the mandir in Chigwell. They completed the pratistha ceremony. The annakut was arranged. The arti was lit. Swamishri saw that Thakorji was facing him. Immediately, he turned Thakorji 90 degree. That is, in such a way, that the right side of Harikrishna Maharaj was visible to Swamishri. He said to his sevak, "Thakorji should also eat the annakut."

title: They Right Medicine
text: During Swamishri's rest period during his walking exercise, Vedantpriya Swami started narrating the special qualities of Pujya Tyagvallabh Swami by saying, "Whatever haribhakta comes with whatever problem, Tyagvallabh Swami always says: 'I will do prarthana. Chant the Swaminarayan mantra. It is very miraculous.' This is his medicine." Swamishri said with emphasis, "It is the correct medicine."

title: A Dedicated Sevak
text: Swamishri and Sadguru Snato reached Yagnupurush Dwar to inaugurate it. They were waiting for Gujarat's Chief Minister Vijay Rupani and other dignitaries to arrive. Thakorji was seated next to Swamishri. The sun was scorching and was falling straight on Thakorji. Without telling or hinting to anyone, Swamishri himself stood up as Thakorji's shade. After the inauguration, the Cheif Minister and other dignitaries went for darshan at the mandir and were going to come to inaugurate the exhibition. There was about 10 minutes to spare, during which Swamishri decided to answer haribhaktos letters. Even in such a big festival, Swamishri thought about his haribhakto.

title: Mahima of Devotees
text:
After finishing his daily routine, Swamishri arrived at the mandir for Mangala arti at 6:00 AM. After doing darshan, Swamishri was returning to his residence. While coming and going to the mandir, Swamishri would meet everyone with his eyes. While they were going back, Apurvamuni Swami asked, "Swami, they are all the same."

Swamshri enthusiastically said, "However many times we meet them, it is less. We benefit everytime we meet them."

title: Keeping Nirdoshbuddhi
text: As Swamishri was leaving from the abhishek mandap, a child named Harsh Mamtora from the Ghatlodia district was standing near the steps dressed as a kite. He said to Swamishri while swaying to both sides, "Swami! I am a kite. Some take me this way and some take me that way. Some even cut me off. But above all, I want to go to Akshardham. What should I do?" Swamishri laughed and said, "That's an important topic…" Then showing the remedy he said, "Keep Nirdoshbuddhi."

title: Mahima of Mutko
text: At 10:38 AM, Swamishri left the Jholi Parva sabha and entered the elevator. For one continuous hour, Swamishri gave samip darshan labh. Speaking of it, Swamishri said an incredible sentence, "Where should we go to have darshan of infinite muktas? Here, everyone was in front of me. So, I sat down." Shortly thereafter, after stepping down from the elevator, Swamishri said, "I can see all of the muktas, who should we say no to?" While seeing everyone, Swamshri made his way to the sant ashram elevator. There, Atmaswarup Swami said, "Today, the entire Ahmedabad has been seen." Swamishri immediately replied with mahima, "I got the darshan of infinite muktas right here."

title: Devotion through Seva
text:
At 11:05 AM, Mahant Swami Maharaj returned to his residence after the opening of a new building. There were a stack of letters. Upon seeing this, Yogvijay Swami said, "Don't you get tired of signing all of these letters?" Swamishri replied, "No. I do not get tired at all."

On an earlier occasion, Shrutipriya Swami had asked the same question to which Swamishri responded, "We're able to offer devotion to Thakorji [through signing the letters]."

Until 11:35 AM, Swamibapa continuously signed 256 letters. Swamishri seized the opportunity to offer his devotion!

title: Above Taste
text:
During dinner, Gunvatsal Swami had a doubt that the parvar (pointed gourd) might be bitter. Munichintan Swami tasted the parvar and they were indeed bitter. They asked Swamishri and he nodded in agreement. The sevaks asked Swamishri, "Why didn't you say anything? You ate three bitter parvar."

Trying to hide his virtues (of non-taste and tolerance), Swamishri responded, "After I ate the first parvar, I thought the second wouldn't be bitter, and then the third..."

In reality, if we had one bitter bite, we probably wouldn't take a second bite. We would reject the food. But here, everyone present witnessed Swamishri's niswadi virtue (no attachment to taste) and detachment.

title: Mahima for Everything
text:
Yogiji Maharaj used to do danvats to haribhaktas' luggage. Similarly, Mahant Swami Maharaj bows down to the different objects belonging to haribhaktas brought to be made prasadi. He has bowed down to haribhaktas' laptops; wedding invitations; santo's footwear; dhotiya-gatariya belonging to santo; and even the room doors where santo stay.

In Surat, they once brought stuffed animals to be made prasadi. Swamishri placed his hand on the heart of the stuffed animals as if he were doing pratishta. Then he did charansparsh (touching the feet with reverence) to the stuffed animals. Swamishri has true mahima and dasbhav not only of the haribhaktas, but also the objects that belong to them.

title: Humble Service
text: Divyanand Swami was having a conversation with Swamishri in his room. He recently had an operation on one of his legs and so was sitting in a wheelchair. Once Divyanand Swami's conversation was over he became perplexed as to who would push his wheelchair and take him out. He managed to take his wheelchair to the door and tried to push the door open with his normal foot. However, by that time, Swamishri started pushing his wheelchair. On coming out of the room everyone was surprised at what they saw. When someone tried to handle the wheelchair Swamishri refused and smilingly wheeled the chair into the lobby. Swamishri did not hesitate at all in serving a young sadhu, and felt great joy in serving him. Humble service is Swamishri's innate nature.

title: 2 Wings to Akshardham
text:
In the evening, Swamishri was writing letters. A question, in one of the letters, stated: "Mahant Swami Maharaj! What can we do to make you happy?"

Swamishri wrote a wonderful reply saying "Agna and Upasana should be firm. This is not a small thing – this encompasses everything. With these two wings, you can fly and go to Akshardham."

title: Divyabhav in All
text:
After finishing chesta, Swamishri went for his evening bath. On his way, he saw a white board that had something written on it: "Make a mind which never minds…"

Based on that statement, a sadhak named Dhigantbhai drew a picture showing one person taking away a ball of another person. The owner of the ball screamed out loud, "Hey! That my ball!" referring to the above statement the second person replied, "Hey! I hope you don't mind me." After reading and observing the sketch, Swamishri on the bottom of the sketch wrote "Why should I? You are a MUKTA"

Everyone present there witnessed Swami Bapa's divyabhav in everyone. no Matter if they are doing wrong, Swamishri sees everyone as a MUKTA.

title: Yogi Bapa's Slogan
text:
During the special evening sabha of Yogi Jayanti, yuvaks asked Swamishri, "What expectations do you have from us?"

Swamishri replied, "Keep Yogi Bapa's slogan of 'Samp, Suhradbhav, and Ekta'. There is no room for abhav avgun in that. It goes away. And keep a behavior that does not shame your guru."

title: The Qualities of Samp
text:
After Swamishri's dinner, a 12-year-old balak named Vedansh stood up. He had a question in his mind, which he asked Swamishri, "Swami! What would life be like without samp?"

Everyone, including Swamishri, was surprised to hear such a question from such a young balak. Swamishri was pleased.

Then Swamishri asked for the microphone and responded, "If there is no samp, then there will be court cases, people will fight, and there will be conflicts at home. See, if there is samp, we would be sitting together, like we are today! They would cooperate with each other, set aside their personal preferences, and tolerate insulting words. All these are the qualities of samp!"

title: Vairagya Towards Vanity
text:
Swamishri arrived at night in his room to rest. Even though the room temperature is usually 27 C (80 F), he still wears a beanie and shawl. Today, a new beanie came. The sevak sant offered it to Swamishri, who said, "no."

"It's just like the one you wear," the sevak sant said.

"We have this one," Swamishri responded while pointing to the old one.

"But use this new one," the sevak sant continued. "It will eventually become wide (fit comfortably)."

"Let's just keep only one like that," Swamishri replied.

"If you wear this new one, then the old one can get washed," the sevak sant cleverly insisted.

"Wash it tomorrow," Swamishri stated.

"Bapa (Pramukh Swami Maharaj) was just like that," Shrutipriya Swami commented, referring to Swamishri's detachment to new objects just like Pramukh Swami Maharaj.

title: A Das's Delight
text:
After breakfast, Swamishri was going to take a nap. Before resting, he sat up for a bit. As he laid down to sleep, he raised both his hands and said, "I, Sadhu Keshavjivandaas, am everyone's das."

"Swami! You are everyone's Guru," Munichintan Swami clarified.

"There is great joy in being a das," Swamishri immediately responded. "[Trying to act superior] to others will cause trouble for one's self and others."

title: Tolerating for Others
text:
Swamishri's dinner was arranged in the Yagnapurush Sabha hall due to the ongoing sant shibir. Extra halogen lights were arranged on the stage to allow the santo to see Swamishri clearly.

About 2-3 minutes after Swamishri started his dinner, Gunvatsal Swami pointed at the halogen lights and asked Swamishri, "Aren't you feeling hot [due to these halogen lights]? How can you sit here?"

Swamishri replied in just one sentence, "Everyone is getting labh!"

For the past 3.5 hours, Swamishri had sat under the hot halogen lights without any complaint.

title: This is Not Bhido for Me
text:
After singing chesta, Swamishri went for a bath. Then he arrived back in his room. Earlier that day, Swamishri had participated in various activities during the kishore-kishori din sabha.

"Please forgive us for any bhido (difficulty, discomfort, hardship, etc.) you had to face during the kishore din sabha today," Uttamshlok Swami apologetically said.

"I don't even consider this to be bhido," Swamishri responded. "Having me just sit around is bhido to me." The Satpurush is always engaged in Satsang seva without any concern for personal health or comfort.

title: A Desire for Seva
text:
While Swamishri was having dinner, Uttamshlokdas Swami came. One sant said to Swamishri, "Your balak friend is here!"

Swamishri replied, "We did seva together - collecting cans."

Uttamshlokdas Swami added, "In 1991 during CFI, we were doing windup seva at Edison. Swamishri took the garbage can and started picking up garbage. Seeing this, I quickly went near him. There were many empty cans which were stuck inside the bushes. Swamishri would reach with his hands inside the bushes and removed all of them. We stopped Swamishri and told him to let us finish the seva. However, it was Swamishri's urge to continue, so we requested, "You hold on to the trash can and we will pick up trash and put it inside. Even then, Swamishri was keen to continue engaging in the cleanup seva."

title: Gharsabha's Guarantee
text: After his morning puja, Swamishri gave ashirvad, "Swamibapa [Pramukh Swami] has given us agna to do ghar sabha. Many things happen from doing ghar sabha. Family unity develops, your children go straight forward. They do not go astray. By doing ghar sabha, there is a guarantee that good qualities come."

title: Hardships for Haribhakto
text:
After having dinner and giving devotees darshan, Swamishri directly went for a bath. Today, Mangaldarshan Swami had the opportunity of bathing Swamishri.

He recalled one occasion when Swamishri had done hectic travel. He said: This prasang took place in 1994, before the consecration of murtis here [in Mahesana]. There was a mass marriage of the Rajput Community in the village of 'Nava Navada' near Barwala. Due to great insistence, Swamishri (Mahant Swami Maharaj) traveled 200 kilometers from here to go there. Swamishri blessed everyone. After making everyone happy, Swamishri immediately returned back. He traveled almost 450 kilometers in just one day to make the devotees happy. Swamishri takes on such hardships for his devotees' joy.

title: Divine Focus
text:
After completing the abhishek of Sahajanand Varni, Swamishri called Rahul Swami near and drew his attention to the corner of Sahajanand Varni's eye and said, "It has become white here, make sure you remove it."

Rahul Swami responded, "Everyday I clean this murti but I never noticed the small water droplet that would remain. Only Swamishri was able to catch this. What amazing observational abilities!"

title: Restless Comforts
text:
Before Swamishri went for his afternoon rest, Anandvihari Swami asked him, "What do you do if you can't sleep?"

Swamishri automatically and very clearly replied "Bhajan!"

Tyagratna Swami then said, "One time, I asked Swamishri as well, 'What do you do when you can't sleep?' Swamishri responded, 'Vichar.'" I further asked, "Of what?" To which Swamishri said, "About samp."

title: Hundreds of Hardships
text:
After cheshta was completed, Hariprakash Swami remembered an incident from the day before and said, "Maheshbhai had asked you on the plane, 'Do you like the plane?' To which you (Swamishri) responded, 'I am fine even if it's a truck, and even if it is a bullock cart, I am fine with that.'"

Supporting this statement, Shreejiswarup Swami said, "On route to Delvada, you had to sleep at the train station. And in the morning, you had to bathe [and get ready] at the train station as well. There wasn't even one (devotee's) house where you could've stayed the night."

Swamishri then spoke, "I have done all sorts of travels. Cart, camel cart, bullock cart, everything."

title: Swamishri's Simplicity
text:
Every day while singing chesta, Swamishri does mala.

Today, he was using a mala offered by Shreejiprakash Swami. Referring to the mala, Shreejiprakash Swami said, "When I received diksha in 1981, I was given this mala that cost 50 paisa."

Swamishri replied, "When I received diksha, I was given a mala that cost 2 ānna. Only the ending bead of the mala has been changed since it was like the other beads."

Munichintan Swami mentioned, "Swamishri still uses the same mala for his puja."

Reference: 1 rupee = 100 Paise, 1 ānna = 6.25 Paise

title: A Mother's Love
text:
After Swamishri finished writing letters in the morning, Shri Anilbhai Nayak, the director of L&T company, came to meet him.

Swamishri blessed him and then fed him prasad with his own hands. Amidst the conversation, before anyone realized, Swamishri pointed and said, "Please give him a paper napkin."

Although Anilbhai cleaned his face with the napkin, some crumbs of prasad were still stuck around his face. But the climax of this prasang came when Anilbhai was about to leave. Swamishri felt Anilbhai's face wasn't clean enough, so he took a napkin and cleaned Anilbhai's face two to three times, very neatly and lovingly.

With great joy, the santo there said, "Just like a mother lovingly cleans her child's face, Swami cleaned Anilbhai's face."

title: Tolerating for Devotees
text:
On his way to the dining room for dinner, Swamishri started to walk up the narrow stairs. But while he walked up and down the stairs, his feet were slightly hurt twice.

Because this happened while Swamishri was going to give bhojan darshan labh, Dharmakumar Swami apologetically said, "Swami! Please forgive us. We are giving you a lot of hardships."

Swamishri gestured 'don't worry' with both of his hands and said, "This is my business."

What an amazing guru we have attained. To please us, he considers tolerating his business!

title: Subtle Worries
text:
Swamishri sat in the car with his hands folded at 4:50 PM ready to leave for Chennai.

While they were driving, Swamishri noticed that the car's air conditioning temperature was 26°C to 27°C (78°F to 80°F) for both the driver and himself. Immediately, Swamishri reduced the driver's air conditioning temperature to 20°C (68°F) so that the driver wouldn't feel hot.

Swamishri is so aware and thoughtful of even the smallest details of those around him!

title: Remembering Details
text:
Swamishri arrived for mulakat at 11:16 AM. Mayur Patel from London was also in line. Upon seeing him, Swamishri remembered that Mayur had earned a first class degree.

Everyone, including Mayur, was surprised because he had earned a first class degree from the London School of Economics. Mayur had written a letter with details on June 6, 2017, seeking ashirwad. Swamishri had responded to thousands of letters since then, yet he still remembered the details of the letter and the person. Truly, Swamishri lives in the hearts of his devotees.

title: Unity with Love
text:
During the rest period of Swamishri's walking, Shrutipriya Swami asked Swamishri, "Swami! One of our devoted haribhakta, Akhilbhai from Makrana, has asked, 'Another organization has been constructing a mandir for a long time, but it is still unfinished. Due to this, they have asked Akhilbhai multiple times to take on the project and even mentioned it wouldn't cost much, but he wanted to ask if he should accept the offer or not.'"

Swamishri answered clearly, "Yes, do it." Then he said, "We all are one! Everyone is Bhagwan Swaminarayan's." He specially added, "Do the work from your heart and to the best of your ability."

title: Faultless Vision
text:
When Swamishri arrived for his afternoon rest, a sevak sant prayed to him, "Swami, may we always see you as faultless."

Swamishri then said, "In this birth, right now, we can see everyone as faultless, if we put aside our mind's desires."

title: United by Love
text:
After the evening sabha, Swamishri came outside of the sabha hall. Here, leaders from the Jalaram Mandir came for Swamishri's blessings for their new mandir. Swamishri blessed their new mandir map. It was already very late. By the time Swamishri sat in the car, it was already 8:35 PM.

Despite being in a hurry, he called the leaders of the Jalaram Mandir again to bless them and assured them, "Your mandir will get ready. It will be completed easily without any hiccups." The leaders were very pleased.

title: Tolerating Travels
text: During lunch, Karunamurti Swami recalled a prasang from Swamishri's previous vicharan and said, "Swami! Around April - May 2003, you went to Kheralu for vicharan. There you fell ill with a fever. However, you didn't inform anyone about your condition. After conducting padhramanis at 4 to 5 places, you arrived to Siddhapur. Even though the meal was prepared and ready, you didn't eat anything and went straight to sleep. Everyone became concerned. After checking, we discovered that you were suffering from a fever. Therefore, urgent arrangements were made to take you to Ahmedabad for treatment. Even though you had a fever and endured fatigue, you tolerated everything silently without uttering a word."

title: Significance of Sabha
text:
'Ravi Sabha Din' was being celebrated and during the evening assembly, a prayer was said to Swamishri, "Swami, Yogibapa had said, 'One should attend Ravi Sabha even if one has to forgo a profit of 25,000 rupees.' Even Pramukh Swami had said, "Attend Ravi Sabha regularly." Now, please write a statement that always motivates us."

Swamishri wrote, "'Ravi Sabha is only for divine bliss.' [Signed] Sadhu Keshavjivandas."

Our gurus have placed a great emphasis on the necessity of attending weekly sabha to make our lives better.

title: Simply a Das
text:
On the way to Bhavnagar from Sarangpur, Vedmanan Swami was traveling with Swamishri for his seva. It was a perfect time to ask a few questions that he had in mind. He asked, "Swami! Numerous people come for your darshan, don't you feel any ego about it?"

Swamishri quickly replied, "They are coming for the darshan of Maharaj and Swami, not for mine."

Vedmanan Swami asked again, "You have so many cameras in front of you, and people taking your photos and videos…"

Swamishri interrupted, stating once more, "Maharaj and Swami… everything is offered to Maharaj and Swami. I am just a das (servant)…"

title: Seeing Bhagwan in All
text:
A while after starting his breakfast, Swamishri made a statement, "I was not able to do darshan of haribhakto [in puja]!" He explained the reason, "There were not enough lights." Then he gestured, "If that's the case, turn on the lights (while he does darshan of the haribhakto)."

When the santos agreed to do so Swamishri was satisfied.

Generally, the term 'darshan' is used when we behold Bhagwan's murti. Swamishri uses it for us. He sees Bhagwan in all of us.

title: Where are You From?
text:
Swamishri was heading towards his room after doing darshan at the mandir. On his way, santos from foreign countries were standing in a row. As Swamishri passed by the santo, they started to give their introductions one by one:

"I am from England."
"I am from America."
"I am from Australia."
"I am from New Zealand."
"I am from South Africa."

Gnanmanan Swami was standing outside Swamishri's room at the end of the line. He asked Swamishri, "Where are you from?"

"From Akshardham." Swamishri promptly replied. Everyone became overjoyed at hearing Swamishri's words.

title: First Thakorji
text:
Swamishri was traveling from Delhi to Mumbai on a flight. Initially, the plane was a bit warm so the santo turned the AC outlet towards Swamishri. Noticing this, Swamishri instantly had them turn the AC outlet towards Thakorji (Harikrishna Maharaj).

As the plane soared high above the clouds towards Mumbai, the sunlight fell directly on Swamishri and Thakorji (Harikrishna Maharaj). Therefore, the sevak santo decided to make arrangements to provide shade to Swamishri.

Seeing this, Swamishri said, "First [provide shade to] Thakorji." Thakorji is always foremost in Swamishri's life.

title: Blessings From A Child
text:
After lunch, Swamishri proceeded towards his room while greeting devotees on the way.

A devotee from Ahmedabad named Shyamalbhai was standing in the line holding his young child Ravi in his arms. Whenever Swamishri sees a child, he always stops to give blessings by placing his hand on the top of the child's head. The same thing happened here.

Just as Swamishri kept his hand on Ravi's head, Ravi also stretched his small hand to keep it on Swamishri's head. Seeing this, his father stopped Ravi from doing so. But Swamishri stood there laughing, waiting for Ravi to put his hand on his head. He humbly said twice, "Place your hand..."

Swamishri has never hesitated to take blessings from a child even though he is the guru of so many.

title: The Secret for Admission
text:
As Swamishri was walking towards the car after finishing shangar arti, youths from Nadiad Chhatralay were standing there doing darshan. They said, "Look..! The principal of Brahmavidyani College comes towards us! Swami! Will you give us admission into your Brahmavidyani College?"

"If you keep nirdosh buddhi (understanding that Bhagwan and Satpurush are free of all faults) in everyone, then you will get admission." Swamishri shared the secret of getting admission into Brahmavidyani College.

title: Respect for Children
text:
After the evening sabha, Swamishri sat in the car to go to the Sant Ashram. On the way, all the children that had performed in the dance during the sabha stood in a line.

A sevak pointed them out to Swamishri by saying, "These are all of the children who danced today."

Swamishri looked at the children affectionately. However, upon reaching the Sant Ashram, he corrected the sevak, saying, "They are not children. They are 'bal mukto' (liberated souls)!"

The sevak apologized, "Sorry, Swami! From now on, we will use the term 'bal mukto'."

title: Sanctified by Association
text:
Swamishri entered Yogiji Maharaj's room. Here, sadhaks present something creative everyday based on Yogi Bapa's prasangs, or incidents.

Today, they had placed a bucket of water labeled YYUC (Yogi Yuvak Upvas College) in front of Yogi Bapa's murti. Swamishri asked, "Why this?"

Shaanbhai Sadhak, the main brain behind today's creative display, was called forward. "That's how Yogi Bapa kept it," Shaanbhai said. "Those who did upvas had the chance to assist Yogi Bapa when he bathed. We've presented that here..."

Then to everyone's surprise, Swamishri suddenly dipped his hand in the bucket of water and placed the water on his head!

"Swami! This water isn't actually prasadi (sanctified)," the sevak clarified. "So then why did you place it on your head?"

"It is prasadi," Swamishri responded. "Because it was placed in front of Yogi Bapa, it is now associated with him. Therefore, it is prasadi!"

title: Indifference to Pain
text:
A specialist physician had come to check Swamishri after he finished his breakfast. After the examination, the doctor prescribed medication and advised the sevaks, "He (Swamishri) will be happy after taking this medicine."

"I am always happy." Swamishri said. Then he explained, "I said it because you asked, or else it (pain) would continue... The pain had started since I was in Kolkata (in April)."

Atmaswarup Swami asked, "What if he doesn't take this medication?"

The doctor replied, "He may experience more pain."

Swamishri said, "Atma-bal (the thought of being different from the body) allows me to continue."

The doctor said in delight, "You are very strong. Otherwise, it is tough to bear this pain. I have seen people cry as the pain increased." The doctor was very pleased and impressed after speaking with Swamishri.

title: What's in the Name?
text:
At 6:50 PM, Swamishri sat in a car to go to the evening sabha in Yogi Farm. Jigneshbhai Panchal, a well-known builder from Anand, was accompanying him. Jigneshbhai expressed his wish, "Swami, I have one wish. Please give me permission. I'm building a new house. Please allow me to name my new house as 'Keshav Palace'."

Swamishri refused to do so. Jigneshbhai insisted again. Swamishri said, "Guru's name should be highlighted."

Jigneshbhai requested again. Swamishri replied, "Pramukh Swami is there! (Then why use my name?)"

Jigneshbhai said, "Until now, all of the previous sites have been named after Swamibapa (Pramukh Swami Maharaj). Now, please allow us to name them after your name."

Swamishri replied, "Everything is encompassed in his (Pramukh Swami Maharaj's) name."

title: True Rest
text:
After mangala arti, Swamishri went to take some light rest. But after just 10 minutes of resting on the bed, he got up. Seeing this, the sevak santo asked, "Are you not sleepy? Don't you want to rest?"

Swamishri, out of pure devotion, replied, "What rest? Remembering Maharaj and Swami is [true] rest."

Remembering Maharaj and Swami at all times is true rest for Swamishri.

title: The Peak of Humility
text:
After finishing his lunch, Swamishri returned to his room. He finished his routine and bathed before going to sleep.

In the evening, Swamishri came outside in the hallway for his walking exercise. During his walk, he came near the kitchen. Outside of the kitchen, all of the santos shoes were neatly arranged in the hallway.

While walking, Swamishri folded his hands and bowed down to the shoes.

Swamishri's humbleness is higher than the highest!

title: Infinite Love
text:
After puja, musician santo from Sarangpur came to offer a garland made by the balika mandal in Bhavnagar. They requested, "Similar to how Swamibapa (Pramukh Swami Maharaj) had said 'I love you all', you have also said, 'I love you all'. So please shower your love upon us."

Swamishri compassionately replied, "You love me, but I love you a lot more."

Gunatitanand Swami Maharaj has said, "We believe that we have love for God, but God and his holy Sadhu have even more love for us (Swamini Vato 1/196)." That same Gunatit legacy and love are in Swamishri.

title: Mahima of Ekadashi
text:
While preparing for chestha, a sevak said, "Tomorrow is ekadashi."

Atmaswarup Swami remarked, "Yogibapa used to say, that [ekadashi] is the day of 'Diwali'."

The sevaks started to say in Yogibapa's style: "No eating, no drinking, staying up all night, responding to letters, and preparing reports." Swamishri agreed with his laugh.

Atmaswarup Swami added, "And enjoy the bliss of [devotion to] Bhagwan and nothing else on the day of ekadashi."

Swamishri said right away, "Yes, exactly. That's the purpose of fasting."

title: Magnificence in the Miniscule
text:
As Swamishri was heading for a shower in the afternoon, Santcharit Swami asked, "Swami! Narayanmuni Swami asked if there is insufficient lighting when you read the Shikshapatri because you take it very close to your face?"

Swamishri replied, "No, no, it has Shriji Maharaj's murti in it, and the linings of the murti are wonderful. I bring it closer so I can do darshan of it properly. However, I can read the Shikshapatri from afar too."

In the following days, the same murti of Shriji Maharaj was shown to Swamishri. He pointed out the linings on the thick paper and said, "It (the murti) looks great. I bring the Shikshapatri closer to do its darshan." He added, "This murti is beautiful... it looks innocent!"

title: Prioritizing the Prakash
text:
In the morning, Swamishri was taken to the dining room to answer letters in an open sunlit environment.

Swamishri said, "I want to read the Prakash (Swaminarayan Prakash - a monthly BAPS Gujarati magazine)."

A sevak sant reminded him about pending work and replied, "Swami! We still have scheduled personal meetings, letters to answer, and other such tasks left."

Swamishri apathetically uttered, "I haven't read the Prakash [for a long time]..."

The sevak santo suggested, "We can read it during your walking."

Swamishri responded, "There's no fun in that." Even in his busy schedule, Swamishri finds time to stay updated by reading the latest publications.

title: Brahmavidya Defined
text:
After finishing dinner, Swamishri was introduced to devotees. After meeting with the devotees, Swamishri went up in the elevator.

Here, Anantanayan Swami who had arrived from Sarangpur, was waiting upstairs outside the elevator. He presented a question that was wandering in his mind to Swamishri, "Swami! You talked about Brahmavidya this morning. Please define Brahmavidya in one sentence."

Swamishri promptly replied,

"Brahmavidya means to understand everyone to be divine (divya)."

title: A Unique Vision
text:
After completing his morning puja, Swamishri arrived at the small elevator in the sant ashram. As they were going up in the elevator, Brahmavihari Swami said, "Swami! It's very difficult for you. Everyone is hungry to get labh from you...yet you give labh and darshan very patiently!"

Swamishri replied, "I see Swamibapa (Pramukh Swami Maharaj) in everyone... [That's why I do darshan very patiently]."

Swamishri's actions reflect his divine vision and strong connection with his Guru.

title: The Taste of Discourse
text:
After waking up at noon, Swamishri ate some fruit and then drank some soup. A sevak took the remaining sanctified soup and drank it. The soup was extremely sour.

Awestruck, he asked Swamishri, "Did the soup not taste sour for you?"

Swamishri replied, "I was able to finish it because my mind wasn't focused on eating, but on listening."

While Swamishri eats [fruits and soup], he listens to the narration of the Jivan Charitras and discourses. Referring to that, Swamishri showcased how he is always focused on listening to discourses and how disconnected he is from his body and senses.

title: Thinking About Prapti
text:
Swamishri woke up at 2:20 AM in the morning to use the restroom. After finishing, he returned and went to sleep at 3:00 AM. But at 3:53 AM, Swamishri woke up again. He said, "I was not able to sleep at all."

Uttamyogi Swami curiously asked, "Then what did you do?"

Swamishri instantly replied, "Prapti no vichar!"

Uttamyogi Swami further asked, "Were you contemplating about the attainment of Bhagwan?"

Swamishri replied, "Yes!"

title: Selfless Love
text:
Every day, when Swamishri comes out from Sarvasva (his room) and walks down the stairs facing the Chiku orchard, he greets and smiles at a security guard who stands there daily.

Today, when Swamishri came outside, the security guard was not at his usual spot. Swamishri tried to find him before getting into the golf cart. Santo informed Swamishri that his spot had been changed.

Swamishri went for darshan at the mandir and then went for darshan in the Rang Mandap. When he walked down the stairs towards the murti of Shriji Maharaj seated on Rojo Ghodo in the front of the mandir, Swamishri saw the security guard standing near the murti. He delightfully said, "Chowkidar (security guard)!"

The security guard had received the news that Swamishri was looking for him. He was overjoyed by how Swamishri remembered him.

Swamishri equally showers his selfless love to all.

title: Reverence to Thakorji
text:
After Swamishri gave his morning blessings, santo from Africa offered a garland to Swamishri. Swamishri asked, "Did you offer the garland to Thakorji?"

Generally, the garland is offered to Thakorji before santo offer it to Swamishri. Despite that, because Swamishri asked, santo replied, "Let us check."

They received the answer, "Yes, it is offered [to Thakorji]."

Swamishri said, "Then it's fine. Or else instead of this garland, we would have committed a crime [against Thakorji]."

Swamishri devotion to Bhagwan comes naturally as he makes sure Thakorji is always foremost in his life.

title: An Ideal Disciple
text:
In the morning sabha after his puja, Swamishri explained Vachanamrut Gadhada 3-11.

Thereafter, Swamishri proceeded to sant ashram. Referring to the morning katha, Prabhucharan Swami asked Swamishri, "Swami, you mentioned that this was the first Vachanamrut which Yogibapa instructed you to memorize. How long did it take to memorize?"

Swamishri replied, "Instantly!"

Swamishri's action guides us to become an ideal disciple.

title: His Guarantee
text:
During the evening sabha today, highlights of Nadiad Chhatralaya's silver jubilee celebration were presented.

In the end, a group picture of all the youths who participated in the celebration along with Swamishri, was clicked. During these moments, one of the yuvaks near Swamishri asked, "Swami! Will you take us to Akshardham in this birth?"

Swamishri firmly replied, "Do you have any doubt?" Everyone was overjoyed.

We have met Swamishri who has guaranteed liberation for all of us. Now, it is our turn to do as he says, to reach Akshardham.

title: Attending Everyone
text:
While Swamishri was having lunch, Munichintan Swami asked out of curiosity, "Swami! Sometimes the queue of the devotees who want to meet you is long and time is insufficient. Due to this, we have to move the devotees quickly. Thus, they might not be able to talk to you as they would like. In these situations, are their wishes fulfilled or not?"

Swamishri firmly said, "Yes, indeed (they are fulfilled)!"

After hearing that, the santo said, "Although we try to speed up [the line of devotees], you never do anything hastily. That's why everyone is satisfied."

Expressing his inner feelings, Swamishri said, "I attend to every single person."

Swamishri's compassion and care for everyone is always evident.

title: The Greatness of Devotees
text:
After his evening walk, Swamishri was returning to his room. On the way, he paused at the metal bridge connecting the sabha hall and pradakshina. Many devotees were waiting there for his darshan. As usual, Swamishri folded his hands and met each devotee with his gaze before moving forward.

Seeing this incident, Yogvijay Swami commented, "Swami, they are all the same people."

Hearing this, Swamishri became a little irritated and replied, "So what if they are the same people?" Then he added, "If we do darshan of them (devotees) a thousand times, it's still not enough!"

Indeed, Swamishri's vision is endless and boundless when it comes to seeing the greatness and qualities of others.

title: The Master Key
text:
Swamishri was on his way to the mandir for Mangala arti. Near the mandir lift, students from Nadiad Chhatralay were standing for Swamishri's darshan. They had memorized quotations from the 'Vachnamrut' and 'Purushottam Bolya Prite' on the topic of dasbhav (humility).

As soon as Swamishri came near the lift, the students started saying the quotations spontaneously. As he was going up in the lift, Swamishri joyfully listened to the presentation by the students.

Finally, Swamishri reinforced, "Das na das (servant of a servant)." Then he added, "The key - master key"

Swamishri strengthened the importance of humility in Satsang as he went inside the mandir.

title: Granting Akshardham
text:
After sabha, Swamishri arrived at the walkway on the lawn in the middle of the Chhatralay. This was arranged so that the students could have darshan of Swamishri closely.

At the entrance, a few students were dressed up as police officers. As soon as Swamishri took his first step, they stopped him and said, "This is the Akshar Police Station. You cannot go ahead without paying your tax. However, you don't have any money, so what will you give us?"

Swamishri replied, "Akshardham."

Everyone realized that the Satpurush (Swamishri) is capable of granting Akshardham through his wish.

title: Always a Sevak
text:
After finishing his morning puja, Swamishri arrived at the sant ashram.

A devotee was standing there and jokingly said to Swamishri, "Swami, I am Shri Krishna Pandya. I have received the 'Best Teacher' presidential award. I have served as a principal at our school (in Gondal). I have volunteered as a coordinator for many years in our Satsang fellowship. These are all my achievements. Now, please let us know what your achievements are?"

Without any hesitation, Swamishri replied, "Sevak!"

Swamishri's default thought process is to always remain a selfless sevak at heart.

title: Spreading Satsang
text:
After performing pratistha (life invocation ceremony) to the abhishek murti of Ghanshyam Maharaj (childhood form of Bhagwan Swaminarayan), Swamishri gave his blessings:

"We must listen and follow the instructions laid out by Ishwarcharan Swami. In the future, world-renowned personalities will come here, the whole universe will come here. People from 150 countries came to Dehli Akshardham and they will come here as well. Of those who are sitting here, many of us will bear witness to that, and the others will watch from Akshardham."

The satpurush travels far and wide spreading Satsang to all the corners of the world.

title: Inclination to Togetherness
text:
Swamishri was eating lunch.

After some time, Gurumanan Swami arrived to have darshan of Swamishri. In Ahmedabad, he had hurt his foot. As he entered, Vinaypriya Swami immediately offered him his seat.

Seeing this, Swamishri became very happy. With lots of mahima, Swamishri extended his arm and attempted to touch Vinaypriya Swami's feet.

Swamishri showers his immense happiness on those who keep suhradhbhav (togetherness).

title: Oneness with Bhagwan
text:
The model of Gunatitanand Swami's murti had arrived. Santcharit Swami brought both murtis (Harikrishna Maharaj and Gunatitanand Swami) at around 7:00 PM. Narayanmuni Swami and Bhadresh Swami were explaining the details about the murtis to Swamishri online. Swamishri looked at both murtis together. He looked at the murtis with and without vaghas (clothes and adornments). Swamishri observed the murtis for about 55 minutes.

He told the sevak sants, "Please do 11 malas. We have put a lot of strain on Thakorji. We turned them (Harikrishna Maharaj and Gunatitanand Swami) this way and that way. We also changed their vagha."

Swamishri was experiencing the strain that had befallen Thakorji. Swamishri shows his connection and oneness with Bhagwan through his devotion.

title: Tolerating Through Unity
text:
After performing puja of Tapomurti Shri Nilkanth Varni Maharaj, Swamishri was seated on the platform.

Suddenly, it was announced that Pujya Ishwarcharan Swami would be offering a garland to Swamishri. However, the cabin door of the lull was too close to Swamishri's seat. So, they told Pujya Ishwarcharan Swami to offer the garland from the lift and go back down.

He offered the garland from the lift, but Swamishri said, "Bring him here." Sevak santo tried to convince Swamishri that he would have to get up and wait for everything to be set again.

However, Swamishri stood up and waited for everything to be readied as Pujya Ishwarcharan Swami arrived next to Swamishri. Swamishri showered his happiness on Pujya Ishwarcharan Swami and hugged him showing the amount of unity he has to be willing to stand and wait.

title: Bring Thakorji!
text:
After finishing his routine walking, Swamishri did darshan at the mandir before heading to his room.

On his way, there was a swing. Santo requested Swamishri to have a seat on that swing. To satisfy their wish, he went near the swing, but before taking his seat he said, "Bring Thakorji!"

Thakorji arrived. Seeing this, Swamishri joyfully exclaimed, "Wonderful!" Then, he sat on the swing with Thakorji in his lap.

Even in minor actions, Swamishri never forgets to put Thakorji first.

title: Engrossed in Prapti
text:
Swamishri sat down and began to brush his teeth in the morning. Suddenly, he closed his eyes while he was brushing his teeth.

Therefore, Uttamyogi Swami asked, "Are you feeling sleepy?"

Swamishri replied, "No... I'm thinking."

Uttamyogi Swami further asked, "What are you thinking about?"

Swamishri responded, "Prapti."

Swamishri is always engrossed in doing prapti no vichar (thoughts of attaining Bhagwan and the Sant). Whenever Swamishri gets a chance, he inspires us to do prapti no vichar.

title: Unattached to Taste
text:
After finishing his dinner, Swamishri walked 100 steps and then headed towards his room. On his way, he asked the sevak santo: "Did you eat?... Did you eat?.... What did you eat?"

In this manner, Swamishri went to his room by showering his compassion. At that time, sevak santo asked, "Swami! What did you eat?"

Swamishri stopped and tried to think about it, but he couldn't recall what he had ate. Then, he laughed and said, "I eat and see the food items, but I don't know their names."

What a surprise! Naturally, people will know what they eat, but Swamishri does not even harbor crave for food.

title: Interest in Reading
text:
Today, Swamishri's exercise was not scheduled due to the ekadashi fast. Thus, Swamishri read 'Swaminarayan Prakash' for 45 minutes, before taking faral. After waking up from his rest at noon, Swamishri ate fruit and drank soup.

Uttamyogi Swami asked, "What do you want to do now?"

Swamishri enthusiastically replied, "I want to read the Prakash...and I need my glasses."

Uttamyogi Swami clarified, "You already read the Prakash this morning."

Swamishri said, "I want to read it in detail." Swamishri's inclination for reading is evergreen. He read the Prakash for another 45 minutes! In total, he read it for one and a half hour.

title: Care for Thakorji
text:
Because Dhanurmas had started, two small bowls of shiro (one type of sweet) were kept in the thal offered in Swamishri's puja.

Having a few doubts, Swamishri instantly placed his hand on the bowls to check if the shiro was too hot.

Santcharit Swami understood and asked, "Bapa, is it hot?"

Swamishri nodded his head.

Santcharit Swami said, "From now on, we will not offer shiro while it is too hot." Swamishri became completely satisfied and happy.

Swamishri cares for Thakorji to the point where he even makes sure that the food items in Thakorji's thal are never too hot for him.

title: Unphased Equality
text:
After chestha finished, an impromptu goshti started between the santos and Swamishri. Tapovatsal Swami referred to what Swamishri had talked about in the evening sabha about 'what would happen if someone garlands you with a necklace of shoes.' He said, "Today, you spoke amazingly [about the shoes garland]."

Swamishri added, "Imagine how much fun it would be!"

The santos were stunned and asked, "What fun is there in that?"

Swamishri explained, "For a sadhu, everything should be equal."

Remembering the previous day's incident, Hariprakash Swami mentioned, "Maheshbhai asked you if you liked the plane. You replied that you would be fine either way, whether it's a truck or a bullock cart."

title: Incredible Humility
text:
On the way for morning darshan, a haribhakta was standing while holding his little child.

When Swamishri came closer to them, he lovingly patted the child's head softly. Out of innocence, the child extended his arm to place it on Swamishri's head, but he wasn't able to reach.

Seeing this, Swamishri laughed, and with a hand gesture, encouraged the balak to put his hand on his head. The balak then placed his hand on Swamishri's head.

Despite being a revered guru, Swamishri is incredibly polite and humble. He showed his kindness by inviting the little child to interact with him in such a tender manner.

title: Beyond Taste
text:
During Swamishri's meal, santos were bringing dish after dish for Swamishri to try. While serving, a sevak sant said, "Swami, this is muthiyu." Swamishri ate a little piece. After a few minutes, the sevak sant served papad and said, "This is papad." Swamishri tasted a little piece of the papad.

Very softly, Swamishri said, "The first one was papad, and this one is muthiyu." Because Swamishri eats his muthiyu roasted, both items looked quite similar.

With reverence, the sevak sant said, "Swamishri, you know everything, yet you are so niswadi (no craving for tasty food). Please bless us so we can also become as niswadi as you."

Swamishri replied, "If you imbibe true understanding, then cashews, almonds, and peanuts all become the same."

title: The Greatest Reward
text:
Swamishri was on his way to the bathroom. He noticed a message on the whiteboard referring to the ekadashi fast that read, "I will bag trillions and trillions of dollars."

He asked the sevak sant, "What would be done after earning millions and trillions of dollars on ekadashi?" Swamishri replied himself, "It would bestow moksha and will please Maharaj very much."

The sevak sant then inquired, "What will happen when we please Maharaj?"

Swamishri explained, "It purifies us from within...otherwise, we are very impure. The sevak agreed. Swamishri continued, "There are a lot of impurities that need to be cleaned. It becomes clean [by pleasing Maharaj]."

Swamishri remarked on how great of a reward it is to achieve such purification.

title: A Humble Apology
text:
Today marked the beginning of a seven-day parayan on the occasion of Pramukh Swami Maharaj's dhamgaman (return to Akshardham). Many devotees gathered to take part in the parayan.

The devotees taking part in the parayan had come for Mahant Swami Maharaj's darshan. Because there were so many devotees [in the line for darshan], the santo started to hasten their darshan.

Asking for forgiveness in reference to the devotees, Mahant Swami Maharaj started his first blessings as the Guru by apologizing, "Just now, everyone quickly came and quickly went; and so if anyone was treated with disrespect, if anyone was hurt, then please don't hold it in your mind and forgive us (me)."

title: One and the Same
text:
In 1996, a family shibir in the presence of Pramukh Swami Maharaj was held in the Catskills Mountains, New York. Pramukh Swami Maharaj wanted everyone to go home from the shibir with something that they could keep for the rest of their lives. So, he decided to write out six simple niyams in English for all of the children and youth to follow.

Today, during the Kishore-Kishori Din program, Mahant Swami Maharaj was asked to choose six niyams from a list of twelve niyams that he wanted all of the kishores and kishoris of North America to follow. Surprisingly enough, Swamishri chose the exact same six niyams that Pramukh Swami Maharaj had selected in 1996.

What prapti we have attained in Mahant Swami Maharaj! Truly, Pramukh Swami Maharaj and Mahant Swami Maharaj are one and the same.

title: Solace in Servitude
text:
At night, Swamishri sat down on the bed and was supposed to go to sleep. However, he got up to bow down to all the Pujya Santo standing near the door. Pujya Narayanmuni Swami said, "It would've been okay if you didn't get up."

Swamishri replied, "No, it's not okay. If someone is eminent, it's acceptable for them. But we are 'Das na Das,' not eminent!"

Pujya Narayanmuni Swami then said, "You're right, Swami, but how often are you going to bow down? Before you go to sleep, you can just bow down once to everyone like this (folding his hands)."

Swamishri refused and said, "Das na das na das na das! That's where the real joy lies. Being a das brings true happiness. There is not a single worry in being a das, but there are many worries in being a master."

title: Vigilant Love
text:
In the evening, the Yuva Adhiveshan inauguration assembly was held with great anticipation. Swamishri, accompanied by Harikrishna Maharaj, made his way down the stairs towards the Chikuwadi and took his place in the golf cart. The yuvaks joyfully led Swamishri's carriage, infusing the environment with joy and excitement.

While everyone was absorbed in the festivities, Swamishri's thoughts were elsewhere. Observing that the yuvaks were walking barefoot, he turned to his sevak sant and asked, "Aren't their feet burning? After a whole day of intense heat, the stone tiles must still be very hot."

This concern highlighted Swamishri's deep compassion and love for everyone.

title: That's Why I'm Here
text:
At 4:47 PM, Swamishri came out of his residence to go for his routine walking. A yuvak standing there extended his wrist with a nadachadi tied on it towards Swamishri and said, "Swami! My nadachadi has become loose, so will you please tighten it for me?"

Swamishri lovingly tightened the yuvak's nadachadi. Then the yuvak said, "Swami! In this way, when looseness arises in my life, you will be there to tighten it, right?"

Swamishri then emphatically replied, "That's why I'm here!"

Wow! What a great reassurance! With Swamishri by our side, we will be able to stay strong in our Satsang through all circumstances.

title: Motherly Love
text:
Swamishri woke up from his afternoon rest at around 4:00 PM. As Swamishri was freshening up, he asked Uttamyogi Swami, "Did they eat?"

Hearing this, Uttamyogi Swami asked, "Who?"

Swamishri replied, "All of them."

Not sure who Swamishri was referring to, Uttamyogi Swami further questioned, "Who is all of them? The devotees?"

Hearing this, Swamishri replied, "No. Americano (referring to the kishores and kishoris that had come for Swamishri's labh on the Bharat Yatra)."

Having heard this, Uttamyogi Swami responded saying, "Yes, they have eaten." Swamishri showed his motherly love for the India Trip (Bharat Yatra) kishores and kishoris and made sure they were properly taken care of.

title: Prioritizing Prapti
text:
During a discussion before Swamishri retired for rest, Brahmavatsal Swami asked, "Swami, between the thought of prapti (the attainment of Bhagwan) and the thought of kartapanu (understanding Bhagwan as the all doer), which one is the main one?"

Swamishri immediately responded, "The thought of prapti. Everything is within the thoughts of prapti; it is always increasing. While the thought of kartapanu encompasses both creation and destruction, if someone focuses only on destruction, they may become detached from the higher path. However, thoughts of prapti constantly elevate you."

title: Our Daily Read
text:
The kishores and kishoris of Bharat Yatra (India Trip) had a special sabha in the evening with Swamishri. During this sabha, Swamishri was presented four different niyam options from which he would have to choose one niyam:

25-30 minute Puja
1 Vachanamrut and 5 Swamini Vato daily
15 minutes of Prapti no Vichar daily
Read Jivan Charitra daily

Swamishri read each option carefully and thereafter selected "Read Jivan Charitra daily" displaying his deep desire for all of us to read the jivan charitras and learn about the lives of Bhagwan Swaminarayan and our gunatit gurus.

title: Importance of Weekly Sabha
text:
As part of the Vadil Din program, Swamishri gave guidance to all of the attendees through a question and answer session.

The following question was asked: "We don't feel like going to weekly sabha, so what should we do?"

Swamishri responded: "Have faith in Yogi Bapa. He has given the agna that 'no matter what happens, we should attend weekly sabha.' If we follow that agna by any means, we will reap its benefits. Following Yogi Bapa's agna is priceless. Running errands (and doing other wordly tasks) are worth practically nothing."

title: Wishing Well for Others
text:
After bathing, Swamishri was busy signing some very important letters. A sevak asked, "What do you think about while signing?"

Initially, Swamishri responded with a gesture indicating that there was nothing noteworthy. Then, the sevak asked, "Do you think that the issues the devotees face will get resolved?"

Swamishri immediately replied, "Yes, I think of that."

Two days later, on December 15, 2017, in Surendranagar, while elaborating on his feelings, Swamishri said, "I always think for the betterment of all." In all of Swamishri's actions, he always wishes well for others.

title: Seeing only Satsang
text:
As part of a goshthi held during the journey to Secunderabad, Swamishri said, "I love all of the santo and parshads."

Shrijiprakash Swami then asked, "Do you love them even if they have flaws?"

Swamishri replied, "Yes."

Brahmvatsal Swami then asked, "Why do you like them if they have flaws?"

Swamishri explained, "Everyone has countless virtues, which is why they are in Satsang. They understand the importance of Satsang. After endless sadhana, they have earned their place in Satsang. So, we should not focus on their flaws. They have attained Satsang."

Shrijiprakash Swami remarked, "Swamishri is only looking at the Satsang aspect."

Swamishri agreed, saying, "Yes, that is correct. Those who have attained Satsang are the luckiest." For Swamishri, the attainment and association of Satsang are able to overshadow any flaw we may have.

title: Bhagwan's Das
text:
An eight-year-old balak named Kavish Barot from Chicago had come for a mulakat with Swamishri.

After looking at Swamishri, he asked, "You look like Bhagwan, so are you Bhagwan?"

Immediately and very politely, Swamishri responded, "No, I am Bhagwan's das (servant)."

Regardless of however many praises Swamishri is showered with, he remains steadfast in letting everyone know that he is first and foremost a das.

title: A Tireless Guru
text:
After Swamishri finished eating his lunch, the local santos prayed and requested, "Please take care of your health. You are leaving, but please come back soon."

One sant added, "Swami, please leave your exhaustion [from here] behind."

With remarkable strength and confidence, Swamishri responded, "I am not tired at all."

At 85 years old, amid such a demanding schedule and responsibilities, who else could utter such words?!

title: Guiding His Children
text:
Today, thousands of children had joined in the Bal-Balika Din program, in the sabha tent, and through a video call.

In the program, 'Akshardham na Balak Ame,' the children learned how they could become Swamishri's ideal balaks and balikas. Swamishri lovingly engaged with them by gesturing with his hands, putting smiles on all of the children's faces.

Further solidifying the message, Swamishri had selected six niyams for the children to follow to truly become 'Akshardham na balaks and balikas.' Through these niyams, Swamishri guided balaks and balikas to foster their dharma, gnan, vairagya, and bhakti in order to trek the path to building their Akshardham within.

Swamishri's subtle care and love for children is always embedded in their future growth and prosperity.

title: Putting Others First
text:
Like every day, Swamishri started distributing prasad to the santo before even properly eating the afternoon snack. He called Bhaktavatsal Swami near and started giving him blueberries from his plate.

Bhaktavatsal Swami commented, "Today you ate these blueberries well. I was watching, and noticed that you ate a little more today than usual."

Atmaswarup Swami replied, "If Swami wants, he can eat the whole bowl [of blueberries]!"

Astonished, Bhaktavatsal Swami asked Swamishri, "Then why don't you eat? This is very good for your health."

Swamishri smiled and then said, "Whatever you like, you should give to others." Wow! Swamishri lives with the intent of always putting others before himself. Unbelievable!

title: Seeing Divinity in Devotees
text:
In the evening, a graduation ceremony sabha was organized. A blanket with all of the photos of the youth in the graduating batch from the Yuva Talim Kendra, along with photos of devotees remembered in the sabha was presented to Swamishri.

When the santo went to cover Swamishri with the blanket, he immediately had them raise the blanket up. Gesturing, he said, "How can the photos of these devotees be placed at the feet?"

As soon as the blanket came up, Swamishri bowed down to all of the photos of the faithful devotees.

title: Dedication to Devotees
text:
When Swamishri had finished taking his shower, it was 1:34 PM. Seeing this, the sevak santo became pleased because it meant Swamishri could start his afternoon rest early. But this is Swamishri! Why would he go even a little early to rest? In reality, he wasn't early but compared to other days, he was ahead of schedule.

Swamishri then asked for letters sent by devotees and sat down to write letters. 5 minutes, 10 minutes, 15 minutes, 20 minutes... the sevak santo who were there to ensure Swamishri rested were sitting there waiting for Swamishri to finish. Slowly, the sevaks began to doze off and some even fell asleep, but Swamishri continued writing letters!

Swamishri wrote letters for about 40 minutes. When Swamishri finally went to rest, it was 2:17 PM! Without caring about his comfort and fatigue, Swamishri makes all of his devotees a priority.

title: Engrossed in Bhakti
text:
Today, due to the colder weather, Swamishri requested during his puja that the heaters be moved closer to him.

Reflecting on this, Santcharit Swami said, "Swami, we should have asked you earlier if you were feeling cold."

Swamishri responded, "I only felt cold towards the end... It was probably cold earlier, but I did not notice..." How remarkable!

This answer prompted Brahmavatsal Swami to ask, "Swami, were you that engrossed in doing puja that you did not notice how cold it was?!"

Swamishri replied while smiling, "Correct..." Then he provided another reason by saying, "And the mukhpath that the balaks were performing!" Swamishri was so captivated by the balaks' mukhpath that he forgot about the state of his own body!

title: Desire to Meet Devotees
text:
After meeting devotees for 45 minutes, Swamishri hurriedly walked to the bathroom and cleared his throat.

Uttamyogi Swami said, "You must've held the cough in!"

Agreeing with this, Swamishri replied, "I had to hold it in! If I get up, 15-20 minutes will go by. In that time, so many devotees would pass by (referring to the devotees coming to meet Swamishri)!"

Just to meet as many devotees as peacefully as possible, who knows how long Swamishri must have held his cough in for!

title: My Disturbance is not a Problem
text:
Swamishri was supposed to go to sleep after singing cheshta. However, mundan was scheduled for tomorrow morning. Swamishri expressed his concern saying, "This (mundan) won't disturb the sabha, right?"

Harismaran Swami replied, "No Swami, that won't be an issue. But that won't cause you any disturbance, right?"

Swamishri immediately responded, "My disturbance is not a problem, but there won't be any disturbance there (at the sabha), right?"

Santos then said, "No Swami. There will be katha going on there. When you arrive at the sabha, you will do puja and then give blessings. In that way, everything will be done on time."

Swamishri was satisfied. But Swamishri's words started a flow of thought in everyone's heart. Other than Swamishri, who else could show this much thought and concern for their disciples?

title: His Problem is My Problem
text:
During the day, Swamishri was informed of one devotee who was facing financial difficulty. This news took a spot in Swamishri's heart.

When Swamishri woke up at 1:00 AM in the night to use the bathroom, he was still worrying about that devotee.

When he woke up at 4:00 AM in the morning, he started restlessly speaking with urgency, "I am very worried about him. How can we solve this problem?" Then he said, "I am worried about him because his problem is my problem."

Swamishri makes our problems his own because he reserves us in his heart due to his love for us.

title: A Singular Thought
text:
Swamishri was traveling from Rajkot to Bhadra when suddenly the tire under Swamishri's seat blew out! The driver immediately regained control of the vehicle and safely pulled over to the left side of the road. As soon as the car stopped, many of the sevaks exited the car to assess the situation. Many wondered how troublesome it would be to fix the car or how they would get to their destination now.

In contrast, Swamishri remained calmly seated in the car. He was entirely unperturbed by the incident, showing no curiosity or concern.

Apurvamuni Swami arrived there shortly and asked Swamishri, "How could the Satpurush's car get a flat tire?"

Swamishri confidently replied, "Bhagwanni Ichha (By Bhagwan's wish)!"

Apurvamuni Swami then asked, "As you are seated peacefully, what are you thinking about?"

Swamishri simply answered, "Bhagwan."

title: Never Wasteful
text:
In the morning, Swamishri sat down to brush his teeth. He held the toothbrush in his right hand and the toothpaste in his left hand. Like every other day, Swamishri put the toothpaste on his toothbrush, but today the toothpaste slipped and fell into the steel bowl that was kept beneath.

Swamishri tried to take the toothpaste that had fallen into the steel bowl: once, twice five times! But still, the toothpaste did not come onto the toothbrush. On the sixth attempt, Swamishri was able to get the toothpaste onto the toothbrush and commenced brushing his teeth.

If we were in Swamishri's position, we would simply take new toothpaste. However, despite being the guru of such a large sanstha, Swamishri still doesn't let even the smallest item go to waste.

title: Interest in Jivan Charitras
text:
As there was no exercise scheduled today, Swamishri listened to Bhagatji Maharaj's jivan charitra. As it turns out, Swamishri completed Bhagatji Maharaj's jivan charitra in Bhagatji Maharaj's birthplace itself!

Uttamyogi Swami then asked, "Which jivan charitra do you want to listen to now?"

Swamishri enthusiastically replied, "I want to listen to Gunatitanand Swami Maharaj's jivan charitra."

Even at such an elderly age, in the midst of hectic vicharan and programs, Swamishri makes it a point to listen to the jivan charitras. Swamishri's inclination to read and listen to the jivan charitras is truly inspiring.

title: Doing Darshan of Devotees
text:
Swamishri finished performing his puja. As he does every day, he folded his hands to convey "Jay Swaminarayan" to all of the santo and devotees present.

However, since it was Jal Jhilani Ekadashi, there was a pool of water in front of him. Due to this, he couldn't do darshan of the devotees seated there.

So, Swamishri stood up and walked to the edge of the stage. Very lovingly, he did darshan of all of the devotees seated there.

Swamishri recognizes the greatness of all devotees and thus keeps a desire to always do their darshan.

title: Liking for Discourses
text:
During a goshthi on the way to Silvassa, Uttamyogi Swami asked Swamishri, "Do you like giving discourses, listening to kirtans, or listening to discourses? Do you like reading or do you like to think?"

Swamishri responded, "I like to listen to katha (discourses)."

Uttamyogi Swami further asked, "Don't you get bored listening to the same things repeatedly, as you already know everything?"

Swamishri strongly emphasized, "No."

title: Wish for Others
text:
After completing his morning puja, Swamishri imparted his morning discourse and blessings before he took leave. He went inside the lift. Today, quotes from Shriji Maharaj and the Gunatit Gurus pertaining to their wishes were written on the lift.
