In the end, the written words asked Swamishri a question: "What is your wish for us?"

Swamishri wrote in response, 'Moksha.'

Apurvamuni Swami further asked, "Whose moksha will happen first? Santos? Devotees? Balaks?"

Swamishri replied, "Those who wish for others [moksha]."

title: Tirelessly Engaged in Sabha
text:
Swamishri arrived to the sabha hall shortly before the solar eclipse started. Following Bhagwan Swaminarayan's agna of suspending all activities and chanting the name of Bhagwan in a purified state, Swamishri ceased all of his daily activities to come to the sabha for the entire duration of the eclipse.

Swamishri participated in the special sabha for more than three hours. During this time, Swamishri participated along with everyone in singing kirtans and watching the skits presented. Swamishri also responded to letters written by devotees, giving a unique memory to all present. Swamishri partook in doing dhun and even spoke on the importance of maintaining samp (unity), suhradbhav (togetherness), and ekta (oneness).

For more than three hours Swamishri sat jovially in the sabha without complaining or becoming tired of sitting there doing bhakti.

title: Importance of Niyam-Dharma
text:
Swamishri had just arrived to his room to rest in the morning when Brahmnayan Swami mentioned, "Swami! We have received a letter that poses a question. You mention, 'Niyam-dharma rahe, to samp rahe (If niyam-dharma are kept, then samp stays).' The question is 'How is that possible?' They are unable to understand."

Swamishri replied, "If niyam-dharma (moral discipline and virtues) are kept, they tend to share similarities which fosters samp (unity) and [a sense of] togetherness. And we can experience it - when someone doesn't follow niyam-dharma, unity will not form."

Swamishri shows how crucial following our niyam-dharma are to keeping samp and sharing similar mindsets to progress in satsang.

title: Bowing Down to Everyone
text:
Before Swamishri began his meal, Gunvatsal Swami requested him to bless the balaks.

Dissatisfied with this request, Swamishri responded, "No, rather than blessing them, we should bow to everyone. We should bow down seventeen times." Saying this, Swamishri quickly began bowing to everyone.

When Swamishri's response and motive behind his action was narrated to everyone present, Swamishri added, "Deficiencies do not remain in a person that [has a habit of] bowing down (remaining humble)."

title: His All: Thakorji
text:
After completing his puja, as Swamishri was returning to his residence, a group of security volunteers were waiting for him so they could take a group photo with him. When Swamishri arrived, he was requested to stand in the center.

As Swamishri stood in the center, he immediately inquired, "[Where is] Thakorji?"

Hariprakash Swami quickly brought Thakorji to Swamishri. Upon taking Thakorji in his hands, Swamishri was pleased and remarked, "You have done a great thing. Without Thakorji, [the group photo] felt meaningless."

For Swamishri, Thakorji is his everything. In the absence of Thakorji, everything is meaningless.

title: Proficient in all Pursuits
text:
A few santo were given the seva of assisting Swamishri prior to his afternoon rest. During this time, one sant introduced Naishthikpurush Swami, saying, "Swamishri, he has learned [how to play] the sitar...He plays classical [music] quite well."

With a gentle smirk, Swamishri responded, "There is no modern genre in sitar (classical is the predominant style). Contemporary music styles are common for banjos and other such instruments!"

Hearing this, the santo agreed, "You are absolutely correct."

Truly, Swamishri is proficient in all walks of life.

title: Thinking of Devotees
text:
After having dinner, Swamishri went to rinse his mouth in the bathroom. Here, Uttamyogi Swami asked Swamishri a question related to his dreams.

With a joyful grin, Swamishri responded, "I do not sleep at all; I am always thinking about the devotees...that all devotees attain moksha. I constantly have thoughts about meeting devotees."

Whether we realize it or not, Swamishri's thoughts are always with us. His example teaches us a simple yet powerful message: he is literally just a thought away.

title: Naturally Extraordinary
text:
Despite having gone to sleep 45 minutes later than usual yesterday, Swamishri woke up at his usual time and got ready. By 5:17 AM, he had already left his room.

On the way, Swamishri laughed and told the santo standing on the route, "I took time getting ready today because I thought puja was going to be in the room."

The santo awestruck, replied, "If you call this taking your time and are calmly coming at this time, then what does it look like [when you are] rushing?"

Things that seem normal to Swamishri, become a type of sadhana for us.

title: Miraculous Memory
text:
After seeing Ramswarup Swami today, Swamishri began to remember their old memories. Swamishri reminisced, "When you were a balak, you used to sing the kirtan, 'Sau par me'r karo chho Swami...(Koti vandan kariye Yogīji)' You had a sharp voice and used to sing in a high pitch [voice]."

Everyone was astonished. When Ramswarup Swami was 10 or 11 years of age, Swamishri had arrived at Gondal or Rajkot and Ramswarup Swami had sung these verses then.

Swamishri remembers so much about his devotees from even the smallest of interactions.

title: An Eternal Servant of Thakorji
text:
Swamishri was scheduled to depart from Mumbai via airplane today. Shortly after departure, per Swamishri's wish, Hariprakash Swami held up the murti of Harikrishna Maharaj near the window so that Thakorji could grace Mumbai from the skies. After some time, Swamishri mentioned, "The sunlight is beaming down [on Thakorji] over there." Such was Swamishri's concern for Thakorji's comfort.

Later, during the flight, when water was brought for Swamishri to drink, Swamishri turned to face the side before he drank the water. Seeing this, Gurumanan Swami asked him why he drank the water in this manner. Swamishri gestured toward Thakorji, who was seated in front of him, implying that it is not appropriate to drink water while seated directly in front of Thakorji.

Swamishri is eternally a servant of Thakorji. Thus, he is always mindful of Thakorji's needs and unceasingly maintains respect for Thakorji.

title: A Mother's Affection
text:
During breakfast, Swamishri offered Pujya Kothari Swami some magas along with a sweet made of fenugreek (methi) and said, "First eat [the sweet made from] methi; then the magas."

It is common knowledge that if you eat magas after eating methi, the sweetness of the magas reduces the methi's bitter aftertaste. Despite this, Swamishri's love is such that he cannot endure even the slightest discomfort to befall his devotees, similar to a mother who cannot resist herself from offering affectionate advice.

title: A Genuine Bond
text:
While Swamishri was meeting the devotees, Hareshbhai Moradiya and his brother, Miteshbhai, came forward. Upon seeing Miteshbhai, Swamishri asked, "Do you live here [in Vidyanagar]?"

Hareshbhai responded, "No Swami! He lives in Surat." Swamishri inquired, "Then who [from your family] lives here?" Everyone began to wonder why Swamishri had asked this question.

Moments later, Swamishri clarified, "Once, you had given me a pair of [prescription] glasses."

Hareshbhai and Miteshbhai thought about it further and recalled, "Yes Swami! Many years ago, in 1992, we used to own a [glasses] shop here. However, [after all these years], though we have forgotten, you still remember!"

Swamishri's genuine bond with his devotees is such that he appreciates, values, and never forgets even the smallest of offerings.

title: Uplifting Through Unity
text:
While delivering ashirwad (discourses) after puja, Swamishri emphasized, "If you maintain samp (unity), then [you will attain] Akshardham."

A few hours later at 11:00 AM, he arrived at the bal shibir. Here, the balaks requested, "Swamishri, please teach us an extraordinary lesson."

Swamishri wrote, "Samp = working together to complete one another's tasks."

For Swamishri, samp is an extraordinary ideal that is dear to his heart. Thus, his life and message infuses and inspires this timeless value within the hearts of all.

title: Never Delaying Darshan
text:
By the time Swamishri departed the assembly hall, it was already 7:40 AM. Due to the late hour, his sevak sant suggested, "Swamishri, given the time, perhaps we could visit Purushottam Swami's shrine on our way to the evening assembly?"

Swamishri responded firmly, "No, [let's go] right now." Exhibiting a slight irritation, he continued, "Why cut (limit) darshan? We do not cut (curtail) other activities, such as eating..."

The sevak folded his hands and humbly replied, "Swami, we are not cutting (limiting) it. We are merely postponing it until the evening."

Swamishri stated, "When we postpone it to the evening, it tends to be delayed further..." With these words, Swamishri proceeded to Purushottam Swami's shrine, where he performed darshan and circumambulations with great reverence.

Swamishri's refusal to limit or compromise on doing darshan underscores his deep-rooted commitment and unwavering devotion to Bhagwan and his gurus.

title: Purposeful Interactions
text:
Today, Swamishri granted 376 mulakats (meetings) in just one hour and three minutes during the morning. Despite the rapid pace at which devotees were moving, Swamishri meticulously attended to each and every individual.

This was evident today when Swamishri's gaze fell upon a youth and he exclaimed, "[He] had become a camel." The youth had, in fact, played the role of a camel in a skit a week prior. Without the makeup on his face and the costume he had worn during that performance, it was nearly impossible to recognize him at that moment.

Swamishri's interactions with his devotees are purposeful, not superficial. He recalls even the smallest and most insignificant details, showing his genuine care and interest in all of his devotees.

title: For the Sake of His Devotees
text:
After performing the third and final murti pratishtha ceremony at BAPS Swaminarayan Akshardham in Robbinsville, NJ, Swamishri returned to his room well after the scheduled time. It was already 1:22 PM before he sat down for lunch.

After finishing his meal, the sadhus remarked, "Today is your birthday; yet you have had to endure the most bhido (hardship)....It is evident that you are determined to please everyone in order to fulfill their wishes, correct?"

Swamishri emphatically responded, "Absolutely! [We] should please them as they have done so much for us!"

Regardless of the occasion, Swamishri is always willing to endure any hardship for the sake of pleasing his devotees.

title: Constant Devotion
text:
Swamishri woke up from his afternoon nap at 4:10 PM. The attendant swami inquired, "Swamishri, were you able to sleep?"

Swamishri replied, "I tossed and turned...My eyes may have been closed, but I was reflecting on various things..." Swamishri then asked the attendant swami, "What were you doing?"

The attendant swami replied, "I am scheduled to speak about your ahnik (various daily acts of devotion) during today's shibir. I was preparing for the katha."

Swamishri laughed and replied, "[I am] constantly engaged in ähnik.... During puja, whether my eyes are open or closed, the same experience continuously persists. During puja, I perform dandavats [in my mind] during mānsi as I am unable to do so physically."

For Swamishri, there is no difference between performing daily tasks and engaging in acts of devotion. He simply engages in devotion at all times and performs all activities while offering devotion.

title: A Humble Leader
text:
After completing his daily walk, Swamishri arrived near his residence. Miteshbhai and his son, Ghanshyam, greeted him at that moment.

Ghanshyam inquired of Swamishri, "How does it feel like to be a guru?"

Swamishri chuckled and replied, "[We should] engage in bhakti with dasbhav (humility). I enjoy humility!"

Swamishri's views his role as a guru not as a position of authority, but as an opportunity to serve and inspire others. His emphasis on humility and devotion highlights his selfless and uplifting nature.

title: Smruti is Rest
text:
Because Swamishri had been awake since 3:30 AM this morning, the attendant swamis had arranged for Swamishri to take some rest between Mangalā arti and Shangār arti. However, after only ten minutes, Swamishri sat up.

The swamis inquired, "Swamishri, do you not wish to rest?"

Swamishri decidedly yet gently replied, "Why rest! To do smruti (to reminisce and reflect) of Maharaj and Swami is rest."

Swamishri's uncompromising desire to engage in devotion supersedes any physical necessity or comfort.

title: Unhesitantly Humble
text:
Swamishri, as usual, began his breakfast with a handful of mamra (puffed rice), which he playfully calls 'mamracharan'.

Narayancharan Swami reminisced, "Swami, on the day of Dashera, Swamibapa (Pramukh Swami Maharaj) would always start his breakfast with jalebi..."

Upon hearing this, Swamishri set aside the mamra in his hand without any hesitation and took a small piece of jalebi, honoring his guru's tradition.

Swamishri's humility shines as he readily sets aside everything in order to follow his guru even through the smallest of actions.

title: Junagadh, Gujarat, India
text: Today, during breakfast, Swamishri continued this humble tradition. Shiro was placed in front of him, but Swamishri asked for jalebi to be brought before him. Swamishri ate a small piece of jalebi and then had the shiro.

title: His Signature Move
text:
Before Swamishri retires for rest, his hearing aids are removed. His humility and flexibility are evident during this daily process. Whenever the attendants approach Swamishri, he invariably adjusts his head in a way that makes it convenient for them to remove his hearing aids.

On this day, in the afternoon, with a revealing grin, Swamishri said, "I enjoy bowing [my head]..."

Santcharit Swami, who was removing the hearing aids, immediately replied, "Swami! We are the ones that should bow our heads..."

Swamishri responded, "Whether you bow or not, we must bow."

For Swamishri, the simple act of bowing his head is more than just a habit. It is his signature move.

title: Keep Divyabhav
text:
After lunch, Swamishri penned a short message to the students residing at the BAPS hostels (chhatralays) in Australia and New Zealand. A special shibir was arranged specifically for the students. In the letter, while revealing his inner wishes, Swamishri wrote in English, "Keep Divyabhav in everyone and happiness is yours."

Swamishri has shared with us a consistent message to reflect upon the divinity within others. In doing so, he has revealed not only his inner wish but also guided us towards the path of everlasting happiness.

title: An Eternal Servant
text:
After gaining insight on how Bhagwan Swaminarayan's murti in Akshardham (Robbinsville, NJ) should be designed, Swamishri was asked how Gunantitand Swami Maharaj's murti should be positioned. He was shown two options of Gunatitanand Swami Maharaj's murti; a replica of Gunatitanand Swami Maharaj's murti from Gandhinagar Akshardham and another from Delhi Akshardham. Swamishri selected the position that Gunatitanand Swami Maharaj is seated in from Delhi Akshardham.

However, Swamishri added, "The murti of Gunatitanand Swami should be such that his entire form radiates humility."

The concept of humility is well defined in Satsang, but the thought of imbibing it into every pore of a murti would only occur to and be expressed by someone who himself is an eternal servant of Bhagwan.

title: Emphasizing Samp
text:
Following his morning blessings, Swamishri was presented with a collection of Samp Books crafted by the India Trip delegates. These books were filled with good qualities the delegates had observed in each other during their journey.

Delighted by this initiative, Swamishri praised the delegates for showcasing their unity and understanding without knowing each other's backgrounds by saying, "This is the best thing." He also declared that this was a significant step towards building our inner Akshardham.

However, because this conversation happend in the cabin and no one else was able to hear it, Brahmavatsal Swami, at Swamishri's request, narrated this entire incident to the assembly. Swamishri's joyful expression and gesture underscored his deep appreciation for the Samp Books.

As always, Swamishri emphasized the importance of unity (samp) and expressed his utmost happiness at witnessing our efforts to foster harmony within our community.

title: Never Wasteful
text:
Vinaypriya Swami mentioned, "Swamishri invariably makes it a point to have all lights turned off whenever there is sufficient natural daylight emanating through the windows." Based on this comment, a discussion on Swamishri's frugality ensued among Swamishri's attendants.

During the discussion, Digantbhai Sadhak shared, "In 2019, Swamishri was in Sarangpur. As he was returning from the bathroom, he turned around and noticed the light was still on. He looked back two to three times, but no one understood why he was looking back. Finally, Swamishri said in a slightly raised voice, 'Light!"

Whether it is electricity, water, or any other natural resource, Swamishri does his part in conserving our planet's resources. The examples from his life teach us to become efficient with our time, finances, and use of resources.

title: Guru Seeks Forgiveness
text:
In an effort to ensure everyone was able to individually meet Swamishri, the devotees were being rushed as they came for darshan. Consequently, a devotee named Pankajbhai Gadhia had to quickly meet Swamishri amidst the rush. Swamishri did not like this and requested an attendant to give Pankajbhai a call. Swamishri said, "When you came in line to meet me, you had to leave in a hurry. Please forgive me [for this mistake]."

Moved by Swamishri's gesture, Pankajbhai returned to meet Swamishri and said, "Swami! You should not ask for forgiveness. After all, I was able to have your darshan." Saying this, he took Swamishri's blessings before departing.

What an extraordinary guru! Despite doing nothing wrong, Swamishri never hesitates to apologize even to a devotee.

title: A Divine Perspective
text:
Santo and devotees did darshan of Swamishri as he performed his daily walking. As he completed his walk, the swamis curiously asked, "What thoughts occupy your mind as you walk?"

Swamishri replied, "[I think] 'This devotee is divine (divya)... this devotee is divine... this devotee is divine...' They are all divine. And my other thought is of Maharaj-Swami."

Swamishri constantly perceives divinity in all, highlighting his unwavering emphasis on always maintaining this thought.

title: A Steady Diet
text:
After breakfast, Swamishri said to his attendant Swami, "My food!" The attendant Swami did not understand Swamishri's comment. Thus, Swamishri repeated, "My food!"

Still confused, the attendant Swami inquired, "What [do you mean by this comment], Swami?"

Each day after breakfast, the virtues of various Swamis are routinely recounted in Swamishri's presence. With this context in mind and with a slightly reprimanding tone, Swamishri clarified, "Gun grahan (to perceive the virtues of others)."

Swamishri deeply values and genuinely looks forward to consuming a steady diet of positivity by reflecting on the virtues of others.

title: Never Fatigued
text:
Today, Swamishri met a total of 1,044 devotees during the mulākāt (meeting devotees) session. Prior to his meal, when Swamishri yawned, the swamis said, "It seems you are tired from the mulākāt session."

Swamishri replied, "How is [meeting the devotees] tiring? I feel tired when I have to eat."

Whether it is a prolonged mulākāt session, an overflowing samip darshan session, or any other interaction with devotees, Swamishri is never fatigued.

The enthusiasm with which he meets devotees is a reflection of his unconditional love for them.

title: No 'Grand Sleep'
text:
Today, Swamishri departed Gandhinagar and flew to Dar es Salaam. After doing darshan and having his meal at the mandir in Dar es Salaam, Swamishri traveled to the shibir venue, White Sands Resort. Given how far and long Swamishri had traveled today, the swamis asked, "Please take some rest now. You have traveled for 7 to 8 hours. Thus, please enjoy some 'grand sleep.'"

Swamishri laughed and said, "There is no 'grand sleep.' [In fact,] I did not sleep this afternoon."

The swamis were awestruck. Yogimanan Swami asked, "If you did not sleep, then what were you thinking about?"

Swamishri immediately responded, "Swaminarayan Swaminarayan... [I thought of] Maharaj-Swami and prayed for some devotees so that they are able to resolve their problems."

For Swamishri, remembering Maharaj and Swami and praying for devotees is far more important than enjoying 'grand sleep.'

title: Swamishri's Slogan
text:
After doing darshan in the mandir, Swamishri came down the stairs. A swami, who was standing by the neem tree, was waiting for Swamishri so that he could ask an important question. When Swamishri approached, the swami asked, "Swami! Yogi Bapa's slogans were 'Bhagwan Saunu Bhalu Karo (May Bhagwan bless all)' and 'Bhagwan Bhaji Leva (We should worship Bhagwan).' Pramukh Swami Maharaj's slogan was 'Bijānā bhalāmā apdu bhalu (In the joy of others, lies our own).' What is your slogan?"

Swamishri replied, "Divyabhav!"

The example that Swamishri sets and the message he spreads are one and the same understanding Bhagwan and his gurus to be divine and seeing, focusing on, and reflecting on the divinity of all that are associated with them.

title: An Unbeknown Sacrifice
text:
After the evening assembly, Swamishri arrived at his residence and sat down for his meal at 8:10 PM. He informed his attendant swami, Gunvatsal Swami, "Since I have had Ensure, I am not hungry. I am eating for the sole purpose of pleasing the devotees. Thus, please bring something that requires excessive chewing."

In this manner, Swamishri ate paneer shak and prolonged his dinner by 30 minutes.

It is evident that Swamishri selflessly sacrifices bodily comforts for the sake of pleasing his devotees. However, he often does so deliberately in a manner that is unbeknownst to them.

title: Appreciating the Volunteers
text:
After the Pushpadolotsav sabha, while Swamishri was returning to his residence, he saw the security volunteers and asked the nearby swamis, "Did they attend [and get to participate in] the Fuldol sabha?"

"No," replied the swamis.

In the elevator, Swamishri sanctified some flowers and flower petals and said, "Place these [flower petals] on the heads of the security volunteers."

Abhayswarup Swami replied, "Yes, Swami! I will personally go [shower them with the sanctified flower petals]."

Swamishri naturally inspires volunteerism because he acknowledges, appreciates, and values the sacrifices that the volunteers make.

title: The One-Word Key
text:
After doing darshan, Swamishri proceeded to the front of the mandir on the pradakshinā path and stopped directly across the central shrine where the swamis were awaiting his arrival. Yogichintan Swami asked, "Swami, because today is a rest day, physically, you will get some rest. However, what can we do so that you always feel at rest?"

Swamishri answered in one word, "Agna."

Following agna is more than an endeavor that leads to one's progress in Satsang. It is a reflection of one's love and devotion for Swamishri. It leads to Swamishri's rajipo and allows him to always feel at rest.

title: It Makes No Difference
text:
After Swamishri's lunch, Dr. Vrajlalbhai suggested, "Swami, it is advisable for you to rest for six continuous hours as opposed to taking short naps."

With a slight grin, Swamishri replied, "Whether I am able to sleep or not, I remain ever joyful [and content]."

Hearing this, the attendant swamis asked, "What type of joy? [The bliss of] Bhagwan?"

Swamishri nodded in agreement. Swamishri further added, "The joy of Aksharam Aham Purushottamadāso'smi' (I am Akshar, a servant of Purushottam)." Swamishri then continued, "Whether I am asleep or awake, it makes no difference."

In all three states, whether he is awake, asleep, or in deep sleep, Swamishri eternally experiences the bliss of Bhagwan. He is above the three states because he is Akshar, a servant of Bhagwan.

title: Believing is Seeing
text:
After doing darshan, while on his way to the sabha hall, Swamishri was passing by the Nilkanth Varni abhishek mandap. Yogvivek Swami asked the pujari that serves Nilkanth Varni, "Has Bhagwan eaten thal?"

Swamishri intervened and said, "Though it is not visible, [Nilkanth Varni] always eats."

In a world where 'seeing is believing' is the norm, Swamishri does not need to see that Bhagwan accepts our devotion to believe. For him, believing is seeing.

title: Prioritizing Purity
text:
After evening sabha, Swamishri was returning to his residence. Outside Swamishri's room, an otto (circular platform) with a murti of Nilkanth Varni on it has been installed under the banyan tree.

Harikrishna Maharaj was placed on the platform while the swamis were offering thal. As Swamishri arrived, fresh hot puris were brought to Swamishri so that he could offer them to Thakorji.

However, Swamishri did not take the puris. When the attendant swami asked Swamishri why he declined, Swamishri revealed that he had not washed his hands. As a result, despite wanting to offer the puris, he did not offer them.

Swamishri prioritizes purity in all acts of devotion.

title: Diwali Blessings
text:
Swami-Shriji
Param Pujya Pramukh Swami

To: Swami Bapa's beloved youths,

Heartiest Jay Shri Swaminarayan from Sadhu Keshavjivandas

HAPPY DIWALI AND HAPPY NEW YEAR

May you all progress in Satsang, your studies, and worldly lives; and may you all experience prosperity physically, mentally, and financially.

Everyone should remain firm in their niyam dharma and develop self-restraint. Do Satsang regularly. Follow the rules of stri-purush maryādā. Use SCREENs (devices) with discretion.

By doing all of this, Bhagwan and the Sant will be extremely pleased, and you will experience inner peace. Your youth will be uplifted and dignified.

Everyone has [my] blessings for the New Year. Stay strong!

title: A Heap of Wealth
text:
After doing darshan of Thakorji in the mandir, Swamishri was exiting the mandir near Ghanshyam Maharaj's shrine. Here, a swami spoke in Marathi, "On this [auspicious] day of Dhanteras, please give us wealth in the form of sādhutā (saintliness)." A swami standing next to him translated this phrase in Gujarati.

Swamishri responded, "Divyabhav. That is wealth. It is a heap of wealth."

Swamishri reminds us that seeing divinity in Maharaj, Swami, and their devotees is a form of spiritual wealth. It truly is a priceless endeavor that enriches our soul.

title: New Year's Message
text:
In the evening, Swamishri individually blessed all of the swamis. Thereafter, during a discussion, the swamis asked, "Swami! On account of the New Year, would you like to say anything? Any specific message?"

Swamishri said, "Divyabhav! Remain immersed in it. After all, it is a deep desire of Shriji Maharaj's and Maharaj has repeatedly said, 'Divyabhav, divyabhav, divyabhav! And it is actually an agna; it is not merely a suggestion or anything else."

The swamis inquired further, "Divyabhav in all swamis and devotees? Or the Satpurush [only]?"

Swamishri clarified, "[In] everyone...By keeping divyabhav in the Satpurush, [the habit of maintaining divyabhav] spreads to everyone else."

title: Everyone is a Mukta
text:
After Swamishri completed his mudrā (yogic hand gestures), during a discussion, an attendant swami said, "Swami! You see everyone as a mukta..."

Swamishri firmly emphasized, "They are! They are! This is not [a figment of one's] imagination or a [false] arrangement. They are! This is a fact. All of you are undoubtedly mukto from Akshardham by association; because you are affiliated with Maharaj! Or else the association would be rendered false. If you remain neglectful after attaining Maharaj, then what can be said? By associating with Maharaj, one's neglectfulness is removed.

Everyone should develop this divine vision: everyone is a mukta."

title: A Selfless Act
text:
After having dinner, Swamishri returned to his bedroom. His attendant swami asked, "Swami, would you like to use the bathroom?"

Swamishri replied, "Shatpadi (to walk 100 steps)."

The attendant swami asked, "Do you want to walk here or outside [the bedroom]?"

Swamishri answered, "It is already late; it would become more late." It was approaching 9:15 PM and the swamis still had not eaten. If Swamishri were to return to the larger room outside his bedroom, the swamis would remain there for Swamishri's darshan, which would delay their dinner even more.

Despite the inconvenience of walking in a smaller, enclosed area, Swamishri completed his 100 steps in the bedroom, thereby enabling the swamis to proceed to dinner. Swamishri selflessly thinks of the needs of others first.

title: Inclination for Mukhpath
text:
After puja, while blessing the balaks who had participated in the Bal Adhiveshan, Swamishri said, "Everyone has memorized the Sahajanand Namavali! Now, all of you should recite it once a week without fail. In doing so, you will always remember it; and this rājipo is immense."

Swamishri not only inspires youths of all ages to develop an inclination for mukhpath, he inspires all to continually recite it so that they may benefit from it and ultimately attain the greatest reward: the rajipo of Maharaj and our gurus.

title: A Humble Guru
text:
Swamishri left his residence to attend the evening sabha. Due to ongoing construction, the path was uneven. With the support of attendant swamis, Swamishri arrived on stage and immediately approached the empty seat beside Atmaswarup Swami. Several swamis corrected him by saying, "Swami, your seat is up ahead on the sihāsan (the main seat reserved for the guru). These [seats] are for the senior swamis."

Swamishri had become the guru approximately four months prior to this incident. Even at that time, when Swamishri was to take his seat on the central sihāsan for the first time as the guru, he approached the empty sofa where the sadguru swamis were seated before the attendant swamis directed him to his sihāsan.

Swamishri eternally considers himself to be a servant of servants, not a guru of many.

title: To The Fullest Extent
text:
Swamishri finished eating lunch at 1:01 PM. He picked up the loto (gourd) that contained water as he prepared to rinse his hands. Because the loto was decorated with beautiful artwork, Swamishri questioned, "This is not made of silver, right?"

The swamis replied, "No."

Only then did Swamishri proceed to wash his hands with the loto.

Swamishri does not use gold, silver, or any other form of wealth as it violates Bhagwan Swaminarayan's agna (command) for renunciants. He carefully adheres to each and every agna to the fullest extent.

title: Ever Resourceful
text:
Swamishri routinely takes honey-based medicinal syrup before retiring for the night. Today, after taking the medicine, he inquired, "Where is [the attendant that prepares the syrup]? A significant amount [of medicine] is being wasted."

Realizing what Swamishri was implying, the attendant swami present replied, "Yes, Swami, some medicine remains in the bowl on all sides. From now on, we will prepare the medicine in a spoon." Pleased with this solution, Swamishri agreed in approval.

Previously, the syrup was being prepared by mixing honey with the medicine in a bowl. As a result, it was near-impossible to scrape all of it with a spoon. Swamishri, ever mindful not to waste, demonstrated a valuable lesson in resourcefulness. His actions teach us to utilize our resources wisely and avoid unnecessary wastage.

title: 1,000 Shloks
text:
Tapomangal Swami, a swami currently residing in Gandhinagar, composed 1,000 shloks extolling Swamishri's glory. On account of Swamishri's birthday, the shloks were presented to Swamishri this morning. Swamishri himself was both surprised and skeptical. He said, "That many incidents related to me have not even occurred. How then could he have written 1,000 shloks! What could he have possibly written in the 1,000 shloks? [He] could only write if there is something worthwhile to write about."

Swamishri truly believes himself to be insignificant and unworthy of such praise. His humility is deep-rooted, genuine, and absolute.

title: Engaged in Reading
text:
Today, Swamishri was scheduled to meet Sheikh Nahyan Bin Mubarak Al Nahyan at his royal Majlis and later visit the Sheikh Zayed Grand Mosque. After his afternoon rest, Swamishri was ready to leave for this historic event but had a few minutes to spare. Thus, he picked up Purushottam Bolya Prite and began to read and reflect on the divine messages of Bhagwan Swaminarayan! This spectacle was reminiscent of Pramukh Swami Maharaj reading Yogiji Maharaj's Tales of Wisdom before he arrived to deliver a historic speech at the Millennium World Peace Summit at The United Nations.

In Satsang Diksha shlok 123, Swamishri states, "One should not let time pass wastefully without satsang or devotion." Our gurus exemplify the practice of continuously engaging in satsang, even when they only have a few minutes to spare before a momentous occasion.

title: A Warm Welcome
text:
Swamishri arrived in Ahmedabad from Morbi this evening. After doing darshan and abhishek, as Swamishri walked ahead, he approached a few balaks. The children asked, "Swami, [on behalf of all] balaks, we welcomed you [to Ahmedabad]. Now, what can we do so that you feel like welcoming us?"

Instantly, Swamishri replied, "Dharma-niyam."

Following the rules of dharma may appear prohibitive. However, dharma-niyam protects us from the influences of maya, keeps us connected to Bhagwan, and provides a path through which we can receive a warm welcome to Swamishri's heart.

title: No Regard for Physical Comforts
text:
In the morning, Swamishri completed the momentous murti pratishtha ceremony of Tapomurti Shri Nilkanth Varni on the Akshardham grounds. After the ceremony, Vishwavihari Swami, the Kothari of Gandhinagar Akshardham, apologized to Swamishri, "Swami, at the age of 91, we have given you undue hardship. Your rest time has been delayed and you were out in the heat for a long time. Therefore, please forgive us."

Swamishri immediately replied, "You did not give us any hardship. In fact, I enjoyed [the ceremony].

Swamishri is never concerned for his physical comforts. He truly enjoys what most would otherwise consider hardship.

title: A Humble Servant
text:
After the evening assembly, Swamishri was returning to his residence. While in the golf cart, an attendant swami gestured towards both the murti of Harikrishna Maharaj and Swamishri and asked, "What is the difference between this Thakorji (Harikrishna Maharaj) and this Thakorji (Swamishri)?"

Swamishri promptly replied, "There is a vast difference...He (Harikrishna Maharaj) is Purna Purushottam Narayan."

"And this [Thakorji]?" the attendant swami asked, gesturing towards Swamishri.

Swamishri humbly revealed, "I am a sevak (servant)."

Despite being praised and revered by many, Swamishri continually remains true to his identity: an eternal servant of Purna Purushottam Narayan Shri Bhagwan Swaminarayan.

title: Engrossed in Mala
text:
After puja, when Swamishri was preparing to take his medication, the attendant swamis noticed his hands were unusually cold. This had occurred because two air conditioning vents were blowing cold air directly onto his hands. Naturally, they questioned why Swamishri did not bring this to their attention. Swamishri explained, "I thought, 'I'll mention it, I'll mention it...' but my mind became absorbed in [doing] mala."

Swamishri becomes so engrossed in devotion that he remains oblivious to physical discomforts.

title: A Dislike For Wastage
text:
As he prepared to leave his room to go to the mandir for darshan, Swamishri took his seat in the wheelchair. Suddenly, Swamishri needed to wipe his nose. Uttamyogi Swami quickly brought two facial tissues. After Swamishri used one to wipe his nose, Uttamyogi Swami hastily scrunched up both the used tissue with the clean one and discarded them at once. Swamishri saw this and immediately reprimanded him, "Why did you discard the other one!"

Swamishri considers the wastage of even a trivial item, like a facial tissue, to be unacceptable.

title: A Night of Mukhpath
text:
Swamishri awoke at 1:35 AM in the morning to use the bathroom. At 1:40 AM, he sat down on the sofa and began to memorize the arti. Swamishri was dreaming of performing arti in the mandir but he had forgotten a few lines. As a result, he decided to wake up and revise as well as memorize the whole arti.

After several minutes had passed, Uttamyogi Swami realized Swamishri was awake. He requested Swamishri to go to sleep, but Swamishri continued to do mukhpath. He reviewed the first and last line of the arti. As he was reviewing the third line, Uttamyogi Swami again requested Swamishri to get some rest. Yet, Swamishri still continued. He even discussed the meaning of the third line. By the time Swamishri finished memorizing the arti, it was 2:40 AM!

Despite being 85 years old, Swamishri was so eager to memorize and learn the new arti by heart in the middle of the night.

title: A Deeper Perspective
text:
After blessing the morning assembly of swamis, Swamishri observed an artifact of a heart-shaped gesture. When Swamishri stood up, Pujya Ghanshyamcharan Swami formed the shape of a heart with his hands and in one motion, rotated his thumbs upward to create a thumbs up with both hands. Seeing this, Swamishri approached him, formed a double thumbs up gesture with his own hands, and playfully touched Pujya Ghanshyamcharan Swami's thumbs with his thumbs. An attendant swami remarked, "Ghanshyam Bapa has a humorous and playful personality. Upon seeing him, one instinctively feels like enjoying a light moment."

Swamishri agreed but added, "He is nirdoshmurti (embodiment of innocence; faultless)."

Swamishri values more than the superficial virtues of swamis and devotees. He perceives everyone with a deeper perspective. He appreciates their spiritual greatness by considering them to be divine and faultless.

title: Sākshāt!
text:
Today, Swamishri traveled from Gondal to Gandhinagar. After doing darshan of the murtis in the mandir and granting darshan to the devotees present, Swamishri proceeded to his residence. Here, Swamishri called Vishwavihari Swami and Dharmavatsal Swami forward and greeted them with three high-five gestures each. Swamishri often acknowledges them in this unique way by placing his palms on their hands three times. While greeting Vishwavihari Swami in this manner, Swamishri said, "Sakshat (in person)!" Everyone was surprised. Two months prior, when Swamishri was in Delhi, he would remember Vishwavihari Swami on a daily basis by giving three additional high-fives to Dharmavatsal Swami. Today, Swamishri was pleased to recontinue the tradition in person.

Swamishri's bond with all of his devotees is genuine, unique, and eternal. Even in their absence, he finds a way to maintain this divine connection.

title: Limitless
text:
The swamis from Europe asked Swamishri to name the sant ashram (residence for swamis) located at the new mandir that is being built in Paris, France. Swamishri named it "Akshar."

The swamis asked for clarification, "Should it be named just 'Akshar' or should it be named 'Akshar Bhuvan?"

Swamishri replied, "Just 'Akshar." Then, Swamishri continued, "Akshar is 'limitless.' If it is named Akshar Bhuvan, then Akshar is limited to the building only. Therefore, it should be named Akshar."

Through this subtle consideration, Swamishri revealed the true nature of Akshar. Truly, only one who is Akshar can understand the vastness of Akshar.

title: Eat With A Purpose
text:
After sanctifying prasād for the devotees, Swamishri entered his room. He sang the shlok, 'Shrimat sadgun shalinam,' with love and devotion and began his breakfast thereafter. The devotees present were doing darshan of Swamishri while enjoying the prasad that he had sanctified for them. Seeing this, Swamishri lovingly advised, "When one eats, one should eat with the intent to please Bhagwan; in doing so, it becomes a form (an act) of devotion. [However], If one eats to satisfy the mind, then [Bhagwan] is not pleased."

Swamishri's message is simple yet profound: any action, when performed with the aim of pleasing Bhagwan, can be transformed into an act of devotion.

title: A Lasting Memory
text:
During the Divya Sannidhi Parva (Karyakar Shibir) evening session, Swamishri was requested, "Please narrate a personal seva experience that you vividly remember, one that will encourage us to [improve how we] do seva."

Swamishri recalled, "One time, Yogi Bapa was in Gondal. Bhailubhai from Advad had brought a new truck for pujan. Yogi Bapa had the seva of loading trash into the truck begin. At that time, he remembered me, 'Where is Mahnat (Mahant) Swami?' Someone replied, 'He has a fever.' I had a 103° fever. Yogi Bapa said, 'Call him, [he] will feel better.' I went and performed that seva for two hours. My fever did not subside, but that seva [experience] became a lasting memory."

Throughout his life, Swamishri's unwavering commitment to seva has remained steadfast, even in the face of illness.

title: Dependent on Bhagwan
text:
During Swamishri's lunch, a unique fruit, two tomatoes connected as one, was brought to him. Seeing this, Vinaypriya Swami remarked, "Some people say that a defective fruit such as this should not be eaten."

Uttamyogi Swami asked, "Can we eat a tomato like this?"

Swamishri replied, "Yes" Then, he quickly added, "We should eat it only after offering it to Bhagwan."

Swamishri is not reliant on any worldly precedents. He is dependent on Bhagwan only.

title: Solved a Riddle
text:
During Swamishri's evening exercise, the following riddle was posed to him: Four birds were sitting on a tree. A hunter shot one. How many birds were left?

Swamishri responded, "Not a single one."

The attendant swamis asked, "Why none?"

Swamishri replied, "All of the [birds] would fly away due to the blast."

The attendant swamis asked, "Have you heard this riddle before?"

Swamishri stated that he had not heard it before. Through these types of interactions, we can discern how clever and contemplative Swamishri truly is.

title: Pleasing A Child
text:
After performing the pratishtha ceremony of Tapomurti Shri Nilkanth Varni, Swamishri was returning to his residence in the panoramic-window vehicle. Within the vehicle, the swamis were admiring and celebrating the historic event that had just unfolded. Meanwhile, a child was running after the vehicle to catch a glimpse of Swamishri. Though no one else noticed, Swamishri saw the child and asked that the vehicle be stopped. He called the child near and gave him darshan, before allowing the vehicle to continue.

While others were praising Swamishri and marveling at his achievement, Swamishri was intent on pleasing a child.

title: The Benefits of Bharat Yatra
text:
During the summer of 2024, kishores and kishoris from North America and Europe visited India for a special trip known as the Bharat Yatra. The final week of the five-week yatra culminated with a variety of labh opportunities in Swamishri's presence in Bochasan. On July 25, a special sabha with Swamishri was arranged for the Bharat Yatra delegates. During the sabha, Swamishri blessed them with immense labh and gave them a lifetime worth of unforgettable memories.

The next day, Swamishri expressed a wish to personally write a letter to the delegates in English. Swamishri wrote an invigorating letter highlighting the numerous benefits of attending the Bharat Yatra. Notably, he concluded the letter with a direct and essential message, one that has shaped his own life philosophy: "Live for BAPS and make Satpurush your life."

title: Affinity For Children
text:
During Swamishri's dinner, Nirmalcharit Swami introduced all the karyakars present. Afterward, he inquired, "Swami, why do you have an [instinctive] affinity for children?"

Swamishri replied, "They are the form of Yogi Bapa...I view them as Yogi Bapa."

Though Swamishri is able to connect with people of all ages from all walks of life, his profound affection for children is particularly unique. He cherishes their innocence and values their potential because he perceives the divinity of Yogi Bapa within them.

title: Conquering The Mind
text:
During the evening sabha, students from the BAPS Swaminarayan Vidyamandir in Junagadh asked a series of questions to Swamishri. The first student asked, "We aspire to do well academically, but we find it difficult to focus our minds...How can we improve our focus?"

Swamishri replied, "Even if one goes to the jungle and endeavors [endlessly], the mind cannot be conquered. Conquering the mind is very rare. It is not meant for an ordinary person. However, by offering devotion to Bhagwan and by engaging in Bhagwan-related activities, the mind can be conquered."

title: Twice As Good As Mine
text:
Swamishri entered his residence after dinner. Pujya Dr. Swami also arrived here. During their conversation, the topic of Dr. Swami's health came up. Adarshyogi Swami, Dr. Swami's attendant swami, asked Swamishri, "How does Doctor Swami's health appear to you?"

"[His health seems] well," replied Swamishri. Continuing, Swamishri emphasized, "I pray everyday: may his health remain twice as good as mine!"

Swamishri's unselfish prayer is a reflection of his sincere appreciation for Dr. Swami and the spirit with which he serves BAPS and his gurus.

title: Appreciation For Karyakars
text: During the Karyakar Suvarna Mahotsav inauguration sabha, Swamishri said, "Pramukh Swami Maharaj would describe all of you karyakars as 'swamis in white (householder) clothes' because your commitment is such and your sacrifices are such. You have endured many hardships and have done so much; no less than I. The women's wing has not done less. Everyone has persistently engaged in seva. All of you have sacrificed your careers and are doing seva with dedication. You have to advance your careers and care for your wives and children. Dedicated [volunteers] are invaluable. There is no compensation... Thus, the work you are doing is similar to that of the swamis. We will celebrate this Karyakar Suvarna Mahotsav to applaud your dedication [and] to appreciate your spirit of sacrifice. This mahotsav will strengthen our faith, deepen our pride for the sanstha, Satpurush, and siddhant, and will foster samp, suhradbhāv, and ekta."

title: From Sorrow to Joy
text:
Today, while the balaks were reciting mukhpath during Swamishri's puja, a 7-year old balak, Aarav, had forgotten his mukhpath in the moment and began to cry. After puja, Swamishri stepped away for a few minutes to take his morning medication. As he was returning to the stage, Aarav and a few swamis were awaiting Swamishri. When the swamis informed Swamishri what had happened, Swamishri bent over to Aarav's level and lovingly listened to his recitation. Pleased with Aarav's devotion, Swamishri blessed him by placing his hand on his head. Suddenly, Swamishri gently pulled Aarav closer and gave him a warm embrace! In a matter of seconds, he removed his sorrow and gave him a memory that he will cherish for the rest of his life.

Swamishri's compassionate nature is such that he is capable of turning our misery into joy in an instant.

title: A Great Gift
text:
A balak asked Swamishri, "Swami Bapa, it is customary for us to give each other gifts on our birthdays. Yesterday was Pramukh Swami Maharaj's birthday. Thus, what should we gift him on his birthday?"

Swamishri lovingly replied, "First, you may offer whatever physical items you may have, but infuse your faith and devotion [in the offering]. Do not engage in gossip or other such negative talks, but whatever [you have decided] to give to Swami Bapa, whether you have written something or prepared a card, do so in a thoughtful manner so that Bapa remains before [and with] you. Secondly, whatever Maharaj likes, by keeping Satsang and heedfully engaging in your studies, that is considered a great gift.

In this manner, Swamishri guided the children on what they can gift Pramukh Swami Maharaj on his birthday.

title: The Epitome of Humility
text:
After his morning puja, Swamishri partook in a virtual question and answer session with swamis from Toronto. During the session, the swamis asked, "If Shriji Maharaj were to physically appear and grant [you] one boon, what would you ask for?"

Swamishri immediately replied, "I would ask [for blessings so that I may] become dāsānudās (a servant of a servants)."

In a world where it is commonplace to seek superiority, Swamishri embodies the epitome of humility.

title: "This Is The 'Mission'"
text:
In the evening, during Swamishri's breathing exercises, the attendant swamis, Swamishri's doctors, and Swamishri were discussing a recent study that described how detrimental the air quality in Delhi is. The study revealed that breathing Delhi's air for 24 hours is akin to smoking 23 cigarettes. Dr. Mamtora, one of Swamishri's physicians, remarked, "The external pollution will remain. However, please bless us so that we are able to remove our internal pollution."

Swamishri emphatically responded, "This is the 'mission.'"

Then, Swamishri was asked, "Which is more harmful? Internal pollution or external pollution?"

Swamishri replied, "Both are harmful. But internal [pollution] is more fatal. External [pollution] can be eliminated through [a variety of measures], but internal [pollution] is 'permanent.'"

In this way, Swamishri reminds us of the importance of our primary 'mission': to purify our hearts.

title: Powerful Memory
text:
Before retiring to sleep, Swamishri recalled an old memory from his childhood. When he was around 4 years old and residing in Jabalpur, Madhya Pradesh, a brahmin would recite a prayer, "He Prabhu mangaldātā, gnān hamko dijiye," which means, "Oh Bhagwan, bestower of bliss, enlighten us with knowledge."

Swamishri's memory is remarkable. He effortlessly recalled a poem he had heard 87 years earlier!

title: "A Great Precedent"
text:
After cheshtā, the swamis informed Swamishri about a new Australian law that aims to ban children under the age of 16 from using social media. Hearing this, Swamishri was extremely pleased and expressed his support, "[Australia] has set a [great] precedent."

Uttamyogi Swami remarked, "Now, children will be able to preserve their time and re-allocate it for more useful purposes."

Swamishri corrected him, "Not time, but character," implying that children will be able to better preserve their values if they are protected from the negative influences of social media.

By offering his support for this law, Swamishri warns us of the harmful nature of social media. He appreciates and supports any initiative that promotes healthy character development in children.

title: A Letter Of Appreciation
text:
Just hours before the Karyakar Suvarna Mahotsav grand celebration, at 10:52 AM, Swamishri wrote a letter to Pujya Yagnapriya Swami, in which he expressed his deep love and appreciation for the karyakars:

To Swami Bapa's beloved Pujya Yagnapriya Swami,

Today, my joy knows no bounds. I can see Yogi Bapa and Pramukh Swami in all the karyakars. Since today morning, I have been thinking of the greatness of the karyakars and doing their pujan. I am doing chāndlo to them. I perform chandan archā on them. I place rice grains on their foreheads and adorn them with garlands of jasmine and roses. I am prostrating to them all.

May you all remain pleased with me.

Heartfelt Jai Swaminarayan from Sadhu Keshavjivandas.

All of you swamis and karyakars are my hands and feet.

Although Swamishri serves tirelessly day and night, he continuously celebrates the service of others with all his might.

title: Benefits of Mukhpath
text:
During the evening assembly, a balak asked, "Swami Bapa, what benefits do we experience from doing mukhpath?"

Swamishri replied, "Oh! You will benefit immensely! First, the [mukhpath excerpts] are Bhagwan's divine speech; they are Gunatitanand Swami's divine speech. Only after accumulating many merits [from previous births] do these these books (scriptures) come in our hands…[Gunatitanand] Swami himself has said, 'Even after giving tens of millions of rupees, these spiritual talks are not attainable.' However, we have easily obtained them for 60 rupees. This is not the way [to consider these talks]. Who is speaking? Bhagwan is speaking. How great is Bhagwan! He is sarvopari (supreme) Bhagwan. By understanding the value [of mukhpath, the messages from] the passages that we recite are instilled in our souls."

Mukhpath is very dear to Swamishri's heart. It represents an unparalleled opportunity to earn his innermost blessings.

title: An Eternal Servant
text:
A set of murtis to be installed in a new hari mandir were placed in Swamishri's room. The set included murtis of Akshar-Purushottam Maharaj and Ghanshyam Maharaj. After performing the pujan of the murtis, Swamishri admiringly observed the beautiful murti of Ghanshyam Maharaj.

Seizing the opportunity, Gurumanan Swami asked, "What is the difference between this murti (Ghanshyam Maharaj) and this murti (gesturing towards Swamishri)?"

Swamishri humbly replied, "He is Bhagwan, Purna Purushottam Narayan! And I am [merely] a servant. 'Aksharam Aham Purushottamadāso'smi.'"

Swamishri eternally considers himself an eternal servant of Bhagwan Swaminarayan.

title: "Grasp The Depth."
text:
After blessing the assembly of swamis in the afternoon, Aksharjivan Swami, who spearheads a virtual goshthi (Satsang discussion) channel, approached Swamishri and said, "Our goshthi mandal is progressing well. It feels as if you are present in our goshthi [discussions]. This has been our experience. If you wish to say anything, please share your thoughts."

Swamishri replied, "Grasp the depth [of Satsang]. There is enjoyment in that. Surface-level [discussions] are commonplace, but the enjoyment [derived] from delving deep should be captured."

Swamishri encourages us to fully immerse ourselves in Satsang to appreciate and experience its profound benefits.

title: A Natural Love
text:
Swamishri awoke from his afternoon rest at 4:00 PM. Today, Swamishri expressed a wish to deviate from his daily routine and requested the attendant swamis, "Allow me to read for an hour [before continuing with the schedule]." He added, "Sākārāy (one of Shriji Maharaj's 108 names)," implying he would like to read the Sahajanand Nāmāvali.

Swamishri began reading at 4:15 PM and continued reading uninterruptedly until 5:27 PM. He then read the Swaminarayan Prakash until 5:40 PM, before proceeding with his breathing and walking exercises per his daily routine.

Swamishri's inclination and natural love for Satsang reading is a reflection of his unwavering devotion. Satsang reading is not merely a hobby; it is a means to connect with and become one with Bhagwan.

title: A Heart-Touching Encounter
text:
After the Guru Purnima evening sabha, Swamishri was returning to his residence. A young balak named Gunatit was standing nearby. The swamis asked Swamishri a question on his behalf, "At the end of the [welcome] dance, when this balak was in your immediate vicinity, you placed your hand on his chest. What were you doing?"

Swamishri responded, "I was measuring his heartbeat."

All were touched by Swamishri's response. Swamishri's empathetic nature prompted him to measure Gunatit's heart rate, which was elevated as a result of performing in the dance.

Swamishri's compassion is all-encompassing. He wholeheartedly cares for the physical, emotional, and spiritual well-being of all devotees.

title: A Singular Wish
text:
Following his lunch, Swamishri returned to his room. There, Gurumanan Swami inquired, "Swamishri, today marks the beginning of Pramukh Swami Maharaj's centennial year. In honor [of this day], do you have a special desire for the swamis and devotees on this occasion?"

Immediately, Swamishri expressed his inner wish, "May everyone become ekāntik (an elevated spiritual state consisting of righteousness, knowledge, detachment, and devotion). That's it."

Swamishri's singular wish for his devotees is for them to achieve a heightened spiritual state, one that allows them to experience the true bliss of Bhagwan.

title: The Greatest Award
text:
In the evening, as Swamishri was about to retire for the night, a discussion concerning various awards unfolded. Uttamyogi Swami asked, "If you were to receive a great award, would you accept it or not?"

Swamishri responded, "[I would] take it for the sake of taking it."

An attendant swami asked, "Bapa, in your opinion, what is the greatest award?"

Swamishri instantly answered, "Akshar!"

The swamis further inquired, "So 'Akshar' is an award?"

Swamishri explained, "No, it has to be created." Swamishri further elaborated, "If there is a poor [devotee] that lives in a hut but has firm faith; one should become a servant of his."

The swamis asked, "Is that the real award? Is that true greatness?"

Swamishri concurred in complete agreement.

In a world where accomplishments are acknowledged with accolades, for Swamishri, the greatest award of becoming Aksharrup is achieved by becoming a servant of a devotee.

title: Growing Closer To The Satpurush
text:
At approximately 7:00 PM, Swamishri attended a meeting with swamis who had come from North America. During the meeting, the swamis gave Swamishri a few updates concerning the upcoming adhiveshan and sought Swamishri's guidance. After the meeting, when the swamis departed Swamishri's room, Swamishri was waiting for the next meeting to begin. During this time, Swamishri continued to reflect on the adhiveshan. After a few moments, he turned to Gnanmanan Swami and without any prompt, said, "Mukhpath will bring you closer to the Satpurush."

In one statement, Swamishri revealed perhaps the greatest benefit of mukhpath. It not only increases one's knowledge, asmita, and faith, but it ultimately allows one to become closer to Swamishri.

On December 23, 2024, Swamishri again stressed the importance of mukhpath in the daily brahmavidhya lesson when he wrote, "Mukhpath brings us closer to the Satpurush."

title: A Home's True Value
text:
After puja, Swamshri approached a table to sanctify a variety of items. Bhagwatcharan Swami gestured towards a set of Akshar-Purushottam Maharaj murtis and said, "There is a devotee from the village of Sisva who has built a new bungalow worth nine crore rupees. These murtis are to be installed in that home."

As Swamishri sanctified the murtis, he said, "If the murtis are installed, then [the home] is worthy. Otherwise, [it is like] a crematorium."

Anything and everything devoid of Bhagwan is worthless to Swamishri whereas the presence of Bhagwan is priceless.

title: An Addiction For Kathā
text:
Due to the Atlanta Mandir Dashābdi (10-year anniversary) event, today's schedule was busy with extensive programs. Given the already demanding schedule, the attendant swamis informed Swamishri, "There is no kathā (discourse) today so that you can rest."

Swamishri replied, "Today, there should be kathā! Today is dashābdi."

Arrangements were swiftly made for Swamishri to deliver kathā. He blessed the assembly with a 25-minute discourse.

As Swamishri was leaving the hall, the swami managing the program folded his hands and humbly remarked, "Swami, we did not plan for a kathā to ensure your schedule is maintained."

Swamishri replied, "If not kathā, what [else] should we do?"

In the Yogi Gita, Yogiji Maharaj states, "One should cultivate an addiction for kathā-vārtā." Swamishri's life is a living example of one who is addicted to listening to and delivering kathā.

title: Bowing With Reverence
text:
Today, the attendant swamis asked Swamishri, "You bow down to Pujya Tyagvallabh Swami three or so times in the morning: once while performing darshan in the mandir below; later prior to puja; and then after puja. With what thought do you bow down [to him]?"

"[With] reverence," replied Swamishri. Then Swamishri added, "The more we bow down, the more we benefit."

Swamishri's habit of bowing to others with reverence is a testament to his unparalleled humility.

title: Respect For His Gurus
text:
While receiving naturopathy treatment, Swamishri was asked to lie down with his head facing the edge of the bed. However, in this process, Swamishri's feet were facing a wall that displayed a murti of Shastriji Maharaj. Thus, Swamishri immediately requested, "Cover Shastriji Maharaj's murti."

The attendant swamis asked, "Why?"

"My feet are extended in the direction of Shastriji Maharaj," replied Swamishri.

The attendant swamis responded, "But it (the murti) is placed above and your feet are below."

Swamishri firmly said, "No, cover it nonetheless."

Swamishri's devotion for his gurus is such that even the subtlest form of disrespect is intolerable.

title: Understanding The Satpurush
text:
During the evening sabha, a summary of the program based on the theme 'Iti Vachanamrutam' was presented to Swamishri, "A discussion was held on how we should understand the Satpurush. A variety of opinions were presented based on different qualities: saintliness, management, etc."

Thereafter, Swamishri was requested to describe how we should understand the Satpurush, as only he can reveal the true glory of the Satpurush.

Swamishri said, "[The Satpurush] eternally beholds Bhagwan. That is his greatest power. Everything else is possible [by others], but to behold Bhagwan is not possible."

Swamishri is eternally one with Bhagwan. They are inseparable. Therein lies his greatest strength.

title: True Rest
text:
After lunch, Swamishri returned to his room. Per his daily routine, it was time for his afternoon rest. However, Swamishri said, "I want to read."

The attendant swamis asked, "Do you not want to sleep?"

Swamishri expressed his disinterest for rest and began reading the July, 2019 edition of the Swaminarayan Prakash at 1:37 PM. Finally, at 2:10 PM, he agreed to take his afternoon rest.

Swamishri prioritizes Satsang reading even if it requires sacrificing his own rest. For Swamishri, Satsang reading is true rest.

title: New Year's Message
text:
While Swamishri was replying to letters, Gurumanan Swami asked, "Tomorrow is New Year's day according to the English calendar. Thus, please tell us how we can improve [for the coming year]?"

Swamishri replied, "You should [identify and] think about whatever mistakes you may have committed over the past year. In addition, ensure that you do not repeat the same mistakes this year."

Gurumanan Swami asked further, "Do you have any other message for 2018?"

Swamishri replied, "No. Happy New Year!"

The start of the New Year is filled with joy, excitement, and new resolutions. Swamishri encourages us to set aside time to reflect on our past experiences, learn from our mistakes, and set meaningful intentions for the year ahead.

title: Calm and Composed
text:
During a question and answer session, Adarshjivan Swami asked Swamishri about an incident that had occurred in 1970. He said, "In 1970, you were traveling [by air] from Entebbe, Uganda to Mwanza, Tanzania [with Yogiji Maharaj and Pramukh Swami Maharaj]. During the flight, you were seated next to the airplane's door when it had unexpectedly come open. In a situation like this, one would [naturally] panic at the possibility of falling to one's death in Lake Victoria below. Swamishri, did you panic?"

Swamishri replied, "Both gurus were present. Thus, there was nothing to worry about."

Swamishri's ability to remain calm and composed in all situations is a reflection of his unwavering faith and conviction in Maharaj and his gurus.

title: A Message in Swahili
text:
After delivering blessings, Swamishri added one statement in Swahili, "Tumempata Mungu. Tuna furaha," which means "We have attained Bhagwan. We are happy."

Whether he speaks in Gujarati, Hindi, English, Swahili, or any other language, Swamishri continually reminds us that the source of true happiness is Bhagwan, whom we have attained through Swamishri.

title: Exceptional Memory
text:
After Swamishri's meal, while the swamis introduced Yoginbhai Chaniyara, Swamishri added, "When we visited his factory, he was 6 years old. [When] I threw a ball, he hit it and [the ball] spun round and round."

Everyone was surprised, especially Yoginbhai, because this event had occurred 37 years prior! However, Swamishri remembered it like it happened yesterday!

Swamishri's memory is exceptional; he values the time he spends with others and ultimately uses those moments to connect with countless swamis and devotees.

title: Samp Without Any Exception
text:
After Swamishri's morning ashirwad, yuvak karyakars from Louisville offered a samp-themed garland to Swamishri. After accepting the garland, Swamishri said, "Samp has to be kept. 'It is [a] must.'"

Soon thereafter, while returning to his residence, Swamishri stopped to take a group photo with approximately 30 yuvak karyakars. During this time, Swamishri was still dwelling on the topic of samp. Thus, he turned to the yuvaks and said, "One may understand the glory of 30 people but if one has an allergy (aversion) towards one person, then everything becomes a waste (futile)."

Swamishri emphasizes the importance of developing samp with everyone without exception. True samp is inclusive of all. 'It is [a] must!

title: Disregard For Taste
text:
After performing a routine check-up, the naturopathic specialist voiced his opinion, "For now, Swamishri should avoiding consuming the following items: sweets, fried foods, chāsh, and yogurt."

Hearing this, Swamishri became pleased and clapped as he exclaimed, "Very good!"

While most would consider such advice an unwelcome restriction, Swamishri's reaction highlights his preference for simplicity and complete disregard for taste.

title: "Suhradbhāv"
text:
During the evening question and answer session, Swamishri was asked, "Swami, in 2017, when you were in Africa, you came to know about an incident. Subashbhai, who was travelling by car saw a fellow devotee, Mahendrabhai, walking along the side of the road. Seeing this, Subashbhai stopped his vehicle, invited Mahendrabhai in the car, and gave him a ride to his destination. You were so fond of Subashbhai's benevolence that you recalled this incident 20-25 times in a variety of ways. What specifically did you like about this incident that earned your rājipo?"

"Suhradbhāv," replied Swamishri.

Through this one-word answer, Swamishri reveals a sure-fire method to earn his rājipo: by demonstrating empathy, fraternity, and genuine care for a fellow devotee.

title: Nirdoshbuddhi In Everyone
text:
Swamishri was returning to his residence. Shri Han Kop, a staunch devotee from Holland, was standing nearby. He asked Swamishri in English, "What is the best thing I can do for you?"

Swamishri replied, "Nirdoshbuddhi in everyone."

"But you have to help me," prayed Han Kop.

Swamishri gestured assuredly and responded, "[You] will receive lots of help."

In Swamishri's words, the best thing we can do for him is to consider Maharaj, Swamishri, and their devotees to be faultless and divine.

title: A Profound Impact
text:
Swamishri had traveled from Atlanta to Chicago yesterday. The security personnel that had offered their services to Swamishri in Atlanta had written a letter of appreciation, "The time that we have spent with you has been engraved into our minds, hearts, and souls. Our thoughts will be with you. We look forward to the opportunity to once again serve you as your protection detail."

Swamishri's divine persona leaves a profound and lasting impression on all that come into contact with him.

title: A Discussion in English
text:
On Zambia day, during the evening question and answer session, Swamishri was asked, "When you were in central Africa with Yogi Bapa, he would have you ask and answer questions in English. Accordingly, please say something in English."

Swamishri said, "This Satsang is divine."

The swamis asked further in English, "Who are you?"

"I am Akshar," replied Swamishri.

While remembering his guru, Yogiji Maharaj, Swamishri lovingly fulfilled the swamis' requests of speaking in and answering in English. In doing so, he revealed his identity as the form of Akshar and highlighted the divinity of Satsang.

title: Comfortable in All Situations
text:
During the evening question and answer session, Swamishri was asked, "In 2009, when you visited Lusaka, Zambia, a mahapuja was arranged on the occasion of Pramukh Swami Maharaj's birthday celebration. During the mahapuja, rather than providing you with a cushion, a thin quilt was folded and laid down for you to sit on. At that time, the swamis asked, 'Are you comfortable?' You placed your hand on your heart and said, 'It is 'comfortable' here. Therefore, it is 'comfortable' everywhere.' Swami, you remain at peace in all situations. What is the reason for this?"

Swamishri replied, "We have attained Bhagwan. By attaining Bhagwan, there is [an abundance of] peace. Secondly, [due to] understanding and wisdom."

Swamishri's life teaches us how we can remain 'comfortable' and at peace in all situations: through wisdom, understanding, and by fully appreciating whom we have attained through Swamishri.

title: True Sevak
text:
In the evening, during the question and answer session, Swamishri was asked, "In 2019, your residence was at Subhashbhai's home. On the last day, prior to your departure, you were cleaning the bathroom when the attendant swami said, 'We would have cleaned it. Why did you clean it?' At that time, you responded by saying, 'A swayamsevak (volunteer) should be willing to do seva.' But even at this age, why did you choose to do this seva?"

Swamishri replied, "The more seva we do, the more we benefit. Just as one who has a billion rupees wishes for more, when it comes to seva, [one should understand that] this is an alaukik (out of this world; divine) matter. Regardless of how much seva we do, it is not enough."

Despite being the guru, Swamishri considers himself to be a sevak. His example inspires volunteerism in various forms throughout the world.

title: Parabrahma's Service
text:
On the occasion of the inauguration of the newly constructed 'Yagnapurush Gate' in front of the mandir, Swamishri arrived and stood under the entrance gate. Everyone was awaiting the arrival of Gujarat Chief Minister Shri Vijaybhai Rupani and other ministers.

Shri Harikrishna Maharaj was placed next to Swamishri on a beautiful seat. Swamishri's eyes fell on Shri Harikrishna Maharaj. It was 9:25 AM; yet the sun's fierce rays were beaming directly on Shri Harikrishna Maharaj. Without informing or directing anyone, Swamishri himself stood next to Shri Harikrishna Maharaj so that his shadow could provide shade cover for Shri Harikrishna Maharaj.

Truly, Aksharbrahma forever remains in the service of Parabrahma.

title: I like everybody
text:
After completing mandir darshan, Swamishri arrived at the back of the mandir, an area commonly known as the rupchoki. Here, a swami requested Swamishri to say a phrase in English. Swamishri responded, "I like everybody."

Swamishri's statement is rooted in his appreciation for all. He does not harbor animosity for anyone. He sees Bhagwan in everyone and therefore likes everyone.

title: Grace and Efforts
text:
During the afternoon katha, Swamishri said, "...When the swabhāvs (vicious natures) are eradicated, one experiences the bliss of Akshardham. Why has this not occurred, despite [Bhagwan blessing us with] an abundance of grace? Grace! Grace! Grace! But we must put forth an [adequate] effort. We are not making an effort. We are leaving everything up to Bhagwan…Merely leaving everything up to Bhagwan is not how it works. We must put forth an effort."

Then, the swamis asked, "Swami…What should our efforts be like [so that we earn Bhagwan's grace]?"

Swamishri replied, "The efforts should be genuine and rooted in faith. If these two [measures are taken], then everything is encompassed."

Swamishri encourages us to take accountability for our own destiny. Through genuine efforts and faith, we can earn the grace of Bhagwan, who will liberate us from our swabhāvs and bless us with the bliss of Akshardham.

title: A Friend and Enemy
text:
During the Bal Din evening program, Swamishri offered guidance in English concerning mobile phone usage, "If you use it in front of your parents and for your studies and satsang, then it is your friend. And if you use it to waste your time after films, games, etc., then it is your enemy."

Swamishri reminds us that the use of mobile phones and other devices can be both helpful and harmful. He encourages us to use it with discretion and avoid allowing it to become our worst enemy.

title: His Life Long Practice
text:
After the afternoon kathā, Swamishri was about to stand up from his seat. To make it easier for Swamishri to stand, Shrutipriya Swami suggested, "Lean forward and stand up."

Swamishri casually remarked, "True value, indeed, lies in leaning (bowing) forward."

Swamishri's response was simple yet profound. His message resonates deeply because of his lifelong practice of bowing to others.

title: Remarkable Memory
text:
While Swamishri was meeting devotees, a youth, Manan Patel, came forward. Seeing him, Swamishri said, "He sat with us throughout the entire nagar yātrā (procession)."

"Where and in what year?" the swamis inquired.

"In 2004 in Vadodara," replied Manan. "I was walking [during the procession when Swamishri saw me]. Swamishri called me forward, had me sit near his feet, implying, 'You should sit here.'"

This incident had occurred 13 years ago. Manan was a balak at the time! Naturally, he had grown considerably and his face had changed. Yet, Swamishri immediately recognized him and associated him with the correct event.

Swamishri's remarkable memory in 2017 is just as notable as the genuine care he displayed in 2004.

title: Reverence and Respect
text:
After the evening assembly, a fabric adorned with handprints from the balaks and bal karyakars was laid out along Swamishri's path. As Swamishri stepped foot on it, he immediately hesitated, drew the swamis' attention to the area in question and requested, "Please remove 'Swaminarayan.'" In an effort to convey the balaks' and bal karyakars' heartfelt Jay Swaminarayan to Swamishri, the phrase, "Jay Swaminarayan," had been written at the end of the fabric. As a result, Swamishri was being unintentionally requested to step foot on Bhagwan Swaminarayan's name! Though nobody else had noticed, Swamishri was quick to point out the oversight.

Swamishri perpetually maintains utmost reverence and respect for Bhagwan Swaminarayan in every situation and at all times.

title: The Perfect Precedent
text:
In the afternoon, Swamishri awoke from his nap early and was unable to fall back asleep. Swamishri expressed his wish to view the first episode of the Aksharbrahma Gunatit Satra kathā series on "Prāptino Vichār."

The kathā series was scheduled to commence later in the evening, but the swamis from Sarangpur had sent a special link of the video recording for Swamishri. Thus, Swamishri took a seat in the room where he reads and responds to letters, and viewed the entire sabha. He was extremely pleased! After listening to Atmatrupt Swami's kathā, Swamishri said one word, "Spasht (clear)." In doing so, he praised Atmatrupt Swami's clear and concise messaging along with his ability to clearly articulate his thoughts in a manner that is easy to digest.

Swamishri set the perfect precedent by enthusiastically watching the hour-long inaugural sabha on prāptino vichār. In doing so, he became the first to view the Aksharbhrama Gunatit Satra!

title: Fully Present
text:
In the evening, when Swamishri was ready to begin cheshtā, Shrutipriya Swami asked, "Swami, should I start the cheshtā?"

"Is everyone ready?" inquired Swamishri.

In this manner, Swamishri stressed the importance of being fully present and absorbed in Bhagwan Swaminarayan's divine form during cheshtā. Swamishri's example naturally inspires all to similarly immerse themselves, both physically and mentally, while offering devotion.

title: Three Benefits
text:
Whenever a discussion concerning austerities occurs, the attendant swamis often inform Swamishri, "Even if you are willing to accept an illness, you will not be able to because of the austerities the Satsang community is performing for the sake of your health." Swamishri typically responds with an approving smile and nods his head in agreement. Today, during the discussion, Swamishri was asked, "Swami, you are certainly pleased with austerities. But what is the benefit of that rājipo?"

"Akshardham" replied Swamishri. He added in English, "Towards Akshardham."

Swamishri continued, "[By performing austerities], you increase your desire to please the Satpurush. [In fact], you do not merely feel like pleasing him; but it turns into action."

Finally, Swamishri explained a third benefit, "It increases your faith and trust considerably."

In this manner, Swamishri revealed three distinct benefits of performing austerities.

title: Engrossed in Smruti
text:
As Swamishri was preparing for his morning nap, Uttamyogi Swami recited a line from a kirtan that is typically sung as Bhagwan prepares to go to sleep for the night, "Akhiyāmā nindar bharani re, podho podho Sahajanand Swami," which means, "Your eyes appear drowsy; sleep [well], Sahajanand Swami."

Hearing this, Swamishri initially replied no and said, "This is false."

But Uttamyogi Swami rebutted, "Your eyes are visibly filled with drowsiness."

"I was awake the entire night," Swamishri admitted. "...I was merely laying there."

"If you didn't sleep, what did you do?" inquired Uttamyogi Swami.

"Bhajan," replied Swamishri.

"How did you do bhajan?" Uttamyogi Swami asked.

"I did smruti of Yogi Bapa," Swamishri revealed.

Despite not getting sufficient rest the previous night, Swamishri continued with his normal morning routine without attempting to catch up on rest.

title: Pleased the Children
text:
Today was Bal Din. Thus, Swamishri had asked, "How many children will come [today]?"

When the attendant swamis asked Swamishri why he wanted to know, Swamishri revealed, "I would like to feed everyone chocolates. Can arrangements be made?"

The attendant swami replied, "Yes, they will be made. Because it is your wish, [the chocolates] will be served."

Accordingly, during the evening sabha, the chocolate bars were brought forward so that Swamishri could sanctify them. Swamishri lovingly and joyfully sanctified the chocolates, which were distributed to the children at the end of sabha.

Swamishri has a special bond with children. He values their innocence and potential. He sees the divinity of his guru, Yogiji Maharaj, in them. As a result, he genuinely takes immense pleasure in pleasing them.

title: Absolute Faith and Trust
text:
During the evening question and answer session, a discussion ensued concerning a comment that Swamishri has previously made: "One should wish the best for even one's enemies."
