The swamis said, "Bapa, only the gunātit gurus can operate like this. Others cannot even think like this."

Continuing, the swamis raised several concerns with respect to this topic.

In response, Swamishri explained, "Look, Shriji Maharaj is the all-doer. Even a dry leaf cannot be moved without His wish. Thus, why should we worry? Whether you believe or not, Shriji Maharaj is the all-doer. Moreover, everything that occurs, occurs solely because of His wish...and whatever transpires will be for the best."

Swamishri's faith in Bhagwan Swaminarayan is unwavering. He reminds others to remain worry-free in all situations because of his absolute trust in Bhagwan Swaminarayan.

title: Honored the Tabla Instructor
text:
After Swamishri's puja and morning blessings, as the attendant swamis were closing the curtains inside Swamishri's glass cabin, Swamishri pointed to his left in the direction of the tabla player and called him forward. Then, Brahmakirtan Swami introduced him and said, "His name is Raja Thakur. He has a PhD in tabla and teaches our balaks and kishores. He is very devout and has come today to offer his devotion in your puja."

Swamishri was pleased with his devotion and advised the balaks and kishores, "Learn properly [from him]."

In Satsang Diksha shlok 160, Swamishri has written, "One should always respect the learned, seniors and teachers. According to one's capacity, one should honor them with good words and other such deeds." By honoring the tabla instructor, Swamishri set a great example for all youth. Moreover, he inspired the youth to strive for excellence in all pursuits.

title: Identifying the Silhouette
text:
After the evening sabha, Swamishri entered the elevator while returning to his residence. Inside the elevator, a poster was displayed, depicting a silhouette of Swamishri walking hand in hand with a child. As Swamishri observed the poster, Brahmavatsal Swami pointed to the silhouette of Swamishri and asked, "Who is this?"

Swamishri immediately responded, "Shastriji Maharaj."

This moment exemplified Swamishri's profound humility; never recognizing himself, but always seeing his gurus instead.

title: Oblivious to Taste
text:
During dinner, Swamishri typically eats seven to eight pieces of papaya and only one piece of mango. However, on this day, both the papaya and mango had a similar color. As a result, the papaya was mistakenly served instead of mango, and the mango was served in place of the papaya. Thus, he ate seven to eight pieces of mango and, mistaking it for mango, consumed only one piece of papaya. Although the difference in taste between papaya and mango is significant, Swamishri remained completely unaware of the mix-up.

Swamishri is completely detached from and above the sense of taste. During his meals, rather than savoring the flavors of the food itself, his mind is entirely absorbed in the flavor of Bhagwan and his gurus.

title: Earning Profit
text:
After puja, while Swamishri was taking his medication, a swami commented, "Swami, [at the end of puja,] you fold your hands so much (for so long) that we get tired [of keeping our hands folded for as long as you]!"

Swamishri chuckled and replied, "Even then, I am not satisfied. A profit is being earned!" Then, while slowly extending both of his hands outward, he added, "Dās (servant)... everyone's dās… everyone's dās," implying that the more we embrace servanthood, the greater the profit.

Swamishri places immense value in becoming a dās; it is the path to build spiritual wealth.

title: The Greatest Seva
text:
While imparting today's Brahmavidya lesson, Swamishri wrote, "Gun levā jevi koi sevā nathi," which means, "There is no seva on par with perceiving virtues [in others]." Swamishri further elaborated, "All of the scriptures have been encompassed. [To put this in practice] seems easy, like a matter of a two paisa, but everything is encompassed within it. Begin perceiving virtues! We waver back and forth when it comes to perceiving virtues. We falter by choosing sides. This causes a great deal of disarray [and disorder]. One should do this seva with pure intentions."

Through the Brahmavidya lesson, Swamishri redefined the meaning of seva, while simultaneously echoing the sentiments of a sermon from Gunatitannad Swami, "Serve according to one's own faith, but never do disservice. What is that disservice? To perceive faults in others (2/132)."

title: Fifty Vachnamruts
text:
Yogicharitam, a book written by Pujya Ishwarcharan Swami containing a unique collection of incidents from Yogiji Maharaj's life, was being read aloud in Swamishri's presence. During the reading, the topic of mukhpāth came up. The swamis asked Swamishri, "How many Vachanamruts did you memorize?"

"[I] had done approximately fifty Vachanamruts; at Yogi Bapa's behest," replied Swamishri.

From the beginning, Swamishri adopted an inclination for mukhpāth from his guru, Yogiji Maharaj. Even today, like his guru, Swamishri continues to inspire countless devotees to do mukhpāth as a means to earn the guru's innermost blessings.

title: Ever Vigilant
text:
When Swamishri completed breakfast, a bowl was placed before Swamishri to wash his hands. Seeing the bowl's appearance, Swamishri immediately asked, "Is it silver?" The swamis replied, "No. It is an 'imitation.'" Only then did Swamishri proceed to wash his hands.

Swamishri adheres to the smallest of niyams prescribed by Bhagwan Swaminarayan. He is ever vigilant to ensure that he does not violate even a single command.

title: Perfecting Devotion
text:
In the evening, Swamishri was seated, prepared to begin cheshtā. Shrutipriya Swami asked, "Shall I start the cheshtā?"

Swamishri replied, "Is everyone 'set'?"

"Physically, everyone is 'set,' but not mentally," Uttamyogi Swami replied.

Swamishri advised, "The mind is often quite distant," implying that one should make a sincere effort to stabilize and engage the mind while offering devotion.

Swamishri teaches us to offer perfect devotion by preparing and engaging our mind, body, and soul.

title: Inherent Flexibility
text:
As Swamishri was taking leave from the morning sabha, Apurvamuni Swami playfully asked Swamishri, "Do you really want to go?"

Immediately, Swamishri extended his hand toward the sofa while preparing to take his seat and humbly said, "No; whatever you say."

Apurvamuni Swami folded his hands and said, "No, no, Swami! You may take leave."
Only then did Swamishri depart from the sabha hall.

Swamishri's innate flexibility is a reflection of his limitless humility. Though he is the guru, he behaves as a servant of servants.

title: Habit of Satsang Reading
text:
In the evening, Swamishri was ahead of schedule. Subsequently, the swamis requested him to retire early for the night. However, Swamishri glanced at the clock and said, "It is [too] early."

Then, while making a reading gesture, he asked for the Gujarati Bal Prakash. Swamishri had started reading the Bal Prakash the previous day but had only finished half of it. Thus, on this evening, he continued to read the Bal Prakash for about 25 minutes.

Later, as the discussion turned to scriptures, Swamishri remarked, "All pilgrimage places reside within Maharaj, Swami, and Yogi Bapa."

With this final thought, Swamishri retired for the night.

Swamishri has cultivated a lifelong habit of reading our scriptures, the biographies of Maharaj and our gurus, and other BAPS publications. He cherishes them deeply and considers Satsang reading as a vital endeavor for spiritual progress.

title: Preference for Bland Food
text:
During Swamishri's lunch, Gnanpriya Swami recalled an incident, "Swami! This incident is from last year. I had come to Tithal to take your lābh. You eat such simple and bland food but in contrast, you distribute nice [flavorful] prasād to us swamis. So I had a question and asked you, 'Everyone else enjoys fine foods whereas you eat this type of bland food. Thus, do you never wish to enjoy fine foods?' to which you responded, 'No. Never do I wish for nor envy it.'"

Swamishri's profound detachment from all sensory pleasures is particularly evident in his lack of preference for taste. His preference for simple, bland food reflects his elevated spiritual state.

title: Selfless Love
text:
During a session with kishores and kishoris, Swamishri answered the following questions on the topic of love.

Question: "How does your love differ from worldly love?"
Swamishri: "Worldly love is filled with complete selfishness, whereas the Satpurush's love is filled with selflessness."

Question: "All of the kishores and kishoris sitting here wish to experience your love. However, we get caught up in worldly love because we are continuously engaged in worldly activities. Thus, please explain how we can continuously experience your love, the love of the Satpurush?"
Swamishri: "Practice satsang and follow āgnā. By following āgnā, you will become closer to Bhagwan. If you do not follow āgnā, you will become absorbed in perishable, insignificant, and harmful matters."

Swamishri's love is selfless, absolute, and unwavering. By following āgnā, we can continuously experience his love and become closer to Bhagwan.

title: Understanding the Satpurush
text:
During the evening sabha, Swamishri answered several questions:

Question: "How important is the Satpurush on the path to moksha?"
Swamishri: "[The Satpurush is] of absolute importance. Without the Satpurush, everything is meaningless. It is because of the Satpurush that everything is possible."

Question: "How should we take lābh of the Satpurush?"
Swamishri: "By firmly following the niyams established by Maharaj, both Bhagwan and the Satpurush are immensely pleased."

Question: "You are the Satpurush. How should we understand your greatness?"
Swamishri, "Akshar and Purushottam. 'Aksharam Aham Purushottamadāso'smi'. We are the servants of the servants of the servants of the servants of the servants. And He (Maharaj) alone is Bhagwan. This conviction must be deeply instilled in the soul and should never waver; this is what has to be done."

title: Sharing is Caring
text:
The chocolate that had arrived earlier in the afternoon was offered to Swamishri in the evening. Swamishri accepted a small piece in a unique manner. Rather than chewing it, he placed it in his mouth and allowed it to melt.

Then, Vinaypriya Swami asked, "Should we give the rest of the chocolate to Uttamyogi Swami?"

Swamishri said yes. However, as Uttamyogi Swami was about to pick up the remaining piece, Swamishri stopped him and, through a gesture, instructed him to break it in half and give one half to Vinaypriya Swami. Seeing this, Vinaypriya Swami said, "I already had some after the afternoon discourse; he hasn't had any yet. Let him have the rest."

Swamishri agreed and gave Uttamyogi Swami the remaining piece.

Swamishri teaches us how we should accept prasād. Sharing prasād with others is a spiritual value that fosters unity and fraternity.

title: Memorable Yawn
text:
During Swamishri's breakfast, when a bowl of shiro was placed before him, Swamishri yawned. Then, leveraging a play on words, Swamishri said, "Bagāsu khāi lidhu." Although Swamishri's comment is commonly translated as 'I yawned,' the literal translation is 'I have eaten a yawn.'

Vinaypriya Swami replied, "When you yawned, you only ingested air. Now, we should fill that space [in your stomach] with shiro."

Accordingly, with the sole intention of pleasing the swamis, Swamishri ate one spoonful of shiro.

In this manner, Swamishri cleverly utilized a play on words through this light interaction. Moreover, he fulfilled the swamis' wishes and gave them an everlasting memory.

title: Thoughtful and Considerate
text:
During Swamishri's lunch, a balak loudly yet innocently said, "Please eat jalebi!"

Hearing this, despite not being fond of sweets, Swamishri immediately took a small piece of jalebi and ate it. The balak's father then said, "He likes jalebi a lot. Thus, when he saw the jalebi in the thāl, he [could not help but] ask you to eat some."

In response, Swamishri asked for jalebi to be brought for all of the balaks present. Usually, chocolate is given to the balaks at the start of Swamishri's meal, but on this day, jalebi was brought per Swamishri's request. When the jalebi arrived, Swamishri instructed the swamis, "Do not distribute this jalebi to everyone the same way you [distribute] chocolates. Only give it to those who like it."

Swamishri is mindful of everyone's preferences. He is ever considerate, a virtue that stems from his empathic nature.

title: Swamishri's Eternal Identity
text:
In the evening, as Swamishri was on his way to grant samip darshan, he entered the elevator. Here, a poster displaying the five eternal entities in ascending order was visible. Swamishri was asked, "Swami, among these, where does an Aksharmukta stand?"

Swamishri replied, "[An Aksharmukta] is incorporated by jiva or ishwar because, at its core, it is either a jiva or ishwar."

Later, when Swamishri returned to his room, he was asked, "Among jiva, ishwar, māyā, Brahma, and Parabrahma, where is your place?"

Swamishri answered, "Brahma."

In this manner, Swamishri revealed his identity: the present form of Aksharbrahma, eternally above māyā and forever in the service of Parabrahma.

title: Mutual Love and Affection
text:
When the afternoon discourse concluded, Bhaktiswarup Swami, who had arrived from Chicago, approached Swamishri. He first bowed to Swamishri by touching his feet and then, clenching his fist, extended his right hand forward to give Swamishri a fist bump. Swamishri often affectionately greets him in this unique manner. Thus he, too, reciprocated the gesture and returned the fist bump.

Then, Swamishri innocently said, "I have forgotten how to return [a fist bump correctly]."

Hearing this, Bhaktiswarup Swami reassured him, saying, "You did it correctly!" He then added, "I am happy [and blessed] after having your darshan."

Swamishri agreed and replied, "When there is mutual love and affection, you will certainly experience joy!"

Through this unique interaction, Swamishri revealed the premise for his relationship with all swamis and devotees: mutual love and affection.

title: All Mandirs are Akshardham
text:
Before retiring for the night, Swamishri said, "Now, there are four days [remaining before we leave] here."

Uttamyogi Swami asked, "Where are we going from here?"

"Akshardham!" replied Swamishri.

Uttamyogi Swami questioned, "Do you not wish to remain here on this earth?"

"Why not? There are many kāryakars here, so why wouldn't we stay?"

"You mentioned Akshardham so which Akshardham are you referring to – Gandhinagar, Delhi, Surat, or Robbinsville? On this earth, there are these Akshardhams."

Swamishri replied, "All Mandirs are Akshardham."

Swamishri considers all BAPS Mandirs to be the divine abode of Bhagwan Swaminarayan, who, along with Gunatitanand Swami Maharaj and the Gunātit Paramparā, eternally grant darshan to devotees and well-wishers – a pure representation of Akshardham.

title: How Bhagwan Accepts Thaal
text:
During a discussion, the swamis mentioned, "Yogi Bapa was once asked, 'Because Maharaj eats the food [that is offered to him], then the [portions in the] thāl should be reduced, correct?' In response, Yogi Bapa stated, 'He does eat, but He leaves behind 'double' the amount.'"

Swamishri then remarked, "No one has ever explained it this way. Such an interpretation would not occur even in a dream. [Yogi Bapa] provided a profound explanation! If He were to eat the food [without leaving prasād], no one would offer thāl."

Swamishri then added, "Thāl should be offered with love and done with devotion. Then Bhagwan accepts it."

By elaborating on Yogiji Maharaj's explanation, Swamishri provided a unique perspective on the manner in which Maharaj, Swami, and our gurus accept our devotion. Furthermore, he explained how we can ensure that Bhagwan accepts our devotion.

title: Trusting the Guru's Words
text:
During a discussion, Priyavrat Swami said, "We have attained a samarth (capable, powerful, competent) guru."

Swamishri agreed and added, "We have attained an exceptionally, exceptionally, exceptionally samarth guru."

Priyavrat Swami then asked, "Now that we have attained a samarth guru, how can we learn to [fully] accept his words within one's heart?"

Swamishri said, "When one attains realization, it naturally happens."

Priyavrat Swami further inquired, "Swami, what should we do until we attain realization?"

Swamishri answered, "Have faith and accept whatever he says as the truth."

Through this short interaction, Swamishri advised that once a true guru is attained, one must accept his guidance, commands, and blessings with absolute faith in order to achieve complete realization.

title: Trusting the Guru's Words
text:

Swamishri agreed and added, "We have attained an exceptionally, exceptionally, exceptionally samarth guru."

Priyavrat Swami then asked, "Now that we have attained a samarth guru, how can we learn to [fully] accept his words within one's heart?"

Swamishri said, "When one attains realization, it naturally happens."

Priyavrat Swami further inquired, "Swami, what should we do until we attain realization?"

Swamishri answered, "Have faith and accept whatever he says as the truth."

Through this short interaction, Swamishri advised that once a true guru is attained, one must accept his guidance, commands, and blessings with absolute faith in order to achieve complete realization.

title: Worldly and Spiritual Blessings
text:
Today, special arrangements were made for nine couples to get engaged or married at the Mandir. After doing darshan and performing ārti, Swamishri blessed the newly engaged and newly married couples, saying, "You have joined [as a couple]. Thus, may everyone experience bliss physically, mentally, and financially; and [everyone] will be able to become ekāntik (a spiritually elevated state encompassing righteousness, wisdom, detachment, and devotion)."

Swamishri bestowed both worldly and spiritual blessings upon them. His message is a reminder to never lose sight of our ultimate goal of becoming ekāntik.

title: I Know Him
text:
A devotee, Mafatbhai, had come for Swamishri's darshan. Prior to meeting Swamishri, he had informed Amrutswarup Swami, "When you introduce me to Swamishri, please tell him that I am from Bochasan."

While introducing him, Amrutswarup Swami informed Swamishri that Mafatbhai had served as a site engineer at Robbinsville Akshardham. However, he forgot to mention the fact that Mafatbhai is originally from Bochasan. Then, to Amrutswarup Swami's surprise, Swamishri said, "He is from Bochasan! And I know him." In this manner, Swamishri fulfilled Mafatbhai's wish.

Swamishri's compassion is reflected in his remarkable memory. He genuinely cares, and therefore, he remembers, which allows him to connect with his devotees on a meaningful level.

title: The Name Vandan
text:
After Swamishri's dinner, he was asked, "There is a balak who has a school project in which he needs to answer three questions: What is his name? Who gave him his name? And why was he given that name? The balak's name is Vandan. You had given him the name Vandan. But this balak has a question: 'Why did you name me Vandan?'"

"The name Vandan was given because everyone must [learn to] bow down and become humble," Swamishri replied.

Every gesture, decision, and action of Swamishri inspires others to embrace humility, a virtue he exemplifies in every aspect of his life.

title: Heartfelt Concern
text:
The Yuva Adhiveshan inaugural sabha was scheduled to take place this evening. Swamishri, together with Shri Harikrishna Maharaj, sat in a golf cart near his residence. The yuvaks, accompanied by a band, led the way towards the sabha hall with much fanfare. The atmosphere was filled with joy and vigor. Everyone's mind was completely engrossed in the grandeur of the procession.

However, Swamishri, who was focused on the yuvaks walking barefoot, remarked, "Don't they feel hot? The stone tiles must be hot from the intense heat of the entire day."

While everyone was celebrating Swamishri's arrival with great enthusiasm, in that moment, Swamishri's thoughts were with the yuvaks. Swamishri's compassion and concern for others' well-being reflect his selfless love and deep empathetic nature.

title: True Brahmavidhya
text:
In the evening, during the Bal Din program themed 'The College of Brahmavidyā,' the children requested Swamishri, "Swami, please impart a Brahmavidyā lesson that enables us to unceasingly experience the bliss of Maharaj, you, and this Satsang; one that leads to us losing all interest in worldly pleasures."

In response, Swamishri wrote, "Shriji says, 'Everyone is divine.' To live accordingly is true Brahmavidyā."

Swamishri's consistent message of perceiving divinity in others is an all-encompassing spiritual lesson that offers both tangible and intangible benefits.

title: The Power of Agna
text:
Today was Swamishri's final day in Atlanta. After performing darshan in the morning, as Swamishri exited from the back of the Mandir, a group of yuvak-aged volunteers showed Swamishri a picture of a heart and asked, "You have kept a place for us in your heart, but what should we do so that we can reserve a place for you in our hearts?"

"[Follow] āgnā," replied Swamishri.

Then, as Swamishri entered the sant āshram, a yuvak made a gesture by joining both hands together and asked, "Which gesture represents cultivating intense love and attachment for you?"

Again, Swamishri said, "Āgnā."

Through these short interactions, Swamishri revealed the importance of following āgnā. It is the key ingredient that enables one to develop both affection and a deep attachment to Swamishri, and, in his words, it is the tried-and-true method of securing his place in our hearts forever.

title: Preserving Respect for Thakorji
text:
After ārti, Swamishri approached the hindolo. The string attached to the hindolo was touching the ground. Swamishri immediately bent down to pick it up, properly folded it into a small loop and began swinging Thakorji. Swamishri was asked, "Why did you do that?"

On Swamishri's behalf, the attendant swamis replied, "In order to maintain respect for Thakorji…with the thought that the string of Thakorji's hindolo should not touch our feet." Hearing this, Swamishri fully agreed.

Swamishri ensures that respect for Thakorji is always upheld, no matter how big or small it may seem. His attention to detail is a testament to his absolute devotion to Bhagwan.

title: Inclination for Austerity
text:
Swamishri sat down to have breakfast. Vinaypriya Swami, the attendant swami that prepares Swamishri's meals, placed shiro in Swamishri's thāl. With a dispirited expression, Swamishri asked, "Do I have to eat this?"

Vinaypriya Swami nodded and said, "[Yes,] you should eat it."

Swamishri replied, "If I were to fast, would it not be okay?"

Then, everyone humbly requested him to accept it. Only then did Swamishri unenthusiastically eat the shiro.

Swamishri's lifelong inclination for austerity is unwavering. His self-discipline is a reflection of his profound spirituality.

title: The Top of the Top
text:
After waking up from his afternoon nap at 3:45 PM, Swamishri engaged in his walking exercise, during which he took a seat for a brief rest. Then, without context, Swamishri began to recite both Yogiji Maharaj's jivan mantra and the siddhānt mantra, respectively, "Bhagwan saunu bhalu karo (May Bhagwan do good to all)…Aksharam Aham Purushottamadāso'smi (I am Akshar, a servant of Purushottam)."

An attendant swami asked, "Do you continually have these thoughts?"

Swamishri responded, "Yes!"

The attendant swami further questioned, "Swami, what is encompassed by the good of all? What [thought] occupies your mind [when you say this]?"

Swamishri immediately said, "Moksha. Nothing else; nothing less. This goodness is the 'top' of the 'top.'"

Through this casual interaction, Swamishri reinforced the understanding that there is nothing greater than attaining moksha. Nothing else; nothing less.

title: Pleased with the Balaks
text:
After waking up from his afternoon nap, Swamishri was briefed about the evening program details. The balaks had prepared an elaborate program centered around the Akshar-Purushottam Siddhānt. Thus, Swamishri was informed, "Today is Siddhānt Din, and the balaks will be holding a discussion on it."

Hearing this, Swamishri became disappointed and said, "By the time we go [to sabha], everything will have been concluded."

In accordance with his wishes, the schedule was adjusted and Swamishri viewed the program with immense joy and enthusiasm. Pleased with their performance, he showered his blessings upon them.

Swamishri's deep appreciation for the balaks' efforts was reflected in his wish to witness their performance. Swamishri is always eager to bless the balaks and consistently goes above and beyond to grant them his divine bliss.

title: Remembering Bhagatji Maharaj
text:
In Swamishri's blessings during the evening sabha on the occasion of Bhagatji Maharaj's birthday celebrations, he said, "Just as the tongue of Gunatitanand Swami would turn, so would the body of Bhagatji Maharaj; and he attained the ekāntik (spiritually elevated) state. The insults, verbal abuses, and contempt he tolerated are things that no one else can endure; and even in the future, no one will be able to tolerate [as he did]. He was known as, 'Bhagatji, the one who remains unaffected despite enduring all forms of insult.' Such was Bhagatji Maharaj, whom we attained through our lineage of gurus."

On the occasion of Bhagatji Maharaj's birthday, Swamishri teaches us to reflect on the virtues Bhagatji Maharaj exemplified. His life serves as a reminder to follow our guru's commands and endure any hardships that we may face for the sake of earning our guru's rājipo.

title: A Perpetual Message
text:
After his morning puja, as Swamishri was walking towards his residence, a devotee from Canada asked him a question. "Swami, we are also going to celebrate Fuldol over there [in Canada]. What is your message for [the devotees in Canada]?"

"Divyabhāv in everyone," replied Swamishri.

Regardless of the date, time, location, occasion or recipient, Swamishri invariably shares one consistent message: All swamis and devotees should be perceived as divine due to their direct association with Bhagwan Swaminarayan and this Satsang.

title: Every Day is Fuldol
text:
During the Pushpadolotsav festival, Swamishri showered flower petals upon the swamis and devotees, creating a truly memorable experience for all. After the festival, a discussion took place in Swamishri's car, during which a swami remarked, "Festivals were celebrated here in an extraordinary way."

Swamishri, with a voice filled with devotion, said, "We have Harikrishna Maharaj, so every day is Fuldol."

Swamishri's response reminds us that the attainment of Bhagwan and the Satpurush is the ultimate reason for celebration. Their presence is a blessing that leads to everlasting celebration.

title: Unaware of the Flavor
text:
After lunch, Swamishri returned to his room. The swamis wished to ask Swamishri a question, which the attendant swami asked on their behalf: "Swami, during breakfast this morning, an elderly swami fed you some chocolate. However, it turned out to be chili-flavored! Its label had fallen off, so even the swami [who fed it to you] was unaware. The swamis who tasted it said it was extremely spicy. Thus, for someone like you who does not eat spicy food, it must have been unbearably hot! Yet, [why] did you not mention anything?"

Swamishri smiled and said, "I was unaware of what I ate."

Swamishri has no preference for sweet, spicy, or flavorful foods, and his complete lack of awareness of their taste reflects his profound spiritual inclination to eat solely for the sustenance of the body.

title: A Compassionate Hand
text:
During the Bal Din evening assembly, the balaks were joyfully dancing to the kirtan "Jay Bole Jay Bole." As part of the performance, one balak was supposed to bring a lāddu in a bowl at the beginning of a line, offer it to Swamishri, and take it back once the line ended. Per the plan, the balak approached the stage and stood directly in front of Swamishri. However, he forgot his cue and simply stood there, unsure of what to do next. Seeing this, Swamishri rose from his seat, bent down, picked up the bowl, and handed it to the balak with great compassion.

In moments of uncertainty, Swamishri is always available to offer a compassionate hand, providing both timely guidance and comfort through his unwavering support and love.

title: Redefining Exhaustion
text:
During the evening assembly, a balak asked Swamishri, "When do you feel tired?"

Swamishri replied, "If you do not maintain unity, I feel tired."

Then, another question was asked, "Have you ever grown tired of turning the mālā?"

With firm conviction, Swamishri replied, "I could never get tired of it."

To Swamishri, exhaustion is not a matter of physical strain. He cherishes the spiritual ideal of unity so deeply that its absence is the only cause of his exhaustion. Furthermore, when it comes to devotion, it is inconceivable for him to experience any form of exhaustion.

title: An Eternal Servant
text:
Today, while in Swamishri's room, Uttamyogidas Swami asked Swamishri, "Whose guru are you?"

Swamishri's true inner feelings emerged, "I am a servant of all."

Whether alone in his room or before countless devotees, whether as a sadguru swami or the guru of thousands, regardless of time, place, or circumstance, Swamishri eternally considers himself a servant of all.

title: Keeping Swamishri Healthy
text:
Adarshjivandas Swami asked Swamishri a question, "Swami, today is March 25th. Twenty-six years ago, you underwent bypass surgery at Bombay Hospital. We take great care to ensure your heart and health remain strong, but what more can we do so that you remain in good health? We wish for your health and heart to always remain well so that you stay with us for at least another ten years."

With deep affection, Swamishri replied, "You have already done so much and continue to do so, but if, from within, you truly understand each other's greatness, bow [to one another], and maintain a divyabhāv… Although this body will eventually perish, the divine bliss we are receiving will remain forever."

Swamishri reveals the measures we can take to keep his heart and health strong. Moreover, we remain forever indebted for the divine bliss he bestows – a bliss that will last a lifetime.

title: A Revealing Moment
text:
At the conclusion of the Akshardham Bhumi Pujan assembly, as Swamishri was departing, an Australian architect was introduced to him. Viratswarup Swami informed Swamishri, "He will be the lead architect for the Akshardham project."

At that moment, Swamishri unexpectedly spoke in English, saying, "According to my wish, you [will] design." Swamishri typically does not speak in this manner, but in that revealing moment, he connected with the architect on a profound level. Deeply moved by Swamishri's words, the architect expressed his gratitude repeatedly, saying, "Thank you, thank you."

Through this brief exchange, Swamishri's heartfelt expression left a lasting impact, revealing the power of his guidance and vision. Swamishri inspires countless people in a variety of ways, with each connection being uniquely tailored to each individual.

title: A Practical Approach
text:
In the morning, Swamishri typically makes use of a long saffron towel while brushing his teeth. Today, upon noticing loose threads on the towel, he gestured for them to be cut. He had done the same two days earlier. When asked why he requested the threads to be cut, Swamishri gave a thoughtful response, saying, "If [the threads] are not cut, more will continue to unravel. And if they remain uncut, one is inclined to pull on them, causing even more to come loose. That is why they should be cut immediately."

Swamishri's attentiveness to even the smallest details reflects his deep sense of orderliness. His practical approach in having the loose threads cut maintains neatness and prevents unnecessary waste, demonstrating his mindful and efficient way of living.

title: A Thoughtful Consideration
text:
In the morning, Pujya Bhadresh Swami conveyed some good news to Swamishri. As a result, while having breakfast during the 25-minute drive back to his residence after puja, Swamishri remembered Bhadresh Swami and ate some shiro. A swami then suggested to Swamishri, "Today, Bhadresh Swami should also be given prasad, right?"

Swamishri said yes and added, "He should eat almonds."

"Should he not eat shiro?" asked the swamis.

Knowing that Bhadresh Swami has diabetes, Swamishri shook his head and advised against eating shiro. Swamishri's meticulous attention to detail in caring for swamis and devotees reflects his profound affection and compassion. His thoughtful consideration for their well-being, even in the smallest of matters, highlights his sincere concern for their health and happiness.

title: Maharaj-Swami
text:
During the afternoon sabha with the swamis, Adarshjivan Swami narrated a prasang from 2018. A kishore from Auckland brought a wristwatch to Swamishri, who sanctified it by having his pulse rate measured with it. After narrating the incident, the swamis asked, "Swami Bapa, your heart is beating; if someone were to listen to those heartbeats, what would they hear?"

Swamishri immediately replied, "Maharaj-Swami."

Every thought, action, and moment of Swamishri's life is centered around Maharaj and Swami. His mind is constantly absorbed in their remembrance, his words reflect their teachings, and his deeds embody their virtues. He is the very embodiment of Maharaj and Swami.

title: Unwavering Devotion
text:
After sabha, during the car ride back to the Mandir, Swamishri and the swamis were singing cheshtā together. As they approached Swamishri's residence, Uttamyogi Swami noticed kangaroos on the Mandir campus and, assuming Swamishri would like to see them, said, "[Look,] kangaroos have come!"

Hearing this, however, Swamishri expressed his displeasure with the suggestion as he was deeply immersed in singing cheshtā. In fact, Swamishri's eyes remained closed as he continued singing cheshtā. In this way, Swamishri did not allow the kangaroos to distract him from his devotion. No object, person, or animal can hinder Swamishri in his devotion. For Swamishri, Bhagwan is his only true desire. He never sets Bhagwan aside for any reason whatsoever.

title: Selfless and Compassionate
text:
After Swamishri's puja, during the morning question-and-answer session, Swamishri was asked, "Swami, [in 2017], when you were in Atlanta, because you drank Ensure [one morning], you did not feel like having breakfast. However, because the devotees were scheduled to offer their report [during your meal], you informed the attendant, 'I am having breakfast to please the devotees. Bring something that requires more chewing so that I eat less but spend enough time [for the devotees] to complete their reporting.' Swami, what else do you do to please us?"

Swamishri replied, "Everything I do is for the sake of pleasing [others]."

Swamishri's selflessness and dedication to his devotees are truly remarkable. His constant desire to please and serve others exemplifies his compassionate nature toward all.

title: Engrossed in Bhagwan
text:
After shangār ārti, Swamishri came to the front of the mandir and blessed the Gurukul staff. As he was coming down in the lift, Atmaswarup Swami remarked, "Swami, I've noticed that you become particularly happy in two instances – one, [when you are] before Bhagwan, and two, when you meet children, you invariably [bless them by] giving them a gentle tap [on the head], correct?"

"Yes," replied Swamishri. Continuing, Swamishri shared an extraordinary revelation, "I only remember Ghanshyam Maharaj, even when I am asleep."

Swamishri is always engrossed in Bhagwan. He constantly thinks of Bhagwan in all states and derives happiness in doing so.

title: Pure Intention
text:
After Swamishri performed the murti pratishthā of Tapomurti Shri Nilkanth Varni, Anandswarup Swami asked the following questions to Swamishri:

Question: "What is your impression of the murti of Nilkanth Varni?"
Swamishri: "Amazing! This murti is serene and charming."

Question: "What did you pray for before Nilkanth Varni?"
Swamishri: "[Now that] we have come here, may Satsang flourish throughout the entire nation."

Question: "What is the purpose of consecrating this murti?"
Swamishri: "This murti has been consecrated for the liberation of all souls."

All of Swamishri's actions, from a simple prayer to the decision to consecrate a magnificent 49-foot murti of Shri Nilkanth Varni, are driven by his desire to uplift others and support their spiritual progress. His intention of liberating countless souls lies at the core of every decision and action of his.

title: Leaving No One Behind
text:
Pleased with the devotion and sacrifices of the Satsang mandal in Australia, Swamishri remarked that he did not feel like leaving. Thus, the attendant swamis jokingly asked Swamishri, "Swami, today you said, 'I don't feel like leaving.' So if you wish to stay longer, let us know and we'll extend your ticket."

Swamishri declined and said, "[We should] continue our vicharan according to the original plan."

Once again, in the same light-hearted spirit, the attendant swamis asked, "If you'd like one of the attendant swamis to stay back for a few more days, please let us know. Whoever you choose will remain."

Swamishri replied, "No one should be left behind."

Swamishri's profound affection for each individual is evident in every action and gesture, reminding us all of his boundless compassion.

title: A Humble Act of Service
text:
In the evening, Vinaypriya Swami shared a memorable story about Anandvihari Swami, saying:

"Swami! He once told me that he had come here with you during his youth, in May 1987, when a shibir was held. Whenever you needed to use the restroom, he would go to the nearby farm to gather the material needed and would carefully prepare it for you to wash your hands with.

On one occasion, after you had finished your morning routine, he needed to do the same. In the same way he had prepared the material for you, you lovingly prepared it for him. And he fondly recalls that just two days later, in Bochasan, you performed dandavats to him."

Swamishri's life is a constant example of selfless service. He never misses an opportunity to serve others, staying humble and finding immense joy in doing so.

title: Consuming Satsang Content
text:
In the evening, during a question-and-answer session, Swamishri was asked about the benefits of reading and reflecting on prasangs of the pragat Satpurush. In his response, Swamishri made reference to and echoed the sentiments that Bhagwan Swaminarayan Himself has expressed in Gadhada I-37, in which He states, "The darshan of such a true Bhakta of Bhagwan is equivalent to the darshan of Bhagwan Himself."

Swamishri also elaborated on how one should consume Satsang content, saying, "One should fully immerse one's mind while performing darshan."

Let us remember the divine words of Bhagwan Swaminarayan as we continue to experience Moments with Mahant Swami with a renewed perspective. By fully immersing our minds in this opportunity, we can benefit greatly from the prasangs shared through this channel.

title: Behaving as the Ātmā
text:
Today, Swamishri performed his morning pujā in his residence. After completing pujā, around 7:30 AM, when the attendant swamis requested him to take his morning nap, he replied, "It is [too] early." The swamis explained that his schedule had been moved up due to today's murti pratishthā ceremony. Swamishri acquiesced and went to rest early.

This is a common occurrence. Whenever Swamishri is asked to take a nap earlier than his usual schedule, he usually resists or asks for an explanation. However, when his schedule is delayed and he ends up going to sleep later than planned, he never complains or even mentions it.

Swamishri remains unaffected by the discomforts of hunger, rest, or changes to his schedule. Rather than conforming to the body's desires, he behaves as the ātmā.

title: Timeless Memory
text:
During Swamishri's lunch, a swami recalled an incident from Yogiji Maharaj's time that took place in Bilimora in 1966, saying, "There, Yogi Bapa fed five large laddus each to Pramukh Swami Maharaj and you."

Hearing this, Swamishri became engrossed in the memory and added, "There was only ten percent chanāno lot (chickpea flour) in it...The laddu was flat at the base; not completely round, [but like a hemisphere]."

Although the incident occurred more than 53 years ago, Swamishri recalled it with remarkable clarity. His love, reverence, and vivid memory reveal the depth of his connection with his guru.

title: A Natural Joy
text:
In the evening, Swamishri participated in a discussion almost entirely in English. An attendant swami asked Swamishri, "What do you like doing the most in your free time?"

Swamishri softly replied, "Chintan (contemplation)."

The attendant swami then asked, "Chintan on which subject, Swami?"

Swamishri replied, "Related to God."

The attendant swami further inquired, "Is there a specific subject related to God?"

"Yes," replied Swamishri. "Dāsbhav (servanthood) and mahimā (glory of Bhagwan and His devotees)."

Swamishri's simple yet profound responses reflect how his mind remains constantly absorbed in Bhagwan. For him, contemplating on Bhagwan, dāsbhav, and mahimā is not a forced practice, but a natural joy he wholeheartedly chooses to engage in during his free time.

title: The Way of a True Swami
text:
When Swamishri woke up from his afternoon nap, Uttamyogi Swami asked, "Will you teach me the ways of a true swami?"

Swamishri replied, "We will teach everyone."

"What [specifically] will you teach?"

"To tolerate." Continuing, Swamishri said, "Nothing is achieved from simply tolerating, but one must endure for [the sake of] obeying the guru's commands."

"When can it be considered that the ways of a true swami have been perfected?"

"One does not realize it, but it is very difficult."

Swamishri, having personally endured many hardships throughout his life, speaks from experience when teaching the ways of a true swami. His words reveal that saintliness does not merely lie in tolerating; it stems from enduring for a higher purpose — obeying the guru's commands.

title: The Depth of Darshan
text:
Today, Swamishri was performing darshan of Thakorji through the live CCTV broadcast. As the murtis in the central shrine appeared on the screen, Swamishri pointed them out to Paramvivek Swami and remarked, "Main murti... main murti, [focus on the] lower portion…"

Through a gesture, Swamishri then indicated, "The payjama (lower garment) of the murtis in the central shrine should be exactly centered."

Swamishri's darshan reflected the same precision and attentiveness as when he is physically present in the mandir. Though viewing remotely, he remained fully aware and spiritually engaged—reminding us that true presence is measured by awareness, not just physical proximity.

title: Taking Responsibility and Leading Through Compassion
text:
During breakfast, Swamishri personally handed out prasad to everyone, carefully keeping track of who had received it and who had not. At the end of the meal, Swamishri noticed that Vinaypriya Swami had been missed and remarked, "You were left out."

The prasad that had been given to Swamishri to distribute was limited in quantity. Seeing this, some of the swamis pointed toward the swami responsible for bringing the prasad and said, "He brings less prasad."

Swamishri immediately responded, "No, I am the one who gives more [prasad]."

Without a moment's hesitation, Swamishri took the responsibility upon himself. Regardless of who was at fault, Swamishri did not blame anyone else. Instead, he embraced the situation with humility, setting an extraordinary example of leadership and compassion.

title: Reverence for Every Corner
text:
After the evening sabha, Swamishri returned to his residence in a golf cart. As he walked up a ramp near the elevator, Swamishri suddenly paused, took a few steps back, and pointed toward a corner, asking, "What is this?"

Vedagna Swami explained, "These are containers used to collect rainwater drainage."

Swamishri gently instructed, "Make sure the corner is kept clean and presentable."

Amidst countless responsibilities, Swamishri's attention to even the smallest details shows his reverence for every part of the mandir environment. His simple guidance reminds us that true devotion is not only shown through grand actions, but also through the quiet, thoughtful efforts to maintain cleanliness, order, and beauty in every corner of our surroundings.

title: Natural Affection
text:
After completing his puja, when Swamishri entered his residence, approximately 25 balaks were eagerly waiting nearby. Seeing the crowd of children, a few swamis playfully remarked, "So many magnets!"

Meanwhile, Swamishri, smiling warmly and with folded hands, gently greeted the children as he walked past them. When he reached the elevator, he paused, turned around, and asked the attendant swami, "Can I go back and gently tap each of their heads?"

Then, holding the attendant's hand, Swamishri walked back to the balaks. One by one, he lovingly placed his hand on each child's head. Though he had already met them, he felt compelled to personally bless each one. For the children, it was unforgettable; for Swamishri, it was natural.

Swamishri's connection with his devotees is such that he is always eager to interact with them personally. Through these interactions, he finds immense joy in simply meeting and blessing each devotee.

title: Respect for All
text:
In the afternoon, a stuffed kiwi bird, native to New Zealand, was brought and presented to Swamishri. Bhaktinidhi Swami pressed a button on it, and the bird began making sounds. Swamishri asked, "[Does it sound] like this when it speaks?"

Bhaktinidhi Swami nodded yes.

Then, the stuffed kiwi bird was placed on a cushion, positioned as if looking at Swamishri. Swamishri also looked at it, joined his hands, bowed his head, and offered his respects at its feet. Seeing this, the swamis asked, "Why did you bow down?"

Swamishri replied, "Why not? One should bow to all living beings."

The swamis countered, "Swami, this isn't a living being. It is merely a toy, a [lifeless] object."

Swamishri replied, "Even the non-living can come alive."

Swamishri's gesture reflects his deep reverence for all forms of life. He sees divinity not only in living beings but also in what they represent. Even a lifeless object is worthy of respect.

title: Offering Thaal Properly
text:
Shortly after Swamishri began his breakfast, a cake was brought to him. The swami who brought it asked, "Would you like to eat this?"

Narayanmuni Swami immediately turned to the swami and asked, "Has it been offered [to Thakorji]?"

The swami replied, "Yes."

Still curious, Narayanmuni Swami continued, "But how was it offered? [Yogi] Bapa had once said in London, 'How did you offer it without cutting it?'"

Swamishri responded with a smile, "It's only meant to be shown to Thakorji." Then, with a light-hearted laugh, he added, "Before Maharaj even has a chance to accept it, it's already taken away!"

Everyone burst into laughter. Yet beneath the humor lay a profound truth: offerings to Bhagwan should be made with sincerity, order, and devotion. It is the sincerity behind the act—not just its formality—that truly reaches Bhagwan.

title: Not at Thakorji's Expense
text:
The following day was Akshaya Tritiya, which marks the beginning of adorning metallic murtis with chandannā vāghā (sandalwood paste). Along with Shri Harikrishna Maharaj's murti, Shri Gunatitanand Swami's murti was to be adorned with chandannā vāghā for the first time.

The attendant swamis asked, "Because tomorrow marks the first day of chandannā vāghā, we were considering adorning Akshar-Purushottam Maharaj prior to puja. Swami, what is your wish?"

For Akshar-Purushottam Maharaj to grant darshan with chandannā vāghā during puja, they would need to be awakened earlier than usual.

Swamishri gently replied, "No; follow the daily routine. There is no need to wake Thakorji earlier than usual."

Swamishri's devotion to Shri Akshar-Purushottam Maharaj is evident in his careful consideration of their routine, always prioritizing their comfort above all else.

title: Exceptional Memory
text:
On the occasion of Ahmedabad Mandir's Pātotsav (Mandir opening anniversary celebration), Rushikesh Swami gathered details about the original pratishthā ceremony from Yogiji Maharaj's life biography and narrated the event during Swamishri's dinner.

During the narration, Swamishri casually remarked, "At that time, [Gulzarilal] Nanda Saheb had worn his cap backwards. His wife pointed it out [through someone], and only then did he correct it."

More than six decades after the pratishthā ceremony, Swamishri recalled not only the key moments from the event but also the smallest, seemingly insignificant details.

title: Guidance in Every Detail
text:
Today, the metallic murtis of Shri Akshar-Purushottam Maharaj, which would later be consecrated in the Mandir, were placed behind Swamishri during his pujā. Swamishri turned toward the murtis after completing his pujā and lovingly performed ārti. Then, Nirmalyogi Swami, who had painted the eyes of both murtis, asked, "Swami, [with respect to the murtis' eyes], is there anything that needs improvement?"

From his seat, Swamishri carefully looked up at the murtis and suggested, "Make the eyes a bit more 'white.'"

He then stood up, pointed to the specific area, and added, "Make them a little 'white'; not too much."

Swamishri lovingly offers thoughtful guidance with care and precision, ensuring everything is carried out with excellence and devotion.

title: Calm and Composed
text:
It was 27 years ago today that Swamishri underwent open-heart bypass surgery. In the morning, reflecting on this event, the swamis asked Swamishri several questions related to his experience.

Question: "Before and after your operation, the doctors observed that your facial expressions showed a sense of certainty, with no sign of worry. You appeared remarkably calm and confident. Facing a major heart illness typically leaves a person feeling anxious and discouraged. How were you able to remain so composed?"

Swamishri: "Because I had Bhagwan's āshro (refuge and protection), I remained at peace."

Swamishri remains calm in all situations. His unwavering faith and firm refuge in Bhagwan reveal the key to maintaining peace and composure in every circumstance.

title: Do It for Rajipo
text:
Today, as Swamishri was about to go to sleep, a discussion arose about fasting.

Shrutipriya Swami recalled, "Swami, this happened when I had just joined your seva. A yuvak from overseas wrote a letter. He worked a night shift and mentioned, 'Swami, I have to stay awake all night for my job. If Ekadashi falls the next day, I struggle to observe it. According to the Shikshapatri, we are not supposed to sleep during the day on Ekadashi. But for me, night is day and day is night. So, should I sleep during the day on Ekadashi, or stay awake?'"

Shrutipriya Swami continued, "Swami, you gave him a firm reply: 'If you truly want to earn rajipo, then you will have to do it.'"

Swamishri's guidance is unwavering when it comes to niyam-dharma. Even in challenging circumstances, earning Bhagwan's happiness requires wholehearted effort—without compromise.

title: Unity Begins at Home
text:
Kevin, a distinguished representative at the United Nations, came to meet Swamishri. Seeking guidance, he asked Swamishri, "How can we foster international unity?"

Swamishri responded with a simple yet practical solution, "Unity starts with the family. Then only will we reach the level of international unity."

Swamishri emphasized that global harmony must be rooted in the strength and unity of our closest relationships.

title: Making Sincere Efforts
text:
In the afternoon, Atmaswarup Swami shared an inspiring update: "Swami, there is a devotee from Ahmedabad, Bipinbhai Soni, a retired judge. During this [COVID-19] lockdown, at the age of 70, he has memorized the entire Sahajanand Nāmāvali and five Vachanamruts!"

Hearing this, Swamishri became pleased and said, "No one [usually] does mukhpāth at the age of 70. One's memory begins to decline at 45. And by 60, it is [almost] completely gone. But at 70, to memorize the Nāmāvali and Vachanamruts—that is incredible!"

Atmaswarup Swami added, "And now he has also resolved to take the Satsang exams."

With genuine joy, Swamishri responded, "May all of your wishes be fulfilled."

Swamishri deeply values those who strive to internalize the principles of Satsang, offering his wholehearted encouragement regardless of age.

title: A Promise Is a Promise
text:
Today, Swamishri was informed that tomorrow, Sunday, 2,100 balaks and balikas would gather in Ahmedabad to offer a special pledge. They would be promising Swamishri that during their summer break, they would complete the full memorization of the Satsang Diksha scripture, and, in doing so, commit to doing their part in fulfilling Swamishri's goal of having 10,000 balaks and balikas do the same.

Hearing this, Swamishri was overjoyed and offered his blessings, saying, "All of you have given this promise. A promise is a promise. Now do as you have promised. Jay Swaminarayan."

Through his words and blessings, Swamishri lovingly encouraged all to embrace mukhpāth and take their commitment to Satsang to heart.

title: Satpurush Is Always With You
text:
During a special virtual sabha with youth from North America, Swamishri read a letter he had written:

Blessings
Surat
April 28, 2025

To: BAPS North America Satsang Mandal,
Jay Shri Swaminarayan from Sadhu Keshavjivandas,

All of you have worked hard and pushed forward with great enthusiasm, which cannot be captured in words. Congratulations! Seeing your efforts in mukhpāth, Yogi Bapa would have been extremely pleased and given many dhabbās (pats on the back). To ensure you do not forget what you have done, keep up with regular 'revision.' You will truly enjoy reflecting on and contemplating what you have memorized.

"Go for it to benefit more and more. And you will feel that the Satpurush is always with you."

title: True Praise, True Unity
text:
Vishwaswarup Swami spoke of one swami's virtues. Hearing this, Swamishri smiled and remarked, "He is very dynamic."

Then, addressing all the swamis, Swamishri said, "All of you are champions. You should wholeheartedly sing each other's praises and truly believe them from within. Many may praise others outwardly, but internally think, 'All of this is good and well, but he is deficient in some manner.' That mindset is not appropriate. If you discard [such thoughts] and sing the praises of one another, then you will progress." Swamishri concluded, "Rājipo lies in doing everything with samp (unity)."

Swamishri's words remind us that true unity is not just spoken, it must be felt. Real praise comes not from lips alone, but from a heart free of comparison, ego, and doubt.

title: Akshar
text:
It was 27 years ago today that Swamishri underwent open heart bypass surgery. Reflecting on this event, the swamis asked various questions to Swamishri:

Question: "Dr. Bhattacharya, who performed your bypass surgery, once said, 'While performing the surgery, I experienced [Swamishri's] divinity.' Why does everyone who comes into contact with you experience divinity?"

Swamishri: "Because there is a connection with the divine."

Question: "He also said, 'When I operated on him, I felt that he was meant to be a leader.' Did you ever feel that you were going to become a guru?"

Swamishri smiled and said, "No; even now I do not feel that way."

Then Adarshjivan Swami asked, "Who are you?"

"Akshar," replied Swamishri.

Swamishri's true identity is Akshar, eternally linked to and a humble servant of Bhagwan Swaminarayan.

title: Never Compromising
text:
It was 27 years ago today that Swamishri underwent open heart bypass surgery. Reflecting on this event, the swamis asked Swamishri, "A few days after your bypass surgery, it was Hari Jayanti (a day when all satsangis observe a waterless fast). You were prepared to observe the full fast without water. However, when Pramukh Swami Maharaj advised against it, you only had a small amount of orange juice, just enough to take your medicine. In such a fragile state, how did you still maintain such a strong desire to perform austerities?"

Swamishri replied, "It is Bhagwan's command. There is never any compromise in that."

Swamishri demonstrates his unwavering commitment to following every command of Bhagwan. Even in moments of physical fragility, he maintains a firm resolve to perform austerities.

title: Motivation for Mukhpath
text:
A spiritually uplifting morning unfolded across North America as Swamishri joined a special virtual mukhpāth motivation sabhā. Swamis shared mukhpāth prasangs from Yogiji Maharaj's life, and led an interactive goshthi with Swamishri.

Swamishri listened attentively as devotees shared their struggles. In a powerful gesture, he repeatedly tore a piece of paper, symbolizing his resolve to help remove their inner obstacles. Just as Yogiji Maharaj often proctored mukhpāth, Swamishri did so live.

He gave a virtual air hug that reached into every home, then placed his hands on the names and photos of nearly 1,300 devotees who had memorized all 500 quotes. He offered a written assurance: "For those that do mukhpāth, the Satpurush is always there to help. Do not doubt that."

title: Becoming His Best Friend
text:
In the morning, Swamishri arrived in the pradakshina area to perform darshan of the Guru Paramparā. As he approached Yogiji Maharaj's murti, a young child standing nearby asked a heartfelt question, "Swami! You are my best friend, but how can I become your best friend?"

Swamishri smiled affectionately and replied, "Yes, follow niyams."

In that quiet moment, Swamishri showed that true friendship with the Satpurush isn't based on words alone, but on living a disciplined and sincere life. When we follow our niyams with love, we naturally grow closer to him.

title: Constant Care
text:
In the morning, Swamishri arrived in the pradakshina area to perform darshan of the Guru Paramparā. As he approached Yogiji Maharaj's murti, a young child standing nearby asked a heartfelt question, "Swami! You are my best friend, but how can I become your best friend?"

Swamishri smiled affectionately and replied, "Yes, follow niyams."

In that quiet moment, Swamishri showed that true friendship with the Satpurush isn't based on words alone, but on living a disciplined and sincere life. When we follow our niyams with love, we naturally grow closer to him.

title: Eternal Bliss
text:
It was 27 years ago today that Swamishri underwent open heart bypass surgery. Reflecting on this, the swamis asked, "Swami, after recovering in Mumbai, you went to Ahmedabad for Pramukh Swami Maharaj's darshan. He was extremely pleased upon seeing you. He offered you a jasmine garland, gave you mango as prasād, and said, 'The operation went well, and your recovery has been excellent. Now you have attained eternal bliss. Your health will remain good. There is peace now.' Here, what did he mean by 'eternal bliss'?"

Swamishri gently replied, "From a worldly perspective, the surgery was successful, so there would be no further problems."

Truly, even after 27 years, Swamishri's heart remains healthy, and he has faced no hardship. In this manner, Swamishri gave everyone a reassuring update on his heart.

title: Absorbed in Pramukh Swami
text:
Before Swamishri's lunch, during a question-and-answer session, Anandswarup Swami asked, "What does it mean to attach [one's self] to the murti?"

Swamishri replied, "To become absorbed in (one with) the murti."

Then, Adarshjivan Swami shared, "In 2017, some youths asked you, 'What did you like most about [the murti of] Pramukh Swami?' You replied, 'When Swami Bapa would walk, both of his heels would rub against the ground, causing the soles to wear down.'"

Adarshjivan Swami added, "Truly, only one who has become completely immersed in Pramukh Swami Maharaj can notice such subtle details."

Then, Swamishri was asked, "How did you notice this?"

Swamishri simply said, "[I was fully] absorbed in Pramukh Swami."

title: Prayer in Action
text:
Today, Swamishri was informed about the 7.7-magnitude earthquake that struck Myanmar. After seeing the destruction and hearing about the loss of life, he felt deep sorrow. He spoke with devotees in the affected area, gave blessings for strength, and prayed there would be no further aftershocks. Afterward, Swamishri looked concerned. Shrutipriya Swami suggested, "We could organize a special dhun tomorrow morning after pujā."

However, Swamishri immediately replied, "[In addition to tomorrow], let us do dhun right now."

The murti of Shri Akshar-Purushottam Maharaj was placed before Swamishri, who began the dhun with his eyes closed. Later, he called the swamis in the region to discuss how BAPS could assist, and arrangements were made to provide food and shelter to those affected.

title: Sweet Memories
text:
Today marked the anniversary of Yogi Bapa's departure to Akshardham. Accordingly, a special question-and-answer session was held.

Question: "Swami, which moment with Yogi Bapa stands out as the most special memory for you?"
Swamishri: "When Yogi Bapa would be asleep and I would wake him up; at that time, he would have to be helped up and we would naturally embrace. This is a special memory."

Question: "As a youth, how many times did Yogi Bapa apply the tilak-chandlo on your forehead?"
Swamishri: "About 50 times." He added, "When I went to Yogi Bapa, I would sometimes wipe it off. Yogi Bapa would then reapply it, pressing firmly, which I greatly enjoyed."

title: The Present Form of Yogiji Maharaj
text:
During the question-and-answer session on the anniversary of Yogiji Maharaj's physical departure to Akshardham, Swamishri was asked, "Many people today have not had the darshan of Yogi Bapa. So, how can they have Yogi Bapa's darshan nowadays?"

Swamishri replied, "[Simply] realize what all of you have already understood."

Adarshjivan Swami inquired further, "If we understand through the words of the guru, that is considered the best. So please explain it to us yourself."

Swamishri succinctly replied, "Yogi Bapa and I are one."

Just as Shastriji Maharaj had once said, "I am Yogi and Yogi is me," Swamishri revealed that he is the present form of Yogiji Maharaj. Having the darshan of Swamishri is equivalent to having the darshan of Yogiji Maharaj himself.

title: The Epitome of Humility
text:
During the question-and-answer session on the anniversary of Yogiji Maharaj's physical departure to Akshardham, a series of questions were asked to Swamishri.

Swamishri was asked, "What quality of Yogi Bapa did you admire the most?"

Swamishri replied, "His patience. No one could endure as much as he did. He tolerated beyond limits."

Another followed, "You had the association of both Yogi Bapa and Pramukh Swami Maharaj. What similarities did you observe?"

Swamishri answered, "Both had extreme humility and a profound spirit of service. They would immediately take up any opportunity to serve."

The final question was, "Yogi Bapa once told a youth, 'Mahant Swami is me.' When you hear such praise, do you feel special?"

Swamishri shook his head, attempted to bow down, and humbly said, "I have never felt like I am anything special."

title: Laabh Through Test
text:
During the question-and-answer session on the anniversary of Yogiji Maharaj's physical departure to Akshardham, a series of questions were asked to Swamishri.

Question: "In addition to giving you immense lābh, Yogi Bapa tested you a lot. What was your mindset [when he would test you]?"

Swamishri: "He was the manifest form of Shriji Maharaj. Thus, just as one would stand before Maharaj and take his lābh [be tested], I would take his lābh. If I were not at fault, I would think that he was giving me a memory through this lābh."

Swamishri's response reveals the depth of his realization—seeing Yogi Bapa not just as a guru, but as the manifest form of Shriji Maharaj himself. With this understanding, even difficult moments became divine opportunities for lābh.

title: Swamishri's Best Friend
text:
In the evening, during the Bal Din sabha, the balaks played a special game called 'Best Friend' with Swamishri. In this interactive game, the children asked Swamishri fun and heartfelt questions, and he replied by writing down his answers.

Finally, the last question was asked, "Who is your best friend?"

Swamishri wrote, "Everyone who follows niyam-dharma is my best friend."

For Swamishri, true friendship isn't based on age, background, or any external trait. It is rooted in how sincerely we live by the values of satsang. To follow niyam-dharma is to earn a special place in the heart of the Satpurush.

title: Protecting an Ant
text:
When Swamishri entered the bathroom in the morning, there was an ant inside the sink basin. He needed to gargle, so Uttamyogi Swami filled a bowl with water and gave it to him. Swamishri gargled carefully so the ant would remain unharmed. After finishing, he handed the bowl to Uttamyogi Swami, who poured the remaining water over the ant and washed it down the drain. Seeing this, Swamishri felt saddened.

Within moments, the ant crawled out of the drain, trying to save itself. Uttamyogi Swami extended his finger, let the ant climb on, and placed it in a safe spot. Only then did Swamishri feel satisfied.

Then, Swamishri said, "If the poor ant is trying to survive, and we just wash it away like this, then we shouldn't do such things."

Swamishri's compassion is limitless. Even a tiny ant is protected by him.

title: Care in Every Detail
text:
After finishing his dinner, Swamishri received a routine medical check-up from the doctors, including Dr. K.N. Patel. Following the check-up, Swamishri blessed him and offered him prasād, placed in a paper bag. Seeing the bag, Swamishri asked, "Everything has been placed in the bag. It's not a bag that will tear easily, is it?" He checked it himself to ensure it was sturdy.

As Dr. K.N. Patel bowed and turned to leave, Swamishri gently called out, "Your shirt has become untucked. Be sure to tuck it back in."

Hearing this, Dr. K.N. Patel was filled with joy and said, "Swamishri looks after us so much! He has so much affection for us!"

Swamishri's love is expressed not only through blessings but also in the smallest acts of care. We are never out of his sight or heart.

title: Pramukh Swami Maharaj's Example
text:
On the occasion of Pramukh Varni Din, during the evening sabhā, the swamis asked Swamishri, "Swamibapa dedicated his entire life to fulfilling the words of his guru. What inspiration should we take from Pramukh Varni Din?"

Swamishri replied, "That's it, just like him. Note all of the hardships and work he did. Don't keep any doubts. Everything will fall into place. Doubts may come, but if you keep your vision on Swami, everything will be fine."

He continued, "His love for Shastriji Maharaj was so deep that everything became possible through that alone. Even a million rupees a month wouldn't be enough to endure what he did. If we live with those same qualities, then Akshardham is right here. There won't be a need to come back again."

title: The Secret to a Strong Heart
text:
It was 27 years ago today that Swamishri underwent open-heart bypass surgery. Reflecting on this, the swamis asked, "Once in London, you stated, 'My heart is the strongest part of my body.' And Dr. Tejas remarked, 'Your heart won't have any issues until you're at least 100.' But we want to make your heart even stronger. What should we do?"

Swamishri gently replied, "You are already doing everything."

The same question was asked several times in different ways, and each time, Swamishri gave the same response. Finally, when asked a fourth time, Swamishri made a subtle hand gesture as if turning a mālā and softly replied, "Bhajan."

Through this simple response, Swamishri revealed that offering devotion sincerely nourishes our own hearts and upholds the very path that sustains his.

title: The Rhythm of His Life
text:
From Dubai, Swamishri arrived at Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel International Airport in Ahmedabad at 10:55 PM IST. He proceeded directly to Anand by car, a drive of about one and a half hours.

Despite the tiring journey and the late hour, Swamishri asked an attendant swami for a mālā and quietly began turning it. With steady focus, he remained engrossed in bhajan throughout the entire car drive, continuing until he reached Madhubhan Resort at 12:45 AM. Within twenty minutes, Swamishri retired for the night at 1:05 AM.

Even after a long day of travel, Swamishri stayed fully absorbed in devotion. For him, bhajan is not something he does only when time permits or when convenient; it is the natural rhythm of his life.

title: A Bitter Almond
text:
Swamishri began his lunch by eating five to six blanched almonds. On this day, one of the almonds happened to be bitter, yet Swamishri refused to set it aside. Only after several requests from the attendant swamis did Swamishri finally remove it. Swamishri then remarked, "In four years [since becoming guru], this is the first time a bitter almond has come."

Vinaypriya Swami recalled, "Swami, when you were a sadguru sant, bitter almonds would sometimes be served, and you would eat them."

Swamishri smirked and said, "Once, four bitter almonds came one after another." Through his expression, he conveyed, "We should eat them."

Swamishri does not seek contentment from food or any other source. He accepts whatever is served without complaint because he is innately fulfilled through his connection with Bhagwan.

title: Entry Requirements
text:
During the evening sabhā, a member of the Akshardham security team asked, "Swami, what kind of pass will be required to go to the Akshardham above?"

Swamishri replied, "Samp (unity) and divyabhāv (seeing divinity in all)!"

However significant one's spiritual accomplishments may be, Swamishri's simple yet profound message reminds us that entry into Akshardham requires strengthening our relationships with others through both samp and divyabhāv.

title: His True Name
text:
After the evening ārti, all of the attendant swamis stood before Swamishri as Uttamyogi Swami gently asked him to identify each one. To everyone's surprise and delight, Swamishri accurately said each of their names.

At the end, Gurumanan Swami asked with a smile, "And what is your name, Swami?"

Without hesitation, Swamishri replied, "Akshar."

Through this one-word answer, Swamishri revealed his true identity: Aksharbrahma, the ideal devotee and eternal servant of Purna Purushottam Bhagwan Swaminarayan. Recognizing this truth liberates one from the bondage of māyā.

title: With The Snap of His Fingers
text:
As part of his evening routine, Swamishri engaged in his walking exercise and responded to letters. As he was finishing his snack, a small portion remained in the bowl because Swamishri was unable to lift it into the spoon. As he persistently tried to scoop it up, an attendant swami offered, "Swami, give it [to us]. We will instantly scoop it up."

Swamishri smirked and replied, "This can't be done [by me]," and while snapping his fingers, added, "but I can instantly grant moksha."

Once, Bhagwatcharan Swami playfully asked Pramukh Swami Maharaj how he could grant kalyān if he could not even remember his name. In response, Pramukh Swami Maharaj snapped his fingers and said, "I can instantly grant kalyān." Likewise, Swamishri echoed his guru. Though he may display human-like characteristics, he is undoubtedly divine.

title: The Servant of Devotees
text:
In the evening, volunteers from Surat were enjoying Swamishri's darshan during his dinner. For 45 minutes, they quietly soaked in the moment, immersed in devotion and gratitude.

As Swamishri completed his meal, Shrijinandan Swami offered a heartfelt prayer on behalf of the volunteers, "Swami, please help us attain ekāntik dharma."

Hearing this, Swamishri gently folded his hands, did darshan of all the devotees with respect, and humbly said, "I am the dās (servant) of all of you."

Though he is the guru, Swamishri considers himself a das of his devotees. Rather than seeking honor, he remains humble and serves them with the utmost respect.

title: Compassion for an Ant
text:
In the morning, during Swamishri's bath, an attendant swami accidentally stepped on a makodo (large ant). Seeing this, Swamishri immediately remarked, "On Bhim Ekadashi, such a good day and..."

"…And it has gone to [Akshar]dhām!" added another attendant swami.

Swamishri gently corrected him, "No, it hasn't gone to dhām. Its back has been broken. Place it somewhere safe and it will regain its form by itself."

Following his guidance, the attendant swami gently lifted the makodo using a tissue, placed it inside his pāgh, and covered it to ensure warmth and protection.

Later that afternoon, Swamishri noticed a makodo crawling across the carpet and inquired about its well-being. When the attendant checked the pāgh, it was no longer there—it had regained its form and strength.

For Swamishri, no life is insignificant, and every creature deserves care and respect.

title: Natural Inclination
text:
After completing his pujā, Swamishri folded his hands and bowed to all of the swamis present. After performing ārti, the curtains closed momentarily. When the curtains reopened, Swamishri once again bowed to the swamis, even though he had already done so after completing his puja.

Noticing this, Adarshjivan Swami remarked, "Today, you did something new: you bowed to the swamis a second time!"

Swamishri humbly replied, "No matter how often we bow, it is never enough."

Swamishri's repeated gesture reveals his natural inclination to offer respect to others. Bowing is not just an act for him; it reflects his humility and mahimā for others.

title: Everyone, Be Free
text:
During Swamishri's lunch, chocolate was distributed to the children present. At Swamishri's request, the children unwrapped the chocolates and ate the prasād. Unsure of what to do with the wrappers, they instinctively slipped them into their pockets.

After some time, Swamishri requested, "Take the wrappers from them." Then, with gentle care, he told the children, "Everyone, be free [from the burden of carrying and disposing of the wrappers]."

Swamishri's actions reveal his desire to take away any unnecessary burdens we may be carrying, whether material in nature or far heavier, such as grief or misery. In doing so, he enables us to live freely, without the weight of excess baggage.

title: Our Purpose
text:
During the evening goshthi, Uttamyogi Swami asked Swamishri, "What have we come to do?"

While replying, Swamishri gently gestured with his hand, mimicking the turning of a rosary, and said, "To worship Bhagwan."

"From what [endeavor] is the most krupā (grace and blessings) earned, Swami?"

"By spreading [the Akshar-Purushottam] faith."

After the completion of Delhi Akshardham, when Pramukh Swami Maharaj was asked, "What is your next project?" he replied, "To worship Bhagwan and inspire others to worship Bhagwan," highlighting that this was, and always would be, his lifelong mission. Likewise, Swamishri echoed these sentiments by urging us to stay absorbed in bhajan and to inspire others to do the same, for that is ultimately the purpose of our life.

title: Pragat Prapti
text:
In the morning, while Swamishri was delivering a discourse on Vachanamrut Gadhada II-61, he emphasized: "We must have firm faith in Maharaj–Swami and the Satpurush. Gunatitanand Swami, Bhagatji Maharaj, Shastriji Maharaj, Yogi Bapa, and Pramukh Swami Maharaj—we must have unwavering faith in all of them. These forms have not left (they remain present today). We may not be able to see them, but they are here. Every day, we should say 'Jay' with the awareness that they are present."

Swamishri reminds us that true prapti lies not in what is visible, but in recognizing the eternal presence of Bhagwan and the pragat Satpurush through unwavering faith.

title: The Bliss of Akshardham
text:
After dinner, while getting up from his seat, Swamishri said, "If no one ever found faults in others, how enjoyable would [life] be?"

Then, Swamishri himself remarked, "Akshardham!"

Through this casual comment, Swamishri revealed that Akshardham is not an experience limited to the afterlife. It is a divine state that can be felt here and now. By eliminating fault-finding and choosing to see the good in others, we experience the bliss of Akshardham.

As Purushottam Bolyā Prite Chapter 3 describes, "In Mankuva, Shri Hari said, 'The sādhus and devotees are the form of Akshardhām. If one develops abhav (dislike) for them, then one who takes abhav is not able to enter Akshardhām. The fault of taking abhav is the greatest fault of all.'"

The less fault we find in others, the closer we draw to Bhagwan and His eternal bliss.

title: No Excuses for Exercise
text:
Swamishri asked the attendant swamis about their exercise routines. Offering guidance, he remarked, "Some [only] exercise once every fifteen days… They customize everything according to their convenience. But there is no use in that..."

Uttamyogi Swami commented, "Swami, most people take liberties when it comes to exercise."

Swamishri replied firmly, "We should increase the amount of exercise we get. No 'breaks.' It should be done now. [If not now,] then when?" With a gesture, he added, "If we don't exercise, we will become helpless." He continued, "Prānāyam and āsans clear the nādis, and walking builds muscle strength."

Swamishri concluded, "We must do justice to all three: mind, body, and soul." Speaking of himself, he added, "I am tired 24 hours a day. Regardless, I do the exercises the physiotherapist requires—forcefully, but I do them."

title: Refuge in Bhagwan
text:
During a question-and-answer session, Adarshjivan Swami asked, "Swami, 27 years ago you underwent open-heart surgery at Bombay Hospital. The doctors who examined you before and after all spoke of the same shared experience: 'Every time we saw Mahant Swami, his face radiated complete serenity. There was no trace of fear, worry, or doubt.' Most people are shaken by serious illness, and heart disease usually breaks a person mentally. How did you remain so composed?"

"Refuge in Bhagwan," replied Swamishri.

"Swami, in illness, we struggle to keep that awareness. Why is it so difficult for us?"

"Ignorance."

Through his short response, "Refuge in Bhagwan," Swamishri revealed the essence of true spiritual resilience. His unshakable composure stemmed not from personal strength alone, but from complete reliance on Bhagwan.

title: Strength Beyond Age
text:
During the evening cycling session, an experienced local physiotherapist named Nathaniel came to observe Swamishri. After watching the full routine, including cycling and various exercises, he was genuinely impressed by Swamishri's discipline and strength.
