After the session, Swamishri instructed, "Give him some orange juice," and thoughtfully added, "Make sure it's not sour." Touched by this care, Nathaniel offered his respects with folded hands. Before he left, Swamishri gave him chocolate as prasad. Nathaniel was visibly moved, reluctant to leave, and later messaged that it was a night he would never forget.

Reflecting on Swamishri's fitness, Nathaniel remarked how remarkable it was for someone his age to maintain such a routine, especially when even his own grandfather avoids exercise post-surgery. In truth, what powers Swamishri's routine is not just physical stamina but deep inner strength.

title: His First Response
text:
This afternoon, an Air India flight traveling from Ahmedabad to London was involved in a devastating accident, resulting in the heartbreaking loss of many lives and leaving many others injured. During the evening assembly, Swamishri joined the swamis and devotees in dhun, offering heartfelt collective prayers.

Swamishri said, "We are deeply saddened to learn about the plane crash that occurred this afternoon, June 12, 2025, in Ahmedabad. On this tragic occasion, we pray for all those affected. May Bhagwan grant peace to the souls of those who passed away. May their loved ones find the strength to bear this grief. We also pray for the speedy recovery of those who were injured."

In moments of tragedy, Swamishri's first response is always prayer, an expression of his constant care for all.

title: An Expression of Affection
text:
After dinner, Shuddhmuni Swami's name came up in conversation. He is a young swami who received dikshā in 2018.

The attendant swamis gently asked, "Swami, will you be able to remember his name?"

Swamishri smiled, nodded, and clearly said, "Shuddhmuni."

Later, as he got up to go to the bathroom, he softly repeated, "Shuddhmuni." When he entered the room for cheshta, he mentioned his name again, once more on his way to the bathroom, and finally a fifth time as he prepared to sleep.

Over the next two days, although Swamishri kept forgetting his name, he continued trying to recall it and was determined to remember it.

Despite there being over 1,200 swamis in the BAPS Sanstha today, Swamishri's repeated efforts to remember one swami's name reflect the deep respect he holds for every swami and devotee.

title: Meaningful Devotion
text:
Swamishri was seated in his wheelchair, ready to sanctify the ghar mandir murtis that would be placed in devotees' homes. As the process began, he gently instructed Uttamyogi Swami, "Move the wheelchair slowly; not too fast."

Sanctifying murtis is something Swamishri does almost daily. For many, such repetition could become routine. But with Swamishri, there is never anything mechanical. His reverence only deepens with time.

Even when simply touching the feet of the murtis, Swamishri does so with calm, heartfelt devotion. The fact that he feels the wheelchair is moving too quickly shows how fully immersed he is in each moment.

Swamishri's every action is a reminder that true devotion is never rushed, never routine. It is filled with peace, presence, and love.

title: Sharp Memory
text:
During the exercise session after his walk, Swamishri listens to Shastriji Maharaj's jivan charitra. Today, however, before Uttamyogi Swami could start the recording, Swamishri requested, "Start from Kishorbhai."

At first, Uttamyogi Swami was unsure what Swamishri meant. Then someone clarified, "Do you mean the incident where Shastriji Maharaj met Kishorbhai while leaving Vadtal?"

When they asked if that was the incident he wanted to hear again, Swamishri agreed.

What amazed everyone was that Swamishri had heard this same incident just the day before—and yet he remembered both the content and the devotee's name with complete clarity.

Even at his age, Swamishri's memory remains remarkably sharp, so much so that it humbles even the young.

title: Bhajan, No Matter What
text:
After Swamishri had given blessings and the curtains were drawn, the sadguru swamis came forward to bow at his feet. When Dr. Swami stepped forward, his attendants shared a memorable incident, "Swami Bapa, when we were in Sarangpur, there was a sabha conducted entirely in Sanskrit. It lasted for two hours. After we returned to the room, we asked Dr. Swami, 'Swami, did you understand anything?' Dr. Swami replied, 'I didn't understand a single word.' Then we asked, 'So why did you sit there the whole time?' He replied, '[Because I was able to do my] bhajan peacefully.'"

Hearing this, Swamishri was deeply pleased. With firm conviction, he said, "That is exactly what we must do."

No matter the circumstance, Swamishri always emphasizes staying connected and anchored in the remembrance of Bhagwan.

title: Content with Lābh
text:
In the evening, the topic of taking the Satpurush's lābh came up. The attendant swamis asked Swamishri, "You didn't get the same type of lābh from Pramukh Swami Maharaj like you received from Yogiji Maharaj, because Pramukh Swami Maharaj used to maintain a lot of maryādā with you. For example, if you tried to press his feet, he would pull them away. Once, when he was blessing all the swamis by placing his hand on their heads, you had joined the line. But when you reached him, he didn't place his hand on your head. Didn't you feel that you didn't get the lābh?"

Swamishri replied, "No, no, it is all Bhagwan's will." Then he shared a beautiful insight, "The lābh we do receive, that itself is a great [blessing]. If we start comparing, thinking, 'He got more, I got less,' then even the lābh we did receive will lose its joy."

Swamishri revealed that spiritual joy is not found in quantity, but in contentment.

title: Controlling the Mind
text:
After completing cheshta, Swamishri listens to Pramukh Swami Maharaj's Jivan Charitra as part of his nightly routine.

Today was ekadashi, and it had grown late. Swamishri was also feeling physically weak. Out of concern, the attendant swamis gently suggested, "Swami, please listen to the jivan charitra while resting in bed."

But Swamishri firmly declined, saying, "I do not trust the mind (I might fall asleep)."

Even in a moment of physical fatigue, Swamishri displayed vigilance and discipline over his inner self. He showed that true niyam-dharma requires mistrusting the mind's tendencies and prioritizing spiritual focus above personal comfort.

title: Detached from the World
text:
Swamishri was asked, "Swami Bapa, you never ask about what is going on in the world. Don't you ever feel curious about current events or the latest news?"

Swamishri replied, "No, whatever is meant to happen will happen."

He then added, "Bhagwan's glory is so vast that all of this is like just a single drop. There are 14 realms in the entire brahmānd, and even within just this Earth, there are countless wonders. Compared to that, these [worldly news] are nothing. Bhagwan's greatness is so immense that I feel no desire to know any of it."

Swamishri concluded, "Bhagwan created all of this, and Bhagwan will ultimately absorb it all."

In every moment of his life, Swamishri remains entirely immersed in Bhagwan. Thus, he remains truly detached from the fleeting distractions of the material world.

title: All Are Muktas
text:
During noon, Ghanshyambhai Rampariya and his two young sons, Swayam and Savya, were standing in the dining hall. Swayam curiously asked Swamishri, "When others do your darshan, they feel so joyful. But when you see them doing your darshan, what do you feel? What thoughts come to [your mind]?"

Without a pause, Swamishri replied, "Mukta! All are muktas."

Swamishri naturally sees every devotee as a mukta (liberated soul), full of purity, and divine. Despite receiving so much reverence, Swamishri carries no trace of ego. His heart remains rooted in humility, always focused on glorifying others rather than himself.

title: Remembering the Details
text:
During his walk, Swamishri was asked for the date. He responded, "5-5-25," accurately.

Then, revealing how he knew, Swamishri said, "It's written on the mirror in the bathroom." Smiling, he added, "The five is [written] artistically," and demonstrated the stylized shape with a hand gesture.

Since Uttamyogi Swami had written the date, he clarified to Swamishri, "The stomach [of the five] is big."

Swamishri gently corrected him, "Not the stomach—the leg."

When Uttamyogi Swami looked again in the mirror, he realized Swamishri was right. The leg of the five had indeed been extended.

Swamishri's attention to even a small detail shows how deeply he values every act of devotion. If he remembers a handwritten digit, he surely remembers the devotees' devotion and love behind it.

title: Beyond the Clock
text:
After lunch, Uttamyogi Swami informed Swamishri, "Gnaneshwar Swami, Narayanmuni Swami, and Atmatrupt Swami would like to have a 15-minute meeting with you. So please conclude the meeting once the 15 minutes are over."

Hearing this, Swamishri became emotional and gently expressed his dissatisfaction, "So what if it takes 20 minutes? The meeting should be completed. And if not today, then tomorrow."

At 92 years old, Swamishri's sentiments reflected his unwavering dedication to seva. For him, true seva isn't governed by the clock, but driven by love, care, and a deep sense of responsibility.

title: Steady Through Pain
text:
This morning, after darshan, pujā, and blessings, Swamishri performed a special pujan on the occasion of Rath Yātrā and operated a remote-control chariot carrying Shri Akshar-Purushottam Maharaj. After breakfast, Swamishri mentioned, "During the sabha today, I felt pain in my stomach for five minutes." He later added, "My stomach was hurting a lot," to which the swamis replied, "Bapa, you could have told us then!"

In the evening, he attended the sabhā, sat in the chariot, and completed two full circumambulations of the mandir, never allowing anyone to become aware of his discomfort. As he was retiring for the night, Swamishri revealed, "Today, I experienced the 'maximum' pain during the Rath Yātrā. I was unable to enjoy it at all."

Swamishri's willingness to endure physical pain without complaint reveals his profound dedication to his devotees' happiness, placing their well-being above his own.

title: His Inner Wish
text:
Prior to Swamishri's dinner, seizing an opportunity to ask a series of questions on behalf of other swamis, Gurumanan Swami asked, "At the present time, your inner wish is for us to focus on what endeavor—one that eliminates your fatigue?"

Swamishri succinctly yet resolutely replied, "Divyabhāv."

Regardless of time, place, or circumstance, Swamishri persistently encourages all to cultivate divyabhāv in other devotees. To him, it is more than just an endeavor. It is a staple of his life and the essential foundation for peace, collective growth, and harmony.

title: Oriented Around Bhagwan
text:
After completing his pujā, Swamishri performed the murti pratishthā ceremonies for two hari mandirs (Mulund and Thane) in the Mumbai area. Once the ceremony was over, his sofa was moved and placed in front of the murtis.

Noticing this, Swamishri immediately pointed out to the attendant swamis that the murtis of Maharaj and Swami might be hidden behind him. When he mentioned his concern, Shrutipriya Swami gently reassured him, "The murtis aren't covered; your sofa has been positioned accordingly."

Swamishri's immediate concern reveals his deep reverence for Bhagwan. Such awareness arises only in those who truly recognize the glory of Bhagwan and firmly believe that Bhagwan resides in the murti.

title: Our Personal Ideal
text:
On this day, three question-and-answer sessions were recorded for devotees in North America. A few questions were asked by kishores striving to deepen their connection with Bhagwan.

Question: What quality of Nilkanth Varni do you admire the most?
Swamishri: "Bhakti! Doing bhakti."

Question: Which murti of Nilkanth Varni do you meditate on?
Swamishri: "The one where He is standing on one leg with His arms stretched out, performing tāp. I really like that one."

Swamishri's love for Nilkanth Varni is rooted in a deep appreciation for bhakti and penance. He guides us to imbibe that same spirit of devotion and inner strength, and to let Nilkanth Varni's image become our personal ideal.

title: Blessings for Mukpāth
text:
After the curtains closed, Priyakirtan Swami stepped forward. He has memorized 501 kirtans—so thoroughly that he can sing continuously for up to 20 hours—and he reviews them for an hour every day. In addition, he has also memorized verses from both the Harililamrut Sagar and Nishkulanand Kāvya. Swamishri was deeply pleased and offered him heartfelt blessings.

Standing nearby was Gurudarshan Swami, to whom Swamishri also gave blessings. Curious, Gurudarshan Swami asked, "What did you give [me] blessings for?"

Swamishri replied, "To do mukhpāth."

Such is Swamishri's reverence for mukhpāth that he offers blessings not only when one completes it, but even when one simply resolves to begin.

title: Food for His Soul
text:
This morning, after completing his walk, Swamishri began his regular exercise routine. As always, he listened to Shastriji Maharaj's jivan charitra during this time.

Today's audio described the historic moment when Akshar-Purushottam Maharaj was enshrined in Vadhwan. Swamishri listened with full concentration. Once his exercise was over, the audio was paused, as per routine.

But Swamishri immediately said twice, "Play it further."

Uttamyogi Swami gently showed him the time—it was 12:26 PM, time for lunch.

Swamishri, deeply moved, responded, "The true essence has just come, and you are interrupting it."

Swamishri becomes entirely immersed in the jivan charitras of his gurus. For him, they are not merely history—they are divine incidents that nourish his soul more than even food.

title: Enduring Silently
text:
After lunch, Paramanand Swami came to Swamishri to seek blessings for his recurring health issues. Swamishri listened attentively and lovingly gave him blessings.

Then, Uttamyogi Swami shared, "[Paramanand Swami] once remarked, 'It's astonishing how Mahant Swami continues his vicharan and performs [murti] pratishthās. At this age, even raising one's hand or sitting in a sabhā feels like a project. I experience this myself because of my ailments, and Mahant Swami is 92 years old. Imagine how much he must be tolerating!'"

Hearing this, an attendant swami asked, "Swami Bapa, is it really a 'project' for you to raise your hand or sit in a sabhā?"

Swamishri affirmed and said, "Everything happens by Bhagwan's will."

He has dedicated his body to BAPS and continues to endure silently in the service of Bhagwan, his gurus, and his devotees.

title: Measured in Love
text:
After Swamishri completed his puja, the curtains closed. The attendant swamis helped Swamishri stand up so he could take a brief walk to loosen his legs.

During this time, the attendant swamis, speaking quietly so Swamishri wouldn't hear, said, "It's gotten late today, so let's tell [the moderator] to ask only five questions during the question-and-answer session."

However, Swamishri had overheard their conversation. Once seated on the sofa, he responded with dissatisfaction, "What is the problem if it goes five minutes longer?"

As per Swamishri's wish, all the questions were asked without any reduction.

Swamishri never looks at the clock when it comes to serving devotees. His care isn't measured in minutes, but in love.

title: Our True Inspiration
text:
On this day, three question-and-answer sessions were recorded for devotees in North America. Among the questions were those from kishores, eager to deepen their connection with Bhagwan.

Question: What inspiration should kishores take from Nilkanth Varni's life?
Swamishri: "Live a disciplined and austere life. When the senses and mind are under control and aligned with satsang, we can offer genuine seva and bhakti to Bhagwan Swaminarayan. But if the mind is impure, everything outside becomes chaotic too."

Question: How did Nilkanth Varni spread the true siddhant?
Swamishri: "First, through His pure character. And through upasana—constant devotion to Bhagwan. He never forgot Bhagwan, even for a second. Though He was Bhagwan Himself, He performed all actions as an ideal example. Unless you live it, it doesn't truly impact others."

For Swamishri, Nilkanth Varni's principles are the ultimate source of inspiration.

title: Pleasing Bhagwan
text:
Today, in the evening sabhā, as part of the Satsang Diksha scripture parayan, Swamishri explained verses 237 to 250.

While explaining verse 240, he said, "To reinforce profound devotion (parābhakti) towards Swaminarayan Bhagwan in one's heart, one should observe vows during chāturmās according to the guru's instructions."

Swamishri elaborated, "Parābhakti means having the sole desire to please only Bhagwan Swaminarayan—nothing else. Nothing should come in the way of pleasing Him; do not keep any other desire. That is parābhakti. It includes both physical and mental restraint."

Swamishri reminds us that parābhakti is found in deep inner alignment. When every thought and action flows from the desire to please Bhagwan, devotion becomes truly elevated.

title: Effort with Heart
text:
As Swamishri was about to leave, his eyes fell upon the intricate backdrop displayed behind him. The entire piece had been lovingly crafted by the yuvati mandal using the delicate technique of quilling art.

Anandvatsal Swami explained how the art was created and shared, "It took the yuvati mandal approximately 84 hours to complete this. They offered this seva with immense devotion."

Swamishri was deeply pleased and remarked, "This is a work of hard labor." After a pause, he added, "It is a work of hard labor, patience, and faith."

In every act of bhakti and seva, these are the qualities Swamishri values most: effort, endurance, and devotion rooted in faith.

title: A Subtle Eye for Detail
text:
After dinner tonight, a picture was placed in Swamishri's bedroom depicting the moment when Shastriji Maharaj had his very first darshan of Bhagatji Maharaj. In the painting, Bhagatji Maharaj is sitting on the floor, sewing with a needle and thread while doing katha-varta.

Pointing to the image, Swamishri asked, "Is Bhagatji Maharaj wearing a dhotiyu or a chonyo?"

Someone replied, "A dhotiyu."

Swamishri gently corrected, "A chonyo."

Swamishri was asked, "On what basis did you decide that?"

Swamishri pointed to the broader fold typical of a chonyo. Everyone then saw it clearly and agreed.

Swamishri's depth of perception, even in the smallest details, reveals his deep connection with the lives and forms of his gurus. Even the subtlest features don't escape his loving and attentive gaze.

title: Wrong is Wrong
text:
During the Yuva Din sabha, Swamishri offered valuable guidance to youth navigating real-life challenges through a question-and-answer session.

Question: "Swamibapa, nowadays there's a trend of 'Let's try [it] once.' For example, 'What is the harm in watching a movie in a theater just once? What is the harm in smoking or trying alcohol just once?' So can we try it once?"

Swamishri: "There's no need to try it at all. That's the wrong path. Shriji Maharaj has clearly said, 'Wrong is wrong'—it can never become right. So, that path must be completely avoided. What we do in accordance with agna is right. Anything done outside of agna is wrong. That eventually leads to regret. So don't even walk that path."

Swamishri reminds us that righteousness is not based on curiosity or cultural trends, but on clarity of principle. True strength lies in saying no before the first compromise is ever made.

title: Keep Divyabhāv
text:
Today was the sacred day of Guru Purnima. On this special occasion, Swamishri got ready earlier than usual and arrived at the mandir for darshan.

As he reached the central shrine, Pujya Viveksagar Swami told him, "I'm going to Bochasan this morning for the Guru Purnima samaiyo. I will say 'Jay Swaminarayan' to everyone on your behalf... is there anything else you would like me to convey?"

Swamishri replied, "Everyone should keep divyabhāv."

Swamishri's deepest inner wish is for all of us to keep divyabhāv. He guides us to offer our devotion to our guru by living with the vision he asks of us.

title: His True Hardship
text:
During the Kishore Din sabha, Swamishri answered various questions while participating in several activities throughout the day. That night, after Swamishri completed cheshta and had showered, Uttamshlok Swami asked Swamishri for forgiveness in regards to the various activities Swamishri partook in and said, "Please forgive us if you endured any hardships during the kishore mandal sabha today."

Swamishri replied gently, "I don't feel this is a hardship. If you make me just sit, that feels like hardship."

For the Satpurush, seva is not a burden—it is bhakti. From him, true hardship lies not in action, but in being kept from serving Bhagwan and His devotees.

title: Benefits of Mukhpāth
text:
When the topic of mukhpāth arose, Swamishri shared, "By doing mukhpāth, everyone becomes prepared. They become 'all-round'ers. They flourish in all 'fields', in all areas, and in their studies in every way. It leads to holistic development."

Swamishri further elaborated, "One must understand what one has memorized; this is the primary objective. Memorization leads to a firm understanding. Then, in any 'field', one becomes proficient, attains a 'mastery', and progresses. Additionally, one will be able to decipher, 'What should I do? Which direction should I take?'"

Atmatrupt Swami remarked, "[It appears you] are using mukhpāth as a means of molding our souls."

Swamishri affirmed, "It will lead to firm satsang rooted within the soul."

Through mukhpāth, he molds our understanding, sharpens our judgment, and guides us toward improvement in Satsang and in all areas of life.

title: Staying Firm in Agna
text:
During the Yuva Din sabha, Swamishri offered heartfelt guidance to youth through a question-and-answer session.

Question: "Swami, in college, there are so many groups. If we don't join them, we're seen as different or labeled narrow-minded. We know we shouldn't join bad groups, but if we don't, we end up feeling alone. What should we do?"

Swamishri: "If you join them, there will be bad consequences. If you don't, you may have to endure a little [discomfort]. [Your] friends might say things, but our protection lies in this."

Question: "Today's youth often seek shortcuts to earn money—the stock market, cryptocurrency, gambling. Should we get involved in that or not?"

Swamishri: "Understand that the entire path is wrong. Shriji Maharaj has instructed us not to walk that path. If we follow His command, we'll be happy. If not, we'll suffer."

Swamishri reminds us that temporary discomfort is far better than long-term regret.

title: Attuned to Devotion
text:
Today's sabhā ran very late, so Swamishri came for dinner at 8:50 PM. As he entered, he asked to sit on the sofa to begin reciting the cheshtā. The attendant swamis reminded him, "Dinner is still pending." Swamishri was surprised—he had completely forgotten he hadn't eaten yet.

In Swamishri's mind, it was already time for cheshtā. But how could someone forget dinner like this? For most of us, the later it gets, the more we remember we haven't eaten. But for Swamishri, the later it gets, the more he forgets about dinner entirely.

We forget the things we aren't focused on. Swamishri has no focus on eating—that's why it slipped his mind. But when it comes to cheshtā, no matter how late meetings go, he never forgets.

His mind is so attuned to devotion that it becomes automatic—he forgets food, but never forgets Bhagwan.

title: Preparing the Future
text:
After giving his blessings, as Swamishri was heading back to his room, he said to Bhadresh Swami along the way, "All of them have truly become prepared."

Bhadresh Swami responded, "These are still young children who have become prepared, so just imagine how much will be accomplished in five years."

Swamishri said, "The entire universe will be colored [in Satsang]."

Bhadresh Swami added, "[May] those who study in the Siddhant-Sarvasva become scholars and engage in respectful discussions of the shastras with other scholars."

Hearing this, Swamishri joyfully responded, "The bell [of victory] is ringing. Everyone has done mukhpāth in this way."

Bhadresh Swami remarked, "Mukhpāth is a sign of dāsbhāv. Everything else might happen, but not mukhpāth."

Swamishri agreed and said, "Mukhpāth only happens when one becomes completely absorbed in it."

title: A Divine Will
text:
Later in the afternoon, while Swamishri was having his meal, Atmatrupt Swami arrived for a meeting.

After their discussion, Atmatrupt Swami said, "The use of the Sanskrit language has declined. Hardly anyone learns it anymore, but you have said that children abroad will speak in Sanskrit. We cannot understand how such a resolution comes from your heart."

Swamishri humbly replied, "By Bhagwan's will," and then added, "Bhagwan is speaking."

Atmatrupt Swami responded, "In that case, the era will be transformed."

Bhadresh Swami asked, "Do you truly envision that they will all speak in Sanskrit?"

Swamishri affirmed, "They will speak with such strength."

What seems impossible through ordinary vision becomes reality through the sankalp of the Satpurush. When such divine will is spoken, it becomes a force that shapes the future.

title: The Ultimate Focus
text:
After cheshta was completed, Swamishri was shown a video of young lion cubs. He was very pleased by watching it, and especially delighted by the graceful gait of the lions. With delight, he remarked, "It is a fine lion."

Afterward, as he was about to rise from the sofa, Swamishri's eyes fell upon a photograph depicting the first meeting between Bhagatji Maharaj and Shastriji Maharaj. He paused and gazed at it with deep reverence.

Then, Swamishri said something truly insightful: "Why should we end with the darshan of a lion? At the end, we should have the darshan of Bhagatji Maharaj and Shastriji Maharaj." Saying this, Swamishri stood up.

For him, darshan of Bhagwan and the Satpurush is the ultimate focus, the anchor of our hearts, and the vision with which to conclude every day.

title: Cultivating Firm Satsang
text:
During the morning blessings, yuvaks who had arrived from Vadodara to attend a special shibir had the opportunity to engage in a question-and-answer session with Swamishri.

Question: "Swami, how can we develop firm conviction in the supreme attainment we have received?"
Swamishri: "Have faith in Maharaj's words."

Question: "Why are the resolutions we make often unfulfilled?"
Swamishri: "There must be some flaw. Otherwise, they would be fulfilled. Or it may be Bhagwan's will. When Bhagwan desires more work to be accomplished, He does not allow the [resolution] to be fulfilled."

Question: "Maharaj asked for two boons from Ramanand Swami. If you were to ask for a boon for us, what would it be?"
Swamishri: "That everyone's Satsang becomes firm; everything is included in that. If our Satsang is firm, no questions remain."

Swamishri pointed every question back to one solution: firm Satsang.

title: Divyabhāv
text:
Tonight, just before Swamishri's dinner, seizing an opportunity to ask a series of questions on behalf of other swamis, Gurumanan Swami relayed a question that other swamis had asked earlier: "Right now, what do you have a liking for—one which [we can] do to take away your tiredness?"

Swamishri succinctly yet resolutely replied, "Divyabhāv."

Regardless of time, place, or circumstance, Swamishri persistently encourages all to cultivate divyabhāv in others. To him, it is more than just an endeavor. It is a staple of his life and the essential foundation for peace, collective growth, and harmony.

title: Humble Leadership
text:
During a question-and-answer session, Swamishri was asked: "Swami, on July 20, 2012, in Ahmedabad, Pramukh Swami Maharaj appointed you as his spiritual successor through a letter... But you never told anyone. It was only after Bapa returned to Akshardham that everyone came to know. This was a monumental moment, yet you kept it hidden. How were you able to keep such a significant event silent?"

Swamishri replied, "I had no idea at all. Honestly, I only found out when I was told."

He was then asked, "Did you ever feel excited or joyful that now you will become the Guru?"

Swamishri humbly responded, "Even now, I don't feel that way."

Asked how he manages the entire Sanstha, Swamishri answered simply, "Bhagwan takes care of everything. He is the one doing everything, and He is the one who will continue to do everything."

title: The Weight of Disunity
text:
During the evening sabha, balaks held a question-and-answer session with Swamishri.

Question: "[Swami], when do you feel tired?"
Swamishri: "When samp (unity) is not maintained, I feel tired."

Question: "Do you ever get tired from constantly turning the mala?"
Swamishri: "I never get tired."

For Swamishri, tiredness isn't physical — it is when harmony among devotees is lost that his heart feels the weight. His words remind us that true fatigue comes from division between devotees, whereas through devotion and unity, his heart remains light, steady, and tireless.

title: Developing Faith
text:
During the journey from Dar es Salaam to Kampala, a devotee traveling with Swamishri asked, "Swami, we are doing our seva according to your āgnā, but what more can we do in satsang to please you even more?"

Swamishri gently replied, "[Inspire] others to develop faith [in Bhagwan and the Satpurush]."

In just a few words, Swamishri revealed the heart of true satsang: to live with deep conviction in Bhagwan and the Satpurush and to inspire that same faith in others.

title: Faith and Wisdom
text:
During the morning blessings, yuvaks who had arrived from Vadodara to attend a special shibir engaged in a question-and-answer session with Swamishri.

Question: "Often, we struggle to tolerate others and react negatively. What can we do to avoid this?"
Swamishri: "Right now, you're in a growing phase, so some ups and downs will happen. But a time will come when you will become knowledgeable, and then such questions will not arise."

Question: "On social media, we often end up seeing things we shouldn't. What understanding should we keep to avoid being drawn in?"
Swamishri: "[Have] faith in Bhagwan. Just like when a doctor tells us, 'Avoid this medicine, and take this medicine,' we follow it sincerely for our well-being. Similarly, if we do not follow Bhagwan's command, what kind of wisdom do we really have?"

Swamishri's guidance reminds us that spiritual maturity is a journey.

title: The Strength of Niyam-Dharma
text:
During the morning blessings, yuvaks from Vadodara engaged in a question-and-answer session with Swamishri.

Question: "When [we see] other youths not following niyams and enjoying themselves, we feel like doing the same. Is that thought appropriate?"
Swamishri: "It is not appropriate. By following niyam-dharma, you will maintain a stable state, whereas those who do not follow niyams may seem well off, but in the end, there is only loss in it."

Question: "The resolutions we take regarding niyam-dharma last only three or four days, and then our state becomes as before. How can we improve?"
Swamishri: "When a doctor gives advice, we follow it because we recognize the need; we even pay money. This is Bhagwan. But first, have we [truly] accepted Bhagwan? If we have, then no question remains, and everything happens well."

True progress in niyam-dharma begins with firmly accepting Bhagwan in our lives.

title: Sāchu, Sāchu
text:
During a special sabha for the India Trip delegates, the delegates asked Swamishri, "Swami, we want our renewed faith to last, even after we return home. We wish to defeat māyā and attain Akshardham in this very life. Please guide us."

In his response, Swamishri repeatedly described our prāpti as 'sāchu'—true, real, and eternal. Swamishri said, "Look, Shriji Maharaj is sāchā, Gunatitanand Swami is sāchā, ekāntik dharma is sācho, the devotees are sāchā, and everything [within Satsang] is sāchu sāchu. Thus, we should never allow those that are false to influence our minds. Even if our nature remains flawed, our faith should remain firm—that regardless of what hardships come, even if the sky and the underworld become one, our faith should not falter. Apart from Maharaj and Swami, there is nothing. Keep this firm within your souls."

Such conviction will carry us beyond māyā and toward Akshardham.

title: Effort and Faith
text:
During the morning blessings, yuvaks who had arrived from Vadodara to attend a special shibir engaged in a question-and-answer session with Swamishri.

Question: "We do not have any interest in reading, so what should we do?"
Swamishri: "If [you] strengthen your Satsang, interest will [naturally] awaken. In Satsang, [you] will come across topics that connect to your liking, and gradually, you will progress in it."

Question: "This shibir is themed 'Dhanya Dhanya Mam Jivan'. Please bless us so we always feel that our life is truly blessed."
Swamishri: "For that, you will have to make an effort. It won't come for free—because what comes free, leaves just as easily. Start by having firm faith in Maharaj and that everything said is the absolute truth. When true faith arises, everything else follows. The only thing lacking is faith. But once full faith is there, life becomes truly blessed."

title: Sincere Effort Matters
text:
During the evening sabha, a question-and-answer session took place. Swamishri was asked, "When our relatives do things we do not like, we get agitated and angry. Similarly, we are your disciples, and when we do not follow your āgnā, do you feel agitated?"

Swamishri replied, "All of you are honest and truly want to progress [in satsang]. So, it stays in my mind that everyone should progress. And they will [progress] and become ekāntik. That feeling stays in my mind."

A follow-up question was asked, "But when we do not follow your āgnā, do you feel agitated?"

Swamishri said, "A little. I feel that everyone is taking small steps, but because everyone's intent is genuine, everything is [ultimately] fine."

Swamishri's words remind us that what matters most is a sincere desire to progress.

title: Respecting the Murtis
text:
Today, as Swamishri was walking from his room to the pujā cabin, he noticed that in one of the rooms, the murtis of the Guru Paramparā were placed directly on the floor. Upon reaching the cabin, Swamishri guided, "Something should be spread beneath the murtis of the Guru Paramparā; they should not be placed directly on the ground like that."

Through this simple yet profound observation, Swamishri taught that reverence should be shown to all murtis. Regardless of whether a murti is consecrated, it should always be treated with the utmost respect and dignity.

title: True Association
text:
As Swamishri was preparing to retire for the night, an attendant swami asked, "Swamishri, today you spoke about how keeping good company leads to attaining nirdoshbuddhi. I am always in good company, so I will attain nirdoshbuddhi, right?"

Swamishri responded with emphasis, "Only if you [truly] associate!"

Surprised, the attendant asked, "But don't I associate with you? I stay with you—doesn't that count as association?"

Swamishri replied, "No... all of these things—the table and everything here also stay with us. If you have [truly] associated, then the virtues of the person you are with should begin to reflect in your life. Only then can it be said you have kept their company."

Swamishri emphasized that real satsang is not about being physically close to the Satpurush, but about internalizing their virtues.

title: Always Busy in Bhajan
text:
Swamishri arrived in Abu Dhabi. After the welcome sabha, he went to his residence, where the curtains were drawn open, giving a clear view of the mandir from his room. A goshthi took place with all the swamis present, and a good amount of time passed in discussion.

Toward the end of the goshthi, Brahmavihari Swami jokingly asked, "Swami, what is your schedule like now? You must be very busy, right?"

Immediately, Swamishri made a gesture of turning the mala and replied, "'Busy' doing bhajan; otherwise, 'easy'."

This simple yet profound response reflected Swamishri's inner state—always focused on Bhagwan. Amidst responsibilities and travel, his heart remained anchored in devotion.

title: Anchored in Dharma-Niyam
text:
During the evening sabha, Swamishri shared profound guidance through a heartfelt question-and-answer session.

Question: "How can we repay our [spiritual] debts?"
Swamishri: "Live firmly and sincerely by the codes of dharma and niyams. Maharaj has said, 'I reside in dharma and niyams.' Hold onto them strongly—everything is included in that. If difficulties arise in maintaining dharma and niyams, keep a strong resolve and follow them. In short, be cautious, not careless, or else challenges will follow."

Question: "Swami, what can we do to avoid causing you any bhido (pain)?"
Swamishri: "Again, it is the same. Be unwavering in dharma and niyam. Keep a stronger resolve for [following] niyams than you have today. And keep in mind, 'I want to become ekāntik.'"

Swamishri reminded us that sincere, daily effort to stay anchored in dharma and niyams is the foundation for pleasing Maharaj.

title: The True Measure of Seva
text:
During the evening sabha, Swamishri shared profound guidance through a heartfelt question-and-answer session.

Question: "Although all forms of seva are equal, we sometimes feel that one seva is bigger and another is smaller. What should we do about that?"
Swamishri: "Seva is seva. No seva is big or small. All types of seva are equal. In seva, Maharaj looks at your heart and attitude, and assigns you 'marks' accordingly. If your inner intent is pure, you will keep progressing."

Swamishri taught that the true value of seva lies in the sincerity of our heart, not the scale or visibility of the task. When seva is performed with pure devotion, Maharaj is pleased, and spiritual progress naturally follows.

title: Cultivating Dradh Priti
text:
Today, Swamishri blessed the 400 delegates of the North American Summer Camp. The nine-day event focused on Dradh Priti (intense love) through the lens of the Shastras, Siddhant, Sanstha, and the Satpurush.

The following day, the delegates participated in a heartfelt program titled "Live for Swamishri," during which they took an oath through the kirtan "Ame Sau Swamina Balak" (We are all Swami's children).

Swamishri's blessings were conveyed: "[Seeing] all of you gathered at the NSC has given me great joy. Continue taking steps forward and remain strong, and you will experience even greater joy. And dradh priti for the Satpurush is the true essence. [Where this love exists], there is light, and so everywhere, in 'each corner' there will be light and there will be joy."

When dradh priti fills our hearts, progress becomes natural, and happiness spreads to every corner of our lives.

title: Faith Without Proximity
text:
During the evening sabha, Swamishri shared profound guidance through a heartfelt question-and-answer session.

Question: "If we do not get the opportunity to come close to you, what should we do?"
Swamishri: "You have to keep faith. Keep nirdoshbuddhi, trusting that whatever [the Sant] does is for your best. Whether he calls you or not, stay at peace. And truly, the Sant is nirdosh (innocent). He does not have any partiality. So trust that and keep moving forward."

Swamishri reminded us that closeness to the Guru is not measured by physical proximity, but by deep trust, faith, and nirdoshbuddhi. When we stay steady in this understanding, even from afar, we remain deeply connected.

title: Unity Through Humility
text:
During the evening sabha, Swamishri shared profound guidance through a heartfelt question-and-answer session.

Question: "How can we increase samp (unity) among ourselves?"
Swamishri: "Bow down to one another from the heart. Understand the mahima (greatness) that the person in front of you is greater than you—not less, but greater. With this kind of feeling, seva becomes enjoyable, and you will like doing everything. Understand their mahima in this way and cooperate with each other."

Swamishri showed that the secret to unity lies in genuine humility. When we truly see others as greater and serve with that mindset, harmony flourishes and seva becomes enjoyable.

title: Truly Celebrating Ekadashi
text:
In the afternoon, Swamishri was seated on his bed, preparing to rest. Several attendant swamis were present. Swamishri looked at them and commanded with emphasis, "Today, we have to stay awake."

The attendant swamis replied, "Yes Swami, on Ekadashi afternoons we hold a Sant Sabha, so we automatically stay awake."

Hearing this, Swamishri immediately bowed and stretched out both hands toward the swamis, as if to touch their feet! Startled, the swamis quickly responded, "No, no, Swami!" They gently held his hands and bowed respectfully at his feet.

Swamishri was deeply pleased to hear that the swamis spent the entire Ekadashi afternoon engaged in katha and satsang. With joy lighting up his face, he exclaimed, "Katha-vārtā dhām-dhamāvo (let spiritual talks flourish)!"

For Swamishri, true joy comes not from rest, but from the vibrancy of satsang.

title: Bearing for Others
text:
After finishing his breakfast, Swamishri began taking the medicine prescribed by his physician. Seeing this, Gunvatsal Swami lovingly said, "Let us take the medicine instead," expressing a heartfelt desire of all devotees to take on Swamishri's physical pain in his place.

Swamishri responded, "Maharaj has asked for the pain of His devotees [to fall on Him instead]. There is no question of giving it [to anyone else]."

This brief exchange revealed the deep love of the devotees and Swamishri's even deeper selflessness. Even in moments of personal discomfort, he chooses to bear the burdens of others with quiet acceptance, unwavering faith, and compassion.

title: Peace Beyond Preference
text:
While preparing to sleep at night, Swamishri sat on his bed and softly said, "The dhokli today was spicy. I mixed everything together and ate it." Before the attendant swamis could respond, Swamishri added, "And yesterday during breakfast, the almonds were bitter too."

Surprised, the swamis asked, "Then why didn't you say anything?"

Swamishri gently replied, "Everyone was in a joyous mood… and where would I have spat it out?" Despite the bitterness, Swamishri had quietly eaten it to maintain the joy of those around him.

Hearing this, the attendant swamis said, "Swami, please don't hesitate to tell us next time. There are always arrangements of separate bowls."

Swamishri gently smiled, conveying a silent message: remember Bhagwan and eat—no matter the taste.

title: A Lesson of Divinity
text:
Later in the afternoon, Swamishri woke up from his nap to find a message from swamis studying in Sarangpur. They were beginning their English class and had requested Swamishri to say a sentence in English that they could remember.

With gentle compassion, Swamishri said, "Have divine feeling for each other."

In just a few words, he conveyed the essence of divyabhav—to see and serve one another with divine vision and feeling. More than grammar or vocabulary, it was this message of mutual respect, love, and spiritual unity that became their most treasured lesson.

title: The True Raksha
text:
After completing his puja, Swamishri went into the back room to take his medicine. As he was returning, Atmaswarup Swami said, "Swami! Today is Rakshabandhan. Everyone will ask you, 'Please protect us…' But what should we do to be eternally protected from māyā?"

Swamishri replied, "Divyabhāv (seeing divinity) in everyone. The swamis and devotees are all divine. Whoever understands this essential principle, reflects on it, and lives by it becomes truly joyful. Their experience of bliss never fades, and they conquer the world (win over their own mind). Everything is encompassed in this. Without divyabhāv, one remains at a very low level. Then, struggles arise."

Swamishri's words revealed the real raksha (protection) is not simply a thread tied on the wrist, but the divine virtues tied to the heart.

title: The Vision Behind Mukhpath
text:
Today, after dinner, Swamishri was shown a video of a four-year-old child from the Ankleshwar region reciting Satsang Diksha verses in his sleep.

Swamishri was astonished and overjoyed upon seeing the video.

Later, Swamishri was asked, "What is your reason for engaging children in mukhpāth?"

Swamishri replied, "Because I want to take everyone to Akshardham."

Every effort Swamishri makes, whether encouraging mukhpāth, inspiring seva, or guiding our daily lives, is only for the ultimate liberation and betterment of all of the devotees he holds dear to his heart.

title: Putting Others at Ease
text:
After completing his puja, Swamishri went to the prarthana mandir for darshan. As the attendant swamis helped him rise from his wheelchair for arti, he noticed Pujya Ghanshyam Bapa sitting on a chair with his feet dangling.

Pointing toward him, Swamishri said, "Put a footrest underneath." A swami quickly placed a mat, but Pujya Ghanshyam Bapa's feet still hung above the ground.

Once again, Swamishri drew their attention to it. The attendant swamis explained, "Someone has gone to get the footrest." Only after the proper footrest was brought and Pujya Ghanshyam Bapa was comfortable did Swamishri begin performing the arti.

This small yet telling moment speaks volumes: Swamishri's concern for the comfort of others always came before his own needs, even in old age.

title: Always with Thakorji
text:
During the visit to the Surat Akshardham auditorium in the evening, Swamishri sat on a swing while Akshar-Purushottam Maharaj was placed to his right on a slightly higher seat. Swamishri's gaze stayed fixed on Thakorji, and though he wished to hold them on his lap, he remained silent as the program had already begun.

When the curtains closed for a brief intermission, Swamishri was helped up to stretch his legs. Upon sitting back down, he immediately asked for Akshar-Purushottam Maharaj and placed them in his lap. When the curtains reopened, the swamis continued swinging Swamishri, with Thakorji in his embrace.

Even while leaving the auditorium and descending the ramp, Swamishri kept Thakorji on his lap. Later, while meeting a yuvak, he again asked for Thakorji and carried them to his room.

Swamishri never set Thakorji aside, always keeping Him close and central to his being.

title: The Present Form of Pramukh Swami Maharaj
text:
During the morning blessings, a small child innocently asked Swamishri, "Bapa, what [do you imagine] Pramukh Swami Maharaj is doing right now?"

Swamishri chuckled and replied, "[He] is seated here [before you]."

In this manner, Swamishri humbly revealed he is the present form of Pramukh Swami Maharaj.

title: Rest Can Wait
text:
When Swamishri completed his bath, it was 1:38 p.m. The attendant swamis were pleased, thinking Swamishri would be able to rest earlier than usual. While it wasn't truly "early," it was ahead of his normal schedule.

Instead, Swamishri asked for paper and sat down to write letters. Five minutes passed… then ten… fifteen… twenty. The swamis who had come to assist began to doze off, and some even fell asleep. But Swamishri kept writing.

Nearly forty minutes later, at 2:17 p.m., he finally went for his afternoon rest.

Even when given the rare chance to rest early, Swamishri chose instead to serve others, one letter at a time. Each stroke of his pen was an act of love, each word a thread strengthening his bond with those he guided.

title: Truth Above All
text:
During a discussion with Swamishri, Uttamyogi Swami recalled an incident from Shastriji Maharaj's life: "In Surat, when Bhagatji Maharaj's swamis had gone to draw water from a well, Shastriji Maharaj stood up for Bhagatji Maharaj."

Swamishri gently corrected him: "Not Bhagatji—he stood up for the truth."

Then Swamishri added, "When it comes to upholding the truth, one must stand up for it, even if it means doing so in a roundabout way."

Shriji Maharaj teaches this in Vachanamrut Gadhada 3-7: "In no way should one abandon one's loyalty to God and His Bhakta, even if while keeping that loyalty one's reputation increases or decreases, or one is honored or insulted, or one lives or dies." For Swamishri, truth is a sacred stand—one to be upheld at any cost.

title: Faith Beyond Fatigue
text:
Today, despite the Janmashtami fast, Swamishri performed more dandavats than usual. In Bochasan, he offered 15 during Mangala arti, 5 in the Nilkanth Varni abhishek mandap, 5 during Shangar arti, 5 at Purushottam Swami's deri, and 6 during his puja. He then travelled to Chansad, where he offered 10 at Pramukh Swami Maharaj's birthplace and 5 at the Chansad Hari Mandir.

From Chansad, he journeyed to Atladara. The moment he stepped out of the car, he turned towards the mandir and said, "Let's go for darshan." Rain had left water pooled everywhere, yet without hesitation, Swamishri waded through with support. Reaching the mandir, he stood before Ghanshyam Maharaj's murti, remarking, "What innocence!" In the tide of his devotion, his hunger and fatigue were washed away.

By the end of the day, at age 83, Swamishri had performed 71 dandavats—all while fasting. His devotion knew no limits.

title: Discipline Beyond Age
text:
Today, after completing his walk, Swamishri returned to his room. Since it was getting late, the exercises he usually performed after his walk were canceled.

Swamishri asked, "Why?"

Shrutipriya Swami replied, "It is late, and lunch will also be delayed."

Immediately, Swamishri became spirited and said, "So what if it is one o'clock? What harm is there in being half an hour late now and then? But if we don't exercise, we will become like dung!"

With that conviction, Swamishri went ahead with his post-walk exercises.

Even at 92, Swamishri's resolve was absolute. For him, discipline wasn't a mere routine, but an act of worship that consecrated the body, sharpened the mind, and elevated the soul.

title: Faith Over Fear
text:
Swamishri was descending in a crane on his way back to his residence. From above, the entire Akshardham site stretched out before him. Work was in full swing—a massive pillarless assembly hall for 20,000 people was rising on one side, while exhibition halls, a boat ride, welcome center, and residential quarters were all simultaneously under construction.

After showing him the progress, Swamishri was asked, "With so much work happening, don't you feel any tension?"

Swamishri immediately replied, "Bhagwan is here. What is the need for tension?"

The attendant swamis pressed further, "But doesn't even a little worry remain?"

With calm certainty, Swamishri responded, "Everything will be completed."

When one understands Bhagwan as the all-doer, there is no room for worry. When life rests in Bhagwan's hands, we remain free of worry and tension.

title: Pure Inside and Out
text:
Today, during lunch, Swamishri noticed the small hand fan that the attendant swamis were using. Pointing to it, he asked Vinaypriya Swami, "Do you wash the rubber on this fan?"

A green rubber band was tied around the fan. Swamishri had been observing it for many days, and that day, he finally asked about it. He knew that if the rubber band was not cleaned regularly, it would collect dirt over time. At his request, the attendant swamis removed the rubber band immediately.

Swamishri never tolerates impurity, whether external or internal. Just as he insists on keeping even the smallest things clean, he also insists that our souls remain spotless. The niyam-dharma he guides us to follow remove every trace of impurity within, leading us closer to Bhagwan's eternal abode.

title: Polishing the Soul
text:
During the evening sabha, volunteers from various departments of Surat Akshardham reported to Swamishri and then sought his guidance through a question-and-answer session.

Question: "We are also like stones, full of chips and cracks. What understanding should we keep so that these chips and cracks transform into a murti?"
Swamishri: "Maintain satsang strongly and keep inclining yourselves toward satsang."

Question: "When one stone rubs against another, its luster increases. But when we perform seva, our natures clash and we fall into abhav-avgun. How can we avoid this?"
Swamishri: "Serve with an understanding of each other's greatness, then it will happen."

Just as a stone becomes a murti through patient chiseling, we too are shaped into ideal devotees when we live with faith, humility, and unity.

title: Light Within, Guard Within
text:
During the evening sabha, volunteers from various departments of Surat Akshardham sought Swamishri's guidance through a question-and-answer session.

Volunteers from the Electrical Department asked, "The darkness of I-ness and my-ness has enveloped us, preventing us from experiencing the bliss of the Satpurush. What should we do to remove this darkness?"
Swamishri replied, "When knowledge dawns, everything will become clear."

Next, the volunteers from the Security Department asked, "When we keep security for Akshardham, we maintain constant vigilance. What awareness should we maintain to build our inner Akshardham?"
Swamishri answered, "Keep worldly desires far away, and Bhagwan and the Sant within (close)."

True spiritual progress comes from cultivating clarity through knowledge, guarding our hearts from desires, and keeping Bhagwan and the Sant ever near.

title: Boundless Enthusiasm
text:
After his puja, Swamishri was to perform the pujan of the kalashes that were to be consecrated in Jodhpur. The ritual was meant to be done while sitting, but Swamishri insisted, "I want to stand up."

Though the attendant swamis reminded him it was to be done seated, Swamishri persisted, and they helped him stand. He then tried to apply a chandan chandlo to the top of the kalash, but his hand could not reach. Lifting himself slightly on his toes, he still fell short. Smiling a little, he applied the chandlo where he could reach.

Later, during breakfast, the swamis playfully remarked, "If you had jumped, you would have reached."

Swamishri agreed. When asked why he didn't jump, he replied, "It doesn't look good in public."

For him, no effort is too small when offered to Bhagwan.

title: Asking for Forgiveness
text:
The seven-day parayan was to begin in honor of Pramukh Swami Maharaj's return to Akshardham, and many devotees had gathered for the occasion. The sponsors of the day's parayan were to meet Swamishri. However, because the number of sponsors had increased tremendously, the swamis were moving them forward quickly.

In response, Swamishri, in his very first speech after becoming Guru, humbly apologized, saying, "Just now, everyone quickly came [for darshan] and had to quickly leave as well. So if anyone was spoken to harshly or hurt, please do not keep it in mind (please forgive us)."

On a day when the world was eager to hear his first words as Guru, he chose to ask for forgiveness, even when there was no fault of his own. True leadership begins not with claiming honor, but with bowing in humility.

title: Growing into a Mighty Tree
text:
During the evening sabha, volunteers from various departments of Surat Akshardham reported to Swamishri and sought his guidance through a question-and-answer session.

Volunteers from the Landscape Department asked, "We are small plants. What should we do to become a mighty banyan tree?"

Swamishri replied, "Do satsang. Do not miss a single Sunday sabha. Just as we build a fence to protect a young banyan tree, we should protect ourselves by adhering to the fence of dharma-niyam, and remain vigilant."

Just as a sapling grows into a strong banyan only with care and discipline, we too can grow in strength and stability by remaining rooted in satsang and sheltered by the fence of dharma-niyam.

title: In Their Joy
text:
Between 11:05 AM and 11:45 AM, Swamishri blessed 662 devotees by placing his hand on them. Of these, 450 were students from the APC Vidyanagar Chhatralay.

Punyanilay Swami asked Swamishri, "It must be difficult to repeatedly place your hand on all of these devotees, isn't it?"

Swamishri responded, "Everyone becomes pleased!"

In these few words, Swamishri revealed the essence of his heart: true joy is found in bringing joy to others. For him, blessing each devotee was not simply a task, but an expression of love in which their happiness became his own.

title: Eagerness for Sant Shibir
text:
This afternoon, Swamishri awoke at 3:13 p.m. and immediately asked, "Has the Sant Shibir started?"

Uttamyogi Swami replied, "No, there is still time. You can rest."

Swamishri then gestured, asking if he should rest until 4:00 p.m. Uttamyogi Swami responded, "Please wake up by 4:30 p.m. And if you want to rest more, that is also fine, since there is no exercise today and we are going to the sabha at 7:00 p.m."

When he was suggested to rest longer, Swamishri showed his disapproval. Then, at 3:36 p.m., he rang the pager again and asked, "Will the Sant Shibir end today?"

Uttamyogi Swami replied, "No, it will end tomorrow," once again requesting him to rest.

Swamishri's eagerness to join the Sant Shibir shone through clearly—even at the cost of his own rest.

title: Constantly Absorbed in Prapti
text:
In the afternoon, while Swamishri was having lunch, he ate his usual three crushed rotlis mixed with shak and then began drinking buttermilk. Suddenly, he started coughing, so the bowl of buttermilk was taken away, and he was given fruit instead.

After finishing the fruit, the attendant swamis asked if he would like the buttermilk again. When the half-finished bowl was brought back, Swamishri asked in surprise, "Why is this half?" as he expected a full bowl like he usually received.

They explained, "You had started coughing while drinking it earlier, so we had kept it aside." He then drank the rest.

Noticing his mind seemed elsewhere, the swamis asked, "Swamishri, if your mind wasn't on drinking the buttermilk, where was it?"

Swamishri replied, "On the thought of prapti."

title: Silent Endurance
text:
After puja, when Swamishri returned to his quarters, he walked briskly to the bathroom and quickly went to take a bath. Afterward, he mentioned, "My stomach hurt a lot today. It hurt in every corner of my stomach." Though he had been experiencing discomfort since morning, he didn't let anyone realize the pain was so severe.

Despite this, Swamishri gave darshan to devotees through the glass partition, went to the mandir for darshan, and stood up to perform arti. He also stood up to perform the abhishek of Nilkanth Varni. He then arrived at the sabha hall for his puja, gave darshan to all devotees, and gave wonderful blessings to everyone.

All this was done while silently enduring great pain. Only after everything was complete did he mention his discomfort. At 92, most would remain in bed, but Swamishri bore his discomfort with love, placing the joy of devotees above his own.

title: Sanctifying Every Moment
text:
After singing cheshta, Swamishri went to take a shower. When he came back from the bathroom, he asked for a household medicine. Since it took a few minutes for someone to bring it, Swamishri immediately requested Purushottam Bolya Prite. In those 5–7 minutes, he gave a discourse to the swamis present.

When the medicine arrived, Swamishri took it and went to bed at exactly 11:00 p.m.

Even in the smallest pauses, Swamishri showed us how to sanctify time. Instead of letting moments slip away, he filled them with bhajan and katha, reminding us that every second, no matter how ordinary, can become an opportunity for spiritual growth.

title: Emphasis on Satsang Reading
text:
During the afternoon blessings, Swamishri gave an inspiring talk about the upcoming Satsang Exams. He said, "We often say, 'There has never been such prapti in the past, nor will there ever be in the future.' Yet, despite saying this many times, it all goes in vain, and we gain nothing. The reason is a lack of [satsang] reading. If we read, we gain knowledge. Complete knowledge is the state of being param-ekantik."

He continued, "We have received this divine satsang—there is no boundary to its divinity. However, all of it gets wasted due to a lack of reading. We do read, but only if we read properly will we gain something. The mind and body must unite in reading—that is how it should be read."

Swamishri reminded us that satsang reading is not about quantity, but quality.

title: Concentration is Essential
text:
After completing his puja, Swamishri engaged in a question-and-answer session with students from the Vidyamandir, offering insightful guidance in response to their inquiries.

One student asked, "Swami, while studying, our mind does not stay focused. What should we do?"

Swamishri replied, "If one properly practices satsang, it also strengthens one's studies [and develops concentration of the mind]."

Another student asked, "Many students find certain subjects very difficult. How can we make these tough subjects easier?"

Swamishri explained, "You must become engrossed in the subject and cultivate the mindset that you want to master it. Secondly, concentration is essential. Whatever task you want to do well, you need concentration. Being distracted will not work."

Swamishri emphasized that concentration is the key to success in studies.

title: Guidance for Students
text:
After completing his puja, Swamishri engaged in a question-and-answer session with students from the Vidyamandir, offering insightful guidance in response to their inquiries.

Question: "Swami, our mind quickly latches onto negative thoughts. What should we do so we can remain positive?"
Swamishri: "Such wisdom comes from satsang. That wisdom prepares you so you are ready [to face challenges] in your tasks."

Question: "How can we grow in satsang while also managing our studies?"
Swamishri: "You have to make time for it. You must budget your time wisely — only then will everything happen."

Through his answers, Swamishri emphasized that satsang provides the wisdom to stay positive in life's challenges and that careful time management allows one to balance both spiritual growth and academic success.

title: Balance and Priorities
text:
Toward the end of the Gurukul Din evening sabha, the students engaged in a question-and-answer session with Swamishri.

Question: "We genuinely want to study well, but we have become attached to bad influences like mobile phones, TV, and games. What should we do to study well and stay away from such distractions?"
Swamishri: "For that, you should engage in satsang. Through satsang, you gain the understanding and knowledge that helps you naturally stay away from bad influences."

Question: "You often say, 'Those who study become nawabs; those who only play end up bad.' So does that mean we should only study all day? Are we not allowed to play at all?"
Swamishri: "Who says you shouldn't play? Play, jump — but in moderation. Study when it is time to study. And when it is time to play, play. But don't engage in rough or hurtful fun that causes others pain."

Swamishri taught students the importance of balance.

title: Becoming Ideal Students
text:
Toward the end of the Gurukul Din evening sabha, the students engaged in a heartfelt question-and-answer session with Swamishri.

Question: "What should we do to become ideal students?"
Swamishri: "Do satsang. Through satsang, you will gain such understanding. There will be light in your intellect. You will develop vivek (discernment) in every situation, and you won't get sidetracked. You will remain on the straight path."

Question: "The prapti we have received is so great, but how should students behave in a way that reflects [such a great attainment]?"
Swamishri: "Yes, this attainment is indeed great—it is beyond imagination. To behave in a way worthy of it, you must sincerely engage in satsang, and then everything else will [naturally] fall into place."

Swamishri emphasized that the hallmark of an ideal student is living with vivek, discipline, and sincerity.

title: Not Wasting Anything
text:
Tonight, when Swamishri came to the bathroom for his bath, Uttamyogi Swami opened a towel (katko) for him to wear. Noticing a small hole in it, he went to fold it away, intending to dispose of it.

However, Swamishri noticed and shook his head, saying, "Put a patch on it."

Uttamyogi Swami replied, "It is not worth patching."

Swamishri responded, "I will put a patch on it."

Despite being the guru of a global Sanstha, he chose to repair even a torn towel, showing his humility and commitment to conservation. Even with everything at his disposal, he exemplified simplicity, preservation, and a profound appreciation for every resource.

title: Selfless Concern
text:
After the Guru Purnima sabha, Swamishri was returning to his residence. It was a hot day, so Uttamyogi Swami asked Mahendrabhai, who was driving, "Please drive the car faster."

Noticing a police officer running alongside the car, Swamishri expressed concern: "The police officer is running."

The attendant swamis reassured him, saying, "Swami, police are stationed at short intervals. He will be left behind, so it won't be an issue."

Despite the heat, Swamishri's concern was not for himself but for the officer. He demonstrated that true leadership stems from selflessness and prioritizing the needs of others over one's own comfort, even in the smallest moments.

title: True Worth Lies in Devotion
text:
During the charter plane ride from Nairobi to Lenasia, the attendant swamis requested Swamishri to rest. As requested, Swamishri lay down on the bed, but even while resting, he continued to turn the mala.

That night, before Swamishri retired to sleep, the attendant swamis mentioned, "We had arranged a charter flight so you would be able to rest on the plane. The money [that was spent] must be worth it, no?"

Recalling a prasang of Yogiji Maharaj, Swamishri replied, "When Yogi Bapa was going to Banaras via a special bus, he told us, 'If bhajan is performed, the money is worth it. The money is not worth it when we rest.'"

Through this, Swamishri taught that the true worth of resources, be it time or money, lies not in luxury or rest, but in devotion.

title: Rooted in Humility
text:
In the evening, after getting ready, Swamishri came to the balcony overlooking the sea, where many swamis were bathing and boating. When they saw him, they joyfully raised their hands and began waving.

Swamishri lovingly lifted his hands and waved back in the same manner, giving them a special smruti. However, after a short while, he stopped and told Dharmavatsal Swami, who was standing beside him, "[We] cannot do this for too long, or we will become high profile. We are simply servants of servants."

Even in the smallest gestures, Swamishri reminded everyone that true spirituality is not found in recognition or praise, but in remaining firmly rooted in humility and the spirit of servitude.

title: Keeping Thakorji Foremost
text:
In the evening, the swamis were going to get a special opportunity to perform Swamishri's pujan by applying a chandlo of sandalwood (chandan) paste to him.

When asked if they should arrange for each swami to get the opportunity to perform this pujan, Swamishri quickly replied, "First, the pujan should be offered to Thakorji, and only then to me."

Swamishri instantly placed Thakorji before himself, reminding everyone that all honor must begin with Bhagwan. In every action of his life, he keeps Bhagwan first with unwavering devotion and remains eternally humble before Him.

title: His Eternal Identity
text:
After the morning blessings, Brahmanilay Swami and Shubhcharit Swami presented Swamishri with a garland and an ID card for a shibir named Brahmanand, organized for the yuvaks in the area they travel to. Brahmanilay Swami then said, "Swami, your name is written on this ID card, but the mandal (group) and kshetra (center) are missing. So which mandal do you belong to?"

Swamishri replied, "Akshar."

He was then asked, "Which kshetra do you belong to?"

Swamishri responded, "Akshar."

Through this simple yet profound reply, Swamishri revealed his eternal identity — that he is Akshardham himself. His being and his abode are one and the same: Akshar, forever in the service of Bhagwan.

title: True Success of a Celebration
text:
During the evening assembly, a question-and-answer session was held with Swamishri.

Question: "Swami, today marks the start of the mandir's silver jubilee celebrations. After Pramukh Swami Maharaj's centenary celebrations, you were asked, 'Are you satisfied?' You replied, 'Almost.' Then you added, 'Attaining the disposition of the Satpurush remains unfulfilled.' So, after celebrating such grand celebrations, how can we attain the disposition of the Satpurush? What does it mean to attain the Satpurush?"

Swamishri replied, "Since time immemorial, our focus has always been on niyam-dharma and nishtha (faith). If we have these, everything else will be taken care of."

Through this, Swamishri reminded everyone that true celebration is not measured by external festivity, but by living with steadfast niyam-dharma and deep faith.

title: Staying Close to Swami
text:
During the evening assembly, a question-and-answer session was held with Swamishri.

Question: "Swami, you are giving us immense lābh. But since it is not possible to always be in your direct presence, what should we do to ensure that your presence remains with us continuously?"

Swamishri: "Follow the niyams (rules) given by Maharaj, and everything else will happen on its own."

Swamishri emphasized that by living according to the niyam-dharma given to us by Bhagwan and our Gurus, we remain truly close to them. Physical distance does not matter — with niyams, we stay near their heart; without niyams, even physical closeness becomes distance.

title: The Root of True Unity
text:
During the evening assembly, a question-and-answer session was held with Swamishri.

Question: "Swami, you often speak about samp (unity). Once in Rajkot during breakfast, you explained, 'If I give this carrot juice to one sant and that sant distributes it to everyone, that is called samp. Or, if that sant drinks the whole juice and the other santo are still happy, that is also samp.' So, if we want to cultivate the same feeling of samp that you have, what should we do?"

Swamishri: "Follow niyam-dharma with firm conviction. Suhradbhav (fraternity) and samp (unity) will come on their own."

Swamishri revealed that the foundation of samp and suhradbhav lies in the firm observance of niyam-dharma.

title: Swamishri's Birthday Wish
text:
Today, on Swamishri's birthday, Uttamyogi Swami showed him a card that read: "Make a big wish…" Uttamyogi Swami asked, "So, Bapa, what 'big wish' will you make on your birthday? What is your inner desire?"

Swamishri replied, "May all the karyakars (volunteers) become happy through mind, body, and wealth."

Uttamyogi Swami added, "Is this because the Karyakar Suvarna Mahotsav is taking place?"

Swamishri agreed.

"And the devotees, too, right?"

"May they be happy internally and externally," Swamishri added, "Everything is included in that."

On a day when others would expect wishes for themselves, Swamishri's only prayer was for the happiness and well-being of all of his devotees, revealing the depth of his compassion and selflessness.

title: Attending Sabha
text:
During a question-and-answer session, devotees sought guidance from Swamishri regarding attending sabhas.

Question: "Swamishri, these days everything is expensive, and petrol and diesel prices are sky-high. So, if we don't go to mandir or sabha and instead listen to discourses on (online) channels, would that be acceptable?"
Swamishri: "No, that won't do. One must come in person for the mutual darshan (of one another)."

Question: "Bapa! If we go to the railway station and the train has already started, but we catch the last carriage, we still reach our destination. Similarly, if we arrive at the sabha during arti, would that still count as attending the sabha?"
Swamishri: "No, it would not count. An assembly means meeting each other and having direct interaction. In that case, you would be deprived."

Swamishri emphasized that attending sabha in person cannot be replaced by anything else.

title: Smruti & Selfless Love
text:
Accepting the request of the youth of Vidyanagar, Swamishri performed puja at the Vidyanagar chhatralay and then returned to his residence for breakfast. During breakfast, joy was clearly visible on his face.

Seeing this, Vinaypriya Swami asked Swamishri, "Why are you so joyful today?"

Swamishri replied with a radiant smile, "We went to and returned from Vidyanagar." He added, "I was reminded of countless memories of Yogi Bapa."

At 92 years old, traveling from Anand to Vidyanagar could have been exhausting. Yet Swamishri felt no fatigue—only joy. The memories of Yogi Bapa and his deep love for the youth filled him with strength, showing the power of smruti and the selfless love of a true Guru.

title: For the Sake of Others
text:
Today, after cheshta, various topics were being discussed, including Swamishri's meals. At that time, Swamishri remarked, "I don't find anything tasty."

The swamis commented, "Vinaypriya Swami has been bringing new dishes for you these past few days."

Swamishri replied, "I had no idea that he was bringing new things. It all tastes the same to me."

Then Swamishri added, "Whatever I eat, it is only for the sake of others."

In Vachanamrut Gadhada II-55, Shriji Maharaj revealed, "All of My activities are for the sake of the devotees of God; there is not a single activity which I perform for My own personal enjoyment." Swamishri's words reflected this same truth. For him, food was not about taste, but about sustaining the body to serve Bhagwan and His devotees.

title: Tireless Love for Learning
text:
At midnight, Swamishri woke up to use the restroom. At that time, he expressed a desire to read a book on homeopathy.

At 1:38 a.m., the book was brought to him, and he read it intently until 2:38 a.m., searching for a specific medicine. At 2:40 a.m., the lights were turned off, and Swamishri went back to rest.

This simple moment reveals Swamishri's deep passion for reading and learning. Even in the middle of the night, instead of asking someone else to do the task and preserving his own rest, he engaged personally, showing his discipline, focus, and commitment to continuous growth.

title: A Silent Gesture of Respect
text:
During the walking session today, Swamishri was resting while Doctor Mahendrabhai, who currently serves as his doctor, performed a routine check-up. At that moment, an attendant arrived and sat on an empty chair. Once the check-up was complete, Doctor Mahendrabhai stepped aside and stood there, but Swamishri had noticed everything.

Swamishri lovingly looked at the attendant without saying a single word. He folded his hands, silently conveying that the chair should be offered to the doctor. The attendant immediately understood, stood up, and offered the chair. Swamishri was pleased.

Through this quiet gesture, Swamishri not only taught the power of humility and respect without words but also revealed his deep care and regard for those around him.

title: Seeing Bochasan as Divine
text:
After waking in the afternoon, Swamishri had some fruits and soup. The power went out and stayed off for a while. Uttamyogi Swami remarked, "Swami, the power has been out for five minutes and hasn't come back on yet. So what should I consider Bochasan to be?"

Swamishri replied, "Divyā (Divine)."

Uttamyogi Swami asked, "From what [angle] can one consider it divine? It looks just like a village."

Swamishri responded, "[Then you are a] non-believer."

Uttamyogi Swami asked further, "Swami, from what angle do you see Bochasan as divine?"

Swamishri firmly replied, "From all angles."

For Swamishri, Bochasan is divine because it is associated with Maharaj and is therefore equal to Akshardham. To fail to see this greatness is to miss the glory of Bhagwan Himself.

title: Mahārāj is the All-Doer
text:
Swamishri joined a live virtual sabhā with the swamis and volunteers serving in Robbinsville Akshardham.

During the session, Swamishri was asked, "Swami! Whenever we are performing any kind of sevā, what thought should we keep so that we can always experience the bliss of Akshardham?"

Swamishri replied, "Shriji Mahārāj is doing everything; Mahārāj is kartā-hartā (the all-doer). And His power enters us, and only then do we become capable of doing the work. Shriji Mahārāj does everything in all the infinite universes. Mahārāj is also building the Robbinsville Akshardham. If we hold firmly to this strength, we will never face any difficulty on any day."

Swamishri reminded everyone that true bliss in sevā comes from realizing Shriji Mahārāj as the sole doer.

title: It is of Great Value
text:
This evening, a procession was held for the children who had memorized the Satsang Diksha. Swamishri looked at everyone and was very pleased to see the procession. Towards the end of the sabha, a question-and-answer session was held.

Question: "Swami, many children still need to complete their mukhpāth, and only 91 days are left. School has also started, so what should they do now?"
Swamishri: "Get to work. One should get to work, keeping Satsang Diksha as the one goal, because it is of great value."

Question: "Parents often give less importance to mukhpāth and instead prioritize other activities. What should be done then?"
Swamishri: "If they understand the greatness, then Satsang Diksha will remain primary and be given importance. After that, everything else will follow easily."

title: Detached from Status
text:
On this day, Swamishri gave his morning blessings through a question-and-answer session.

Swamishri was asked, "Swami, 13 years ago, Pramukh Swami Maharaj personally wrote a letter entrusting you with the positions of guru and president. Have you ever read this historic letter yourself?"

Swamishri started laughing and replied, "No."

They further asked him, "Did you not feel a desire [in your mind] to read it?"

Swamishri replied with a no and added, "I did not even know where the letter was."

Swamishri's actions reflected profound humility and detachment. For him, becoming guru and president was never about status or recognition, but only about fulfilling Pramukh Swami Maharaj's wish with sincerity, dedication, and service.

title: Bhagwan Does Everything
text:
On this day, Swamishri gave his morning blessings through a question-and-answer session.

A question was asked, "How do you manage the affairs of this organization?"

Swamishri replied, "Bhagwan is there. Bhagwan does everything. He is the doer. If [we] hand it all over to Him, He does everything, and so we have no worries."

They continued, "But you are the one who travels, writes letters, meets with devotees, and endures the hardships. It appears that you are doing everything. What should we understand from this?"

Swamishri responded, "It may appear that way, but it is Bhagwan who is doing it."
