By living in complete surrender, he showed that when everything is placed in Bhagwan's hands, worries dissolve and seva becomes an offering, not a burden.

title: Serving His Gurus
text:
On this day, Swamishri gave his morning blessings through a question-and-answer session.

He was asked, "Shastriji Maharaj had said, 'I was born to build mandirs.' So what were you born for?"

Swamishri humbly replied, "To serve in accordance with my guru's command."

In this simple yet profound answer, Swamishri revealed his unmatched humility and deep guru bhakti. Just as Shastriji Maharaj dedicated his life to mandirs, Swamishri dedicated his entire being to fulfilling his gurus' wishes. His words were a testament to the way he lives—in complete surrender and unwavering service to his gurus.

title: I am a Servant
text:
On this day, Swamishri gave his morning blessings through a question-and-answer session.

He was asked, "In this world, people become very happy when they receive a position. When Pramukh Swami Maharaj appointed you to the positions of president and guru, what did you feel at that time?"

Swamishri replied, "I have never felt that I am the guru or that I have been given such a position. I only feel that I am a servant."

Swamishri's reply revealed the essence of spiritual leadership: true greatness lies in humility. Though entrusted with the responsibility of guiding a global organization, he never saw himself as an authority, but only as a servant of Bhagwan and his guru.

title: The Sanstha's Strength
text:
On this day, Swamishri gave his morning blessings through a question-and-answer session.

Swamishri was asked, "You have lifted this organization, which is like Mount Govardhan. How can we help you support it?"

Swamishri replied, "By keeping Maharaj's āgnā and upāsanā firm."

With this clear guidance, Swamishri taught that the strength of the Sanstha does not rest on one person, but on the collective faith and devotion of all satsangis. To support BAPS is not merely to admire its achievements, but to live by Maharaj's commands and deepen upāsanā in our lives.

title: Not a Minute Earlier
text:
It was time for Swamishri to retire for the night, and he glanced at the clock. It read 9:40 p.m. Seeing this, Swamishri stepped away from his bed and said, "Bring the letters."

The attendant swami replied, "There are no letters."

Hearing this, Swamishri said in an annoyed tone, "What do you mean [there are no letters]?"

The attendant swami explained, "The other swamis are here to assist you and have your darshan. Please retire to sleep so they can go for dinner."

Swamishri sat up more upright and firmly said, "I will stand back up." Another swami added, "Swami, nothing will be read in only 5–10 minutes."

Swamishri responded, "A lot can be read within 5 minutes." Everyone laughed. Despite their efforts, Swamishri sat reading letters until 10:14 p.m.

For him, time was too precious to be spent on himself when it could be used for seva.

title: Concerned for Others
text:
During the evening sabhā, Swamishri was honored by several organizations. Universities from Anand bestowed upon him the title Sanskruti Ke Jyotirdhar. The Dairy Association and other institutions, along with prominent industrialists, also offered their respects.

At the close of the ceremony, Swamishri blessed everyone, saying, "I must ask for your forgiveness because many of you who came today were disabled. Yet, you all endured this hardship. For you, climbing even a single step is like climbing the sky. However, you still came to meet me, and I am truly grateful."

Swamishri had noticed the 10-inch step leading to his cabin. While others focused on his honor, he was concerned only for the discomfort of those with disabilities and the elderly.

title: Asking for Forgiveness First
text:
After the stone consecration ceremony for the Paris mandir, Pujya Ishwarcharan Swami called a ten-year-old child named Yash into the cabin. Because of COVID-19 protocols, Yash, who hadn't worn a mask, had to stand at a distance and did not fully understand why.

Thereafter, Swamishri went for breakfast. When he returned, Swamishri expressed concern that Yash might feel hurt. He instructed the attendants to explain everything and to ask for forgiveness on his behalf. Atmaswarup Swami called Yash and conveyed Swamishri's heartfelt apology. Moved to tears, Yash said, "Bapa, please don't say that. I was the one without a mask."

When asked for his reflection, Yash shared, "I've never seen anything like this in my life, where a guru asks forgiveness from a disciple." Regardless of who was at fault, Swamishri always asked for forgiveness first.

title: Broom!
text:
Today, Swamishri had come to visit the Swaminarayan Nagar. Upon arriving, he blessed the volunteers in the housekeeping department. As he moved forward, he also blessed the volunteers serving in the security department.

At that moment, Swamishri suddenly said, "Broom!" Immediately, the housekeeping volunteers brought one. Sitting in the car, Swamishri took the broom in his hand and swept the ground below him for a short while.

This simple yet profound act showed that for Swamishri, no seva was ever too small. By personally taking part in the same work as the volunteers, he uplifted their efforts and reminded all that true service is rooted in humility, sincerity, and devotion.

title: Connecting With All
text:
After performing his puja, Swamishri returned to his residence from the assembly hall. As he sat down for breakfast, he remarked, "I missed looking at Sarvamangal Swami."

Uttamyogi Swami replied, "We will do it tomorrow."

Swamishri was not pleased with this answer. He gently responded, "Tomorrow, tomorrow, tomorrow—and then it gets left behind." Sensing Swamishri's heartfelt intent, Uttamyogi Swami immediately called Sarvamangal Swami and conveyed, "Swami is saying he missed looking at you." With humility, Sarvamangal Swami answered, "The fact that he remembered me is itself a 'look' for me." Hearing this over speakerphone, Swamishri was overjoyed.

Swamishri's daily practice of connecting with others offers a profound lesson: never postpone small acts of acknowledgment.

title: Honoring Bhagwan First
text:
After Swamishri's morning puja finished, Bhagvatcharan Swami and Yagnasetu Swami came to offer him a farewell garland. In their eagerness, they placed it directly on Swamishri instead of first offering it to Akshar-Purushottam Maharaj.

Swamishri was displeased and gestured toward Akshar-Purushottam Maharaj, indicating the garland should be offered there first.

Even in the simplest acts, Swamishri always directs all honor and devotion to Bhagwan, underscoring the principle that Bhagwan must always remain at the center of all reverence.

title: Absorbed in Devotion
text:
As per the doctors' instructions, Swamishri observes the Ekadashi fast by taking falahar (a non-grain diet) as suits his health. This evening, however, he said, "I am not hungry," and so they performed cheshta first. But as soon as it was over, Swamishri proceeded to go about his nightly routine as usual.

The attendant swamis gently reminded him, "Bapa, you still have to take your falahar." Surprised, Swamishri asked, "It's remaining?" He had completely forgotten about it. Even after being reminded, he showed no interest in eating. Only after the attendants humbly and repeatedly requested him did he agree to take a small portion.

Many may forget devotion while eating, but Swamishri was so absorbed in devotion that he forgot his meal.

title: Attentively Listening
text:
During lunch today, Swamishri suddenly asked, "When Nilkanth Varni arrived in Anand, did they keep Nilkanth Varni there, or did [they] have him leave?" At first, no one understood the context.

Later, everyone recalled that Swamishri listens to Bhagwan Swaminarayan's jivan charitra during his exercise routine. The attendant swamis replayed the audio track. It mentioned, "Nilkanth Varni's mind was not at ease in Anand, so he directly went to Dakor." Swamishri was seeking clarity on whether Nilkanth Varni didn't stay there, or if he wasn't kept there. Adarshjivan Swami then explained, "It's not that he wasn't kept there, but that Nilkanth Varni's mind wasn't settled, so he went to Dakor."

This incident revealed Swamishri's attentiveness and depth of engagement when listening to the life of Bhagwan Swaminarayan.

title: Natural Compassion
text:
This morning, as Swamishri sat for breakfast, a lizard entered the room. Shrutipriya Swami quickly caught it in a plastic container and closed the lid.

Seeing this, Swamishri immediately instructed, "Once you have covered the lizard, release it outside."

This simple incident reflected Swamishri's natural compassion and how he embraces every creature, no matter how small or big, with empathy, love, and care. His response reminds us that true kindness embraces all of Bhagwan's creation.

title: Respect in Every Detail
text:
After waking up in the afternoon, Swamishri had some fruit and then drank soup. After Swamishri was finished, Uttamyogi Swami took the glass from his hand and placed it by the murtis of Akshar-Purushottam Maharaj before going to rinse his mouth.

However, Swamishri immediately gestured to Uttamyogi Swami, indicating that he should move the glass he had placed in front of the murtis. Only after the glass was moved did Swamishri proceed to rinse his mouth.

This simple yet powerful act showed how much reverence Swamishri holds for Bhagwan. Even in the smallest details, his every action reflected honor and respect for Akshar-Purushottam Maharaj.

title: Care in Every Detail
text:
On this day, Swamishri was scheduled to travel from Anand to Himmatnagar at 9:46 a.m. The helicopter took off on time and landed at 10:17 a.m. While in flight, Swamishri expressed concern for the pilots, saying, "Please arrange prasad and meal accommodations for them."

Upon landing in Himmatnagar, Swamishri personally offered prasad to both pilots, after which the swamis prepared a meal for them. Seeing that the pilots were cared for brought Swamishri deep satisfaction.

Though Swamishri speaks few words, his compassion is always expressed through thoughtful action. His quiet attention to others' needs revealed how genuine care transcends position or status.

title: Akshardham is Right Here
text:
During the evening sabha, Swamishri gave his blessings, saying, "The Akshar-Purushottam Upāsanā is spreading—and it will continue to spread in the future. The proclamation of Akshar-Purushottam resounds in all [ten] directions. No matter where you go, it is present in every corner. Therefore, we should always remain in joy — 'Mojmā rahevū, mojmā rahevū, mojmā rahevū re...' Then, for us, Akshardham is right here!"

With satsang and the number of mandirs growing across the world, Swamishri's words remind us that Akshardham is experienced through the joy that comes from realizing the glory of Shri Akshar-Purushottam Maharaj.

title: An Observant Eye
text:
After completing his evening exercise session, Swamishri remarked, "Dr. Mahendrabhai's walking is like an American's." With a smile, he then added, "American gait." The word gait means "a person's manner of walking."

Vednayan Swami curiously asked, "When did you see Mahendrabhai's walking?"

Swamishri gently replied, "I see it every day."

This simple yet striking exchange reveals Swamishri's remarkable attentiveness and precision — observing even the smallest details and expressing them with thoughtful clarity through accurate words.

title: Bhagwan First, Always
text:
During the evening sabha, as part of the welcoming, Nirmalcharan Swami approached to place a chandlo made of sandalwood on Swamishri's forehead. Just as he was about to apply it, Swamishri pointed toward Thakorji and said, "First, perform the pujan of Akshar-Purushottam Maharaj."

Only after this was done did he allow the chandlo to be placed on his forehead.

Through this simple yet profound act, Swamishri demonstrated how Bhagwan must always remain at the center of every action. Even in moments of personal honor, his first thought was of Maharaj and Swami. His life reminds us that true devotion means never letting Bhagwan become secondary.

title: The Spirit of True Seva
text:
After waking up in the afternoon, Swamishri took a bath. When some time passed, his attendant, Uttamyogi Swami, entered the bathroom and was astonished to see Swamishri cleaning the toilet. He immediately stopped him and asked, "Swami, why were you cleaning? There was no such need [for you] to do this."

Swamishri smiled gently and replied, "Seva… swayamsevak (volunteer)! [I] have to do this someday."

Even as the guru and at an advanced age, Swamishri humbly performed seva with a pure heart and no sense of status. Swamishri's deep belief was that true seva is not about position, but about selflessness and humility.

title: Attaining Akshardham
text:
After performing puja and giving darshan to devotees from North America, Swamishri was offered a garland made of roses representing all those who had completed the adhiveshan. Following this, Swamishri engaged in a question-and-answer session based on a letter he had written.

Adarshjivan Swami asked, "You wrote, 'I have noted the people who are doing mukhpath.' What does it mean when you say you have noted them?"
Swamishri replied, "The mukhpath has reached Shriji Maharaj."

Adarshjivan Swami then asked, "What benefit will those people receive?"
Swamishri said, "They will attain Akshardham."

Adarshjivan Swami continued, "But our situation is such that we don't experience the bliss of Akshardham. What should we do?"
Swamishri answered, "By practicing niyam-dharma, bhakti, and satsang honestly."

title: Do Revision
text:
Continuing the question-and-answer session for the North American devotees, Adarshjivan Swami asked, "You wrote that everyone's effort should not go to waste and that we should do revision. But since our mukhpath is on our phones, we logically think: what is the need for revision?"

Swamishri said, "Lock your logic and focus on following the agna; do revision."

Adarshjivan Swami asked, "How can we maintain faith and enthusiasm for revision?"
Swamishri replied, "By understanding the mahima of this agna."

Adarshjivan Swami then asked, "If we do revision, how do you stay with us?"
Swamishri said, "By following agna, your mind stays with me."

In this way, Swamishri showered his blessings upon all devotees of North America.

title: My Heart Overflows with Joy
text:
After performing puja and giving darshan to the youth of North America, Swamishri was informed of their sincere efforts for the adhiveshan. He then joyfully interacted with them through various virtual activities. Upon hearing about the dedication of the balaks and balikas, Swamishri chose a topic for them to recite shlokas on.

He then blessed everyone, saying, "By doing mukhpath with sincerity, one earns the Satpurush's inner rajipo. When I hear that all of you have done mukhpath, my heart overflows with joy."

Thereafter, referring to a line from his letter where he had emphasized revision three times, the youth asked, "How many shlokas should we revise daily?" Swamishri smiled and personally selected the option of 15 shlokas per day. Finally, Swamishri lifted a cupcake and lovingly offered it, symbolically feeding all the youth.

title: The Benefits of Mukhpath
text:
Continuing with the adhiveshan sabha, Swamishri was informed of the efforts of the kishores and kishoris. Then he was asked, "Swamishri, what is the true benefit of doing mukhpath?"

Swamishri replied, "There are three benefits of doing mukhpath. First, by doing mukhpath, one receives immense rajipo. Yogi Bapa becomes very, very pleased. [Second], by reflecting and contemplating on what we recite, our heart becomes purified. Instead of filling it with unnecessary garbage, when we fill it with the divine words of Maharaj, Swami, and the Guru Parampara, our inner self becomes content—what could be greater than that? [And third], when the words of mukhpath become realized within, your heart itself becomes Akshardham. Everything becomes one—there remains no separation."

title: I am Akshar
text:
Continuing with the adhiveshan sabha, Swamishri was informed of the efforts of the yuvaks and yuvatis.

He was then asked, "Swamishri, who are you? What is your true form?"

Swamishri simply replied, "I am Akshar."

When asked which jivan charitra (biography) of our gurus the youth should read to truly understand and draw closer to the Satpurush, Swamishri selected Yogiji Maharaj's Jivan Charitra.

He was then asked, "How many pages should we read daily?" Swamishri chose the option of three pages per day. At the conclusion of the session, Swamishri was lovingly garlanded. With a gentle smile, he placed his hands together in the shape of a heart—blessing all the youth with his love and affection.

title: Every Moment Is Seva
text:
During a discussion, Gurumanan Swami, Swamishri's attendant who assists with responding to devotees' letters, light-heartedly asked, "We 'attack' you from every direction in your every free second—sometimes through letters, WhatsApp messages, phone calls, and even our questions. So, have you ever felt frustrated or angry?"

Swamishri smiled and replied, "Divya (divine), divya, divya!"

Gurumanan Swami asked again, "Have you ever felt bored or wished for time for yourself?"

Swamishri responded, "Never! Just as there is seva in the kitchen, seva for washing dishes, or any other seva, this too is seva."

Swamishri's divine outlook and selfless devotion transformed every action into loving service. He viewed all correspondence and conversations not as interruptions, but as sacred opportunities to serve Bhagwan and His devotees.

title: The Greatest Wealth
text:
On the auspicious day of Dhanteras, Swamishri performed the pujan rituals on behalf of all devotees. Thereafter, he offered his divine blessings, saying, "Today is the auspicious day of Dhanteras. Though there are many 'teras' days, this one is special. On Dhanteras, whatever we sincerely pray to Bhagwan for, we receive. But the greatest wealth of all belongs to those who have true nishtha (faith). One who possesses true nishtha possesses mountains of wealth. As it is said, 'Re Shyam, tame sachu nanu… biju sarve kshanbhangur kachu' (O Shyam, You are the only true treasure; everything else is temporary and fleeting)."

Through his words, Swamishri revealed that the ultimate treasure in life is not material wealth, but Bhagwan Himself.

title: The 'One'
text:
When Swamishri arrived at his room to retire for the night, the clock on the wall flashed 11:11:11. Pleased upon seeing the time, Swamishri smiled and said, "The '1' was not coming in hand. Where did the '1' come from?" Then sharing his deeper reflection, Swamishri said: "'1' means Purushottam Narayan! '2' means Akshar and Purushottam. '3' means Dham, Dhami, and Mukta. '4' means Dham, Dhami, Mukta, and Haribhakto! '5' means Jiva, Ishwar, Maya, Brahma, and Parabrahma — everything is included in that!"

It was the first time he saw 11:11:11, symbolizing Purushottam Narayan — the One beyond all. Through something as simple as the numbers on a clock, Swamishri revealed his ever-present awareness of Bhagwan.

title: The True Light of Diwali
text:
On the occasion of Diwali and the New Year, beautiful floral arches were artistically arranged along Swamishri's route to his room, illuminated with glowing electric lights. As the attendant swami began to wheel Swamishri through the decorated path, he suddenly and eagerly said, "Akshar-Purushottam Maharaj?!"

The attendant replied, "They have already departed." Yet, with deep yearning, Swamishri repeated again, "Akshar-Purushottam Maharaj!" Sensing his strong desire, the attendants immediately brought a murti and placed it in his hands. The moment he held it, a smile blossomed on his face.

Even amidst grand celebrations, Swamishri's heart sought only the presence of Bhagwan. True joy comes from the inner light of Bhagwan within us.

title: The Power of Asking Forgiveness
text:
After breakfast, as Swamishri entered the dining area, he noticed Digantbhai Sadhak standing nearby. Upon seeing him, Swamishri said warmly, "Digant, sorry." His words surprised Digantbhai and the attendant swamis, who wondered why Swamishri was apologizing.

Swamishri then explained, "[I] had that [shawl] removed because it was not proper, that is why." Earlier that morning, for the Annakut, Digantbhai had placed a shawl on the sofa to ensure Swamishri wouldn't feel cold. However, Swamishri had the shawl removed, as he didn't find it quite right. Though the act was small, it had remained on his mind, and that is why he apologized.

Even though he is the guru, his humility in asking for forgiveness reflected a heart free of ego and filled with genuine love for others.

title: Blessings
text:
To Swami Bapa's Beloved Youth,

Sadhu Keshavjivandas's heartfelt Jai Swaminarayan greetings on this New Year. My prayers are that all of you progress in your studies, married lives, and Satsang.

"Believe my words to be me. Whoever follows my words understanding this, I remain with them through the form of my words." (Purushottam Bolya Prite)

In this way, may all of you live by these agnas to attain Ekantik Dharma and may you experience happiness through your body, mind, and wealth — this is my ashirwad.

HAPPY DIWALI
&
HAPPY NEW YEAR

title: Please Forgive Me
text:
As Swamishri's health was in a weak state, he was receiving treatment at Yogiji Maharaj Hospital. During this night, when his sleep was disturbed, he noticed the attendant swamis were still awake. Seeing this, he apologized, "Everyone, please forgive me. I am causing all of you trouble."

The attendant swamis immediately responded, "No, no, Swami."

Even in a moment of personal discomfort, Swamishri's heart overflowed with humility and concern for others. Despite his frail condition, his first thought was not of himself, but of those serving him. His simple words, "Please forgive me," reflected the essence of true greatness: a heart that remains humble, compassionate, and selfless in every circumstance.

title: The True Mark of a Leader
text:
Swamishri was traveling by plane from Mehsana to Jodhpur. During the flight, Brahmavihari Swami asked Swamishri, "What should a world leader be like?"

Swamishri thoughtfully replied, "One who gives peace to everyone."

Then, he added, "Everything else can be found—but peace is not [easily] found."

Swamishri's words revealed the essence of true leadership: to bring peace, not just progress. In a world filled with achievement and ambition, he reminded all that the highest form of success is creating peace—in oneself, and in the hearts of others.

title: The Essence of True Unity
text:
On the occasion of Samp Din (Day of Unity), Swamishri explained, "Samp is a very subtle and delicate thing. Samp is not merely about everyone gathering and making noise. For true samp, the mind and body—everything—must merge."

He then outlined the principles of samp: "The first principle of samp: to look for and correct the faults within ourselves. The second principle of samp: to not keep any expectations. Do not expect whether the other person maintains samp or not; however, you must maintain samp. If your attitude is, 'I will maintain samp only if the other person does,' then problems occur and things will fall apart."

Through his words, Swamishri revealed that true unity is not dependent on others but begins within ourselves.

title: Respect for Others
text:
Today, Dinbandhu Swami, the kothari of the Dhari mandir, came to Swamishri with some rice. The devotees in Dhari were to be served dudhpak in the coming days. His intention was to have Swamishri sanctify the rice, which would then be added to the dudhpak, thus making the entire dish sanctified.

Swamishri duly touched and blessed the rice. Afterward, Dinbandhu Swami bowed down to receive Swamishri's blessings. At that moment, Swamishri first wiped his hands—which had just touched the rice—and then he placed his hand on Dinbandhu Swami's head.

Who else would have such subtle awareness? Truly, such an action is only possible for one who has such immense respect and mahima for others.

title: Bhagwan's Living Presence
text:
During a question-and-answer session with children, Swamishri lovingly explained how Bhagwan accepts prayers and remains ever-present.

Question: "Swami, my grandmother told me that Bhagwan is in the murti, but this murti doesn't walk, so how can Bhagwan be in it?"
Swamishri: "Bhagwan is present [in the murti], so He can do as He pleases. Even if He doesn't speak, He still resides there."

Question: "When we have a problem and we pray to you, does it reach you?"
Swamishri: "Yes, it reaches me."

Question: "How do you listen to it?"
Swamishri: "Bhagwan is present in every part of our being and in every atom. That is how He hears."

Through these simple yet profound answers, Swamishri revealed that Bhagwan is not distant but ever-present.

title: Making Time for Sabha
text:
During a question-and-answer session with children, Swamishri lovingly guided them on how to balance school and satsang.

Question: "Swami, we have so much homework that we don't get any time. So how can we go to bal sabha?"
Swamishri: "If you have mahima, you will definitely make it. [You will find a way to] jump and get there!"

Swamishri's words reminded the children that where there is true mahima and love for satsang, time will never be an obstacle. When our priorities are rooted in faith, we naturally find the strength and determination to make space for what truly matters.

title: Courage and Gratitude
text:
During a question-and-answer session with children, Swamishri lovingly encouraged them to remain steadfast and fearless in their devotion to Bhagwan.

Question: "Our friends tease us a lot for applying the tilak chandlo. Should we still do tilak chandlo or not?"
Swamishri: "You must do it. Even if you face difficulties, be brave and apply the tilak chandlo."

Question: "Why should we perform the tap ni mala?"
Swamishri: "Bhagwan performed immense austerities and endured great hardships for us. As a small symbol of that, we should do the tap ni mala. Bhagwan has already done so much for us, but when we do tap ni mala, He values it deeply and accepts it."

Through his words, Swamishri reminded the children that true devotion requires both courage and gratitude.

title: Becoming an Adarsh Child
text:
During a question-and-answer session with children, Swamishri lovingly explained the importance of living with discipline, respect, and sincere effort.

Question: "Swamis tell us to become adarsh (ideal) children. What should we do to become an adarsh child?"
Swamishri: "To become an adarsh child, you must follow all the niyams given by Bhagwan. And even if you cannot follow all of the niyams right now, you must lean towards the mindset that, 'I must follow all the niyams.'"

Question: "Why should we bow down to our parents?"
Swamishri: "They are older than us, and they nurture and support us in every way. That is why we should [bow down to them]."

True ideals are not achieved overnight but are built through daily effort, humility, and gratitude.

title: Studying with Effort
text:
During a question-and-answer session with children, Swamishri gave simple yet powerful guidance to help them stay focused and disciplined in their studies.

Question: "My mind doesn't stay focused on my studies. What should I do?"
Swamishri: "If you study hard and become prepared, you will become a great professional, and everything else will fall into place. But if you only play games and neglect your studies, you will spoil yourself."

Question: "I feel very lazy about studying."
Swamishri: "This is the time in life to study, so you must study. Set aside your laziness and study."

Swamishri reminded the children that hard work and discipline are the foundation of success.

title: The Constant Bliss of Prapti
text:
Today, after brushing his teeth, Swamishri said aloud, "Prapti," and then made a disapproving face.

Seeing this, Uttamyogi Swami asked, "Swami, what do you mean?"

Swamishri replied, "We have attained such great prapti, yet you still make a gloomy face."

Uttamyogi Swami then said, "So you mean we should remain happy in the morning?"

Swamishri clarified, "Not just in the morning — you should remain happy for all 24 hours."

Swamishri reminded everyone that true bliss lies in constant awareness of our divine prapti — the priceless attainment of Bhagwan and the Satpurush. When one lives with this understanding, every moment becomes filled with peace and joy.

title: Eagerness for Sabha
text:
Today was Shastriji Maharaj's Smruti Parva. When Swamishri went to rest in the afternoon, he asked, "What is the program for this evening?"
Uttamyogi Swami replied, "There is a sabha in the evening."

Swamishri then asked, "What is the program for the sabha?"
Uttamyogi Swami described the program, mentioning that there would be a play about Hiramukhi.

With eagerness, Swamishri asked, "Will we have to go early to watch the Hiramukhi play?"
Uttamyogi Swami replied, "No, it's not like that. They will begin the Hiramukhi play after you arrive."

Swamishri's enthusiasm for hearing and reliving the divine incidents of Shastriji Maharaj and his devotees never waned.

title: The Joy of Contentment
text:
Tonight, after dinner, Uttamyogi Swami said to Swamishri, "Before, there used to be mangoes in the dish prepared for you, but for the last few days, there haven't been any. Is that okay with you?"

With complete contentment, Swamishri replied, "It doesn't matter even if nothing comes." Then he added, "If nothing comes, that is the best."

Vinaypriya Swami then explained, "The mango season is over now, so good mangoes aren't available."

To this, Swamishri said, "There is no need for it."

Vinaypriya Swami then asked, "If I don't bring anything, you would still be pleased, right?"

Swamishri gently affirmed, "Yes."

For him, true joy came not from sensory pleasures but from inner peace and contentment in Bhagwan.

title: The True Essence of Unity
text:
During the evening Bal Din sabha, Swamishri was asked, "Swami, what should we do to maintain samp (unity) with each other?"

Swamishri wrote his answer: "First, one must make firm in the mind that 'I want to keep samp.' Then, one must endure hardships, set aside personal desires, tolerate, and adapt to others."

Through these few words, Swamishri beautifully defined true unity — it is built not on comfort, but on humility, tolerance, and selflessness. When we consciously set aside our own wishes for the good of others, true samp naturally flourishes.

title: Seeing Devotion
text:
Around 11:00 a.m., Swamishri arrived for darshan at the Prarthana Mandir. Although it was Ekadashi, his designated rest day, many devotees had gathered in the hall, eager for his darshan.

After giving darshan to everyone, Munivandan Swami showed Swamishri a small drawing of him made by a young child. Despite its simplicity, Swamishri saw the child's heartfelt devotion in the drawing and was deeply pleased. Then, Munivandan Swami gestured for the child to stand up and directed Swamishri's attention toward him.

However, as a glass partition stood between them, Swamishri lifted his hand above his eyes to see the child clearly and personally bless him.

Swamishri's gesture revealed his divine vision — he never looks at a person's age, skill, or status, but at the sincerity of their heart.

title: A Timeless Connection
text:
During personal meetings, a youth named Janak Jadav came to meet Swamishri and said, "Swami, you have been to my house."

Swamishri immediately replied, "At 11 o'clock."

Curious, the swamis asked, "At night?"

Swamishri shook his head no, indicating it was 11 a.m.

After inquiring further, they discovered that Swamishri had visited the youth's house in 2004. Even after fourteen years, Swamishri remembered not only the home but also the exact time of the padharamni.

Swamishri's perfect recall was not mere memory — it reflected his deep, lasting love and personal connection with every devotee.

title: Sharpness and Care
text:
Today, Swamishri arrived in Mehsana from Himmatnagar.

At night, as Vednayan Swami came while Swamishri was retiring to bed, Swamishri said, "You should take the welcoming ladoo (sweet)."

It was then realized that during dinner, when all of the attendants had come to Swamishri to take their ladoos, Vednayan Swami had not. Even after the fatigue from a long three-hour journey, Swamishri had remembered this detail and made a mental note.

Even at 92 years of age, Swamishri's alertness and attention to others reveal his extraordinary mindfulness and deep, personal love for everyone around him.

title: Keeping Divinity
text:
During the afternoon discourse, Swamishri participated in an English question-and-answer session.

Question: "In your divine words, can you please tell us one thing that we [should] remember every day to help us come closer to you?"
Swamishri: "Keep divinity amongst each other. Maharaj and Swami will be raji (pleased), and we will be more pleased."

Question: "What is constantly on your mind?"
Swamishri: "Divinity amongst each other. In that, Maharaj, Swami, [and all the] muktos [are] all pleased."

Swamishri's simple yet powerful message reminds us that true spiritual progress begins in how we see and treat one another. By seeing divinity in everyone, we cultivate harmony, humility, and the joy of pleasing Maharaj and Swami.

title: Thinking of Swamishri
text:
During the afternoon discourse, Swamishri participated in an English question-and-answer session.

Question: "Do you ever think about us?"
Swamishri: "Yes, many times. Not once, but many times. You are all divine persons — not ordinary, and not people of this world."

Question: "How can we always think about you?"
Swamishri: "You think of Maharaj and Swami, and I am included in it."

Then the swamis prayed to Swamishri, "May our minds stay on you."
Swamishri replied, "If your mind stays on Maharaj, it means your mind stays on me."

Through his words, Swamishri revealed the oneness between himself and Bhagwan. When we keep our minds on Maharaj and Swami, we remain forever connected to Swamishri.

title: True Refuge in God
text:
During the afternoon discourse, Swamishri participated in an English question-and-answer session.

Question: "What is true ashro (refuge in Bhagwan)?"
Swamishri: "Except God, nothing is there for a devotee."

Question: "Swami! You are our true friend. You can see our khamis (shortcomings), so please tell us what we need to improve on?"
Swamishri: "Except God, nothing exists for us. We are all in brahmakoti. So our friendship will forever remain."

Swamishri's words remind us that true refuge lies only in Bhagwan. When we anchor our hearts in Him, every relationship and purpose finds eternal meaning — for in Bhagwan alone, all bonds and friendships become everlasting.

title: he Strength of True Refuge
text:
During the afternoon discourse, Swamishri participated in an English question-and-answer session.

Question: "Out of your krupa (compassion), you have told us your true identity many times, but we do not understand your swaroop (divine form) in the way we should. We don't fully realize our immense prapti (attainment). So, Swami, please give us one prapti nu pad which we can sing and do manan (reflect) upon daily."

Swamishri: "Keep firm refuge in Shriji Maharaj — there is nothing else besides this, nothing else."

Then, giving the kirtan, Swamishri said, "Bhāgya jagyā re āj janavā…"

Swamishri reminded everyone that realizing prapti begins with steadfast faith — holding firmly to the refuge of Shriji Maharaj alone.

title: The Note of Humility
text:
As on every morning, before Swamishri began eating his breakfast, Madhurvadan Swami started reciting the shlok "Shrimad sadgun shalinam…" and everyone joined in. But just as soon as the shlok concluded, Swamishri held the lobes of his ears. Why?

Swamishri explained, "Yesterday, when you (Madhurvadan Swami) recited the shlok, you were probably correct, but I felt like it was slightly off [note]."

Madhurvadan Swami immediately replied, "No, Swami! What you said was exactly right. When I sang the 'Aum,' I descended due to old habits, but the moment I realized, I brought the scale back up, and you noticed it."

Though the error was not his, he was the first to reflect and take responsibility. Through this moment, Swamishri taught that true greatness lies not in perfection, but in humility.

title: The True Honor
text:
In the afternoon, regarding a kirtan sung during Swamishri's puja, Gurumanan Swami asked, "Swami, one verse in the kirtan said, 'Even giving honors of sapphire is not enough.' You are the present form of Pramukh Swami Maharaj, so tell us - how should Pramukh Swami Maharaj and you be honored?"

Swamishri replied, "By following dharma and niyam. Staying firm in dharma and niyam — they should be firm."

Gurumanan Swami then asked, "So that is true honor?"

Swamishri nodded and said, "Yes."

Swamishri taught that the truest way to honor the Guru is not through praise or gifts, but by living with discipline, purity, and obedience to dharma and niyam. True devotion is expressed through action.

title: Discipline Beyond Time
text:
Swamishri had traveled from Gandhinagar to Dar es Salaam. Before reciting the cheshta, a discussion took place for 49 minutes. The swamis then said, "Let's go, now we should get up." However, Swamishri continued to sit. Priyavrat Swami gently said, "We know you don't want to get up but…"

Swamishri interrupted, "It is still 8 p.m.!"

The swamis replied, "But Swami, it's 10:30 p.m. in India. Let's remove this clock from your room. Only then will you get proper rest."

Smiling, Swamishri said, "No, no, I will find it [even if you remove it]."

After some more conversation, Swamishri finally said, "Let's go." When he retired to sleep, it was 9:39 p.m. — 12:09 a.m. India time. Even across time zones and fatigue, Swamishri remained unwavering in his routine.

title: Dāsnā Dās
text:
In the afternoon, after Swamishri completed his lunch, a discussion took place in which he recalled a verse and said, "Whoever becomes a dās nā dās (a servant of a servant) in satsang…"

Santcharit Swami completed the verse and added, "...I will consider his devotion as good."

Pleased, Swamishri said, "Say the entire verse." Santcharit Swami then sang the full couplet: "Dāsnā dās thaīne, valī je rahe satasangmā; Bhakti tenī bhalī mānīsh, rāchīsh tenā rangmā."

Swamishri then explained, "Do you want to be connected with Maharaj? Then this is it. To remain engrossed means the devotee never leaves Maharaj, and Maharaj never leaves the devotee — as long as he keeps humility."

Swamishri explained how humility is the foundation of an unbreakable bond with Maharaj.

title: Zeal for Darshan
text:
Today was Shastriji Maharaj's smruti parva. It was already 9:06 p.m., and Swamishri was supposed to return to his room, recite the cheshta, take a shower, and complete his nightly routine. However, instead of walking toward his room, Swamishri began walking outside. The attendant swamis gently reminded, "Swami, this way. We have to go inside the room."

Swamishri immediately replied, "Darshan."

It was late, and going for darshan would delay his schedule further, but Swamishri did not want to miss the opportunity to do darshan of Shastriji Maharaj on such an auspicious day. The swamis quickly made preparations, and Swamishri joyfully performed darshan.

Despite the late hour, Swamishri chose darshan over convenience.

title: The One Thought
text:
Around 4:30 p.m., Swamishri was sitting on the sofa in his room when Uttamyogi Swami asked, "Swami, what thought do you constantly have for 24 hours?"

Swamishri replied, "Devotees."

To confirm, Uttamyogi Swami asked, "All 24 hours?"

Swamishri said, "Yes."

He then asked, "But what do you think about the devotees?"

Swamishri responded, "To meet them, give them blessings, wish for their benefit, and think about their moksha."

Uttamyogi Swami asked, "You don't think of anything else?"

Swamishri answered, "No."

Swamishri's mind is constantly absorbed in the well-being and spiritual progress of all of his devotees.

title: The Harm of Finding Faults
text:
While Swamishri was resting briefly during his walking session, an attendant swami asked, "What happens when one takes abhav-avgun (finds faults in others)?"

Swamishri replied, "First of all, Shriji Maharaj does not like it… and second thing, the soul of the person taking abhav-avgun gets completely destroyed, and he is not at peace at heart."

Swamishri's words make it clear: finding faults in others not only displeases Shriji Maharaj, but it also destroys our inner peace and weakens our spiritual progress. Conversely, he guides us to focus on the virtues of others to strengthen our devotion and foster a positive outlook.

title: The Highest Level
text:
After completing his breakfast, a discussion took place in which Swamishri said, "Maharaj has said, 'Even the worldly tasks of devotees are divine.' And Yogi Bapa has shown it. In Pondicherry, he performed dandavats and pradakshina to the belongings of devotees in the train!"

Atmaswarup Swami responded, "It is a very high level!"

Swamishri replied, "Here, we are talking about the highest level. These are talks about moksha. Even 99% is not enough. If even 1% is missing, it will not work. 100 out of 100% is required. If all four — dharma, gnan, vairagya, and bhakti — are there, and none are hollow, then one truly attains Bhagwan. These four are like the walls, and Bhagwan is enclosed within them."

The journey to moksha requires total sincerity and completeness.

title: Deep Reverence
text:
After doing darshan in Yogiji Maharaj's room, Swamishri proceeded to the Aksharderi. From there, he went upstairs for darshan in the mandir and then to Yogiji Maharaj's Smruti Mandir. It was there that Swamishri expressed his wish to touch the feet of Yogiji Maharaj's murti.

The attendant swamis helped him stand and guided him inside so he could fulfill this heartfelt wish. After touching Yogiji Maharaj's feet, Swamishri also touched the feet of Shri Akshar-Purushottam Maharaj.

Then, looking at Yogiji Maharaj's murti, Swamishri gestured "nice" with his hands and said, "The murti of Yogiji Maharaj is made exactly like Yogiji Maharaj himself."

His desire to offer physical reverence, even at personal effort, revealed the sincerity of his love.

title: The Fundamental Scripture
text:
This afternoon, after waking up, Swamishri was informed that, in Sarangpur, the sadhaks in the Bhagatji Maharaj class were beginning their study of the Vachanamrut and were seeking his blessings for this occasion.

While offering his blessings, Swamishri said, "The Vachanamrut is a great scripture and it is our fundamental scripture, so study it carefully and thoroughly. Everything is encompassed within the Vachanamrut. The study of all scriptures is included within the Vachanamrut."

With just a few heartfelt words, Swamishri emphasized the unmatched importance of the Vachanamrut. His guidance reminded all of us that sincere, focused study of this scripture can lead to deep understanding, spiritual clarity, and a complete foundation for progressing on the path toward Bhagwan.

title: The Lowest in Satsang
text:
Around 5:30 p.m. in the evening, Swamishri entered the bathroom. On the whiteboard inside, he read a question: "In this satsang, who is considered the lowest?"

Without hesitation, Swamishri replied, "The one who takes abhav-avgun (sees faults in others)."

With just a few words, Swamishri revealed a profound truth: in satsang, the one who constantly finds flaws in others lowers themselves the most. His response teaches that avoiding abhav-avgun is essential for inner peace, spiritual progress, and harmony in satsang. True elevation comes from seeing good in others.

title: Effortless Care
text:
Before Swamishri would retire to bed, the doctor serving him would perform a routine nightly medical checkup. On this particular day, Dr. Koradia had come and was standing nearby.

Immediately noticing this, Swamishri humbly requested, "Please sit in the chair."

Even while being cared for, Swamishri's first instinct was to care for others. His simple request reflected a heart that naturally prioritizes the comfort, dignity, and well-being of everyone around him. True greatness, as Swamishri showed, is expressed not through authority or position, but through quiet, effortless compassion.

title: Fill Akshar Everywhere
text:
After dinner, Swamishri returned to his room. Two swamis had come to ask what devotees should name their new shops.

The first swami asked, and Swamishri replied, "Akshar."
The second swami asked the same question, and again Swamishri answered, "Akshar!"
Then Swamishri added with emphasis, "Fill Akshar everywhere… Akshar, Akshar, Akshar."

Swamishri revealed his deep and unwavering devotion and advocacy to the principle of Akshar-Purushottam, just like Shastriji Maharaj. His repeated and strong insistence on the name "Akshar" reflected his desire for our lives to be rooted in becoming one with Akshar, the servant of Purushottam.

title: Boundless Love for All
text:
Swamishri had expressed his wish to perform the pujan of a cow.

That afternoon, after waking up, Swamishri was taken outside where a young calf named Uttara awaited him. Uttara was blessed with extraordinary fortune as Swamishri gently placed his hand on her head, applied a sandalwood chandlo, offered rice grains, placed a flower upon her, and lovingly performed her puja. He then fed her a bundle of grass with great affection.

Sensing his pure love, Uttara rested her head on Swamishri's lap—an unexpected moment that surprised everyone except Swamishri himself, who remained completely calm and compassionate.

Swamishri's gentle interaction with Uttara reflected his deep love and care for all beings, seeing divinity in every life, big or small.

title: Run with Determination
text:
During a morning question-and-answer session, Swamishri offered guidance to children working hard to fulfill his wish for 10,000 children to memorize the Satsang Diksha.

Question: "Only 15 days remain for Mission Rajipo, and many have reached only 200 shloks. What should we keep in sight so that the mukpath can be fully completed?"
Swamishri: "You must create the same feeling that you are running as if a tiger is chasing you—then it will be done."

Question: "We have memorized all 315 shloks once, but when we recite them for the examiner, they get mixed up. What should be done?"
Swamishri: "It is still raw; it has not been fully perfected. But since they are children, it is forgivable. Still, this is a task given to you, so you must complete it by any means possible."

title: The Art of Love
text:
After breakfast, some artwork prepared for Swamishri's birthday had been placed near the basin. Swamishri noticed it from a distance and said, "I want to see it."

A swami gently insisted, "It's late, Swami. Please go for rest now, and we'll see it later." But Swamishri again asked for it to be brought.

To accommodate his wish, a swami took photos of two pieces of artwork and showed them to Swamishri on the phone. Swamishri was very pleased. Immediately after, he said, "Two more are remaining." He had noticed that two pieces had not been shown yet.

A swami reassured him, "We will see those later." But Swamishri said, "No, I want to see them right now." So the remaining pictures were shown to him.

His insistence showed that what mattered most to him was not the art itself, but the love behind it.

title: Becoming Nirmani
text:
In the afternoon, before lunch, Dr. Golakiya asked during a discussion, "How can one become nirmani (egoless)?"

Swamishri responded, "Only if one understands the greatness of Bhagwan can one become nirmani; otherwise, it is not possible. If a person truly realizes, 'Bhagwan is so great,' then one can become nirmani. Without that [understanding], it is not possible."

Dr. Golakiya then asked, "What should we do to understand Bhagwan's mahima?"

Swamishri replied, "Listen to katha-varta and listen to the divine incidents of Maharaj. Since Maharaj lived completely without ego, reflecting on His actions is a source of powerful inspiration."

Swamishri explained that true egolessness arises from realizing Bhagwan's immense greatness.

title: Choosing Others' First
text:
After Swamishri finished his dinner, the attendant Vinaypriya Swami recalled an incident and said, "Swami, when you were a sadguru sant, I was fortunate to get opportunities to perform your seva. Once, I sat down to feed you. I separated the soft, desirable layers from the middle of the rotlo and served them to you. After you finished eating, you finally said, 'I eat the hard edges (the less desirable parts).'"

Hearing this, Uttamyogi Swami asked, "What is the reason behind you always telling us these things at the end?"

Swamishri replied, "So no one becomes distressed."

This moment revealed Swamishri's extraordinary compassion and adaptability. He consistently chooses others' comfort over his own, so that no one feels hurt or burdened.

title: Love for the Scholars
text:
Today, Swamishri was writing a letter for the revered scholars who had memorized the Satsang Diksha when water began running from his nose. Despite this discomfort, he did not pause or set the letter aside. Instead, he continued writing with one hand while wiping his nose with the other. He worked this way for nearly 30 minutes.

Even through a physical ailment, Swamishri showed extraordinary dedication and an unwavering desire to honor and please the revered scholars.

Swamishri's actions echoed deep love as he continued writing out of respect, choosing to endure his own discomfort so he could wholeheartedly honor their efforts and devotion.

title: Absorbed in Bhajan
text:
Swamishri did not sleep well that afternoon, so he woke up early. Then Swamishri said, "How much [to] sleep, sleep, sleep!"

After that, Swamishri gestured to begin writing letters. As Swamishri started writing, Uttamyogi Swami asked, "Swami, since you couldn't sleep, what did you do?"
Swamishri replied, "Bhajan. Swaminarayan... Swaminarayan…"

Uttamyogi Swami then asked, "Don't you get bored after a while?"
Swamishri gently gestured toward him and, in a deep mood, said, "What is there to get bored of?"

Uttamyogi Swami continued, "Instead of just chanting, didn't you feel like doing some vichar?"
Swamishri replied, "The thoughts are ongoing."

For him, remembrance of Bhagwan was neither boring nor repetitive—it was a source of constant joy, peace, and purpose.

title: The Power of Pure Intent
text:
At 11:04 a.m., the airplane lifted into the sky toward Delhi. A devotee asked Swamishri, "When we do mansi, does it reach you?"

Swamishri smiled and replied, "Yes!"

The devotee asked again, "But how can we know?"

Swamishri answered, "Pure intent (meaning whatever is done with pure intent reaches him)."

Swamishri then lovingly wrote his blessings: "If one's heart is pure, regardless of how big or small one's financial or mental seva is, Maharaj, Swami, and Pramukh Swami Maharaj will accept it all. Just like [Maharaj accepted] the thirteen coins offered by Dubli Bhatt."

Swamishri reinforced how true connection with Bhagwan and the Guru is built on purity of heart.

title: Perfection in Devotion
text:
Swamis recalled a memory from 2011, when Swamishri had previously visited Jaipur. It had been very late one night, and due to the delay, everyone recited the cheshta quickly. At the time, Swamishri remained silent and allowed the entire cheshta to finish.

Only after they finished the cheshta did he express his displeasure. He then instructed everyone to recite the full cheshta again—this time slowly, properly, and with full devotion.

It was only after they completed the cheshta calmly and reverently that Swamishri retired for rest.

Swamishri's unwavering insistence on re-reciting the cheshta revealed a profound principle: true devotion is expressed through care, presence, and sincerity—not haste.

title: Performing Seva
text:
Swamis recalled a memory from 2007, when Swamishri had previously visited Jaipur. It was the occasion of Jaipur Mandir's patotsav (anniversary celebration). At that time, an abhishek was performed on all the murtis in the inner sanctum.

During the ceremony, Swamishri personally picked up a wiper and began cleaning the floor of the inner sanctuary. In doing so, Swamishri quietly seized the opportunity to perform seva.

Swamishri demonstrated that true seva lies not in the scale of the task but in the purity of intention behind it. Through his actions, he reinforced a timeless principle: all seva becomes sacred when performed with love, reverence, and the wholehearted desire to please Bhagwan and the Guru.

title: Ever-Watchful Compassion
text:
After the morning discourse, Anirdesh Swami brought the prasad of badam puri.

But there was a small ant in it, which Swamishri immediately noticed and pointed out.

Seeing such attentiveness at the age of 93, Anirdesh Swami was amazed and said, "Even a tiny ant does not escape your eyes, so we have faith that we will never escape your sight."

Swamishri's ability to notice even the smallest details reflects far more than sharp observation—it reveals his constant care for everyone around him. Just as no ant went unnoticed, no devotee's needs, struggles, or spiritual progress ever escape his loving attention.

title: Pavitram… Pavitram
text:
The attendant swamis asked Swamishri, "In 2017, after you immersed the ashes (of Pramukh Swami Maharaj) at Niagara Falls, you sat down to eat without washing your hands. With profound reverence, you said, 'These hands have immersed the ashes of Pramukh Swami, so there is no need to wash these hands.' Generally, you are very particular about cleanliness, so why did you not wash your hands that day?"

Swamishri replied, "Everything of the Guru is pavitram… pavitram (pure)."

Hearing this, everyone was deeply moved. Swamishri's eyes glowed with devotion as he remembered his beloved Guru. In that moment, it became clear that for Swamishri, Pramukh Swami Maharaj was not just his Guru, but his very life.

title: The Measure of Greatness
text:
After the discourse today, Bhagwatcharan Swami shared, "On August 17, 2016, I was sitting with you in Sarangpur. It was only the two of us in the room. During our conversation, I told you, 'We need to test whether the divine powers of Pramukh Swami Maharaj have manifested in you or not.' To this you replied with great conviction, 'I don't know anything about divine powers or miracles, but if there is any flaw in my observance of the five vows [of a sadhu], then it's your sandals and my head.'"

Bhagwatcharan Swami then added, "But now, we can clearly see the same divine powers of Pramukh Swami Maharaj reflected in you."

Rather than speak of miracles, Swamishri grounded his greatness in discipline, obedience, and purity of conduct.

title: A Thoughtful Glance
text:
After giving his blessings, the curtains closed. Then Swamishri's eyes shifted towards the side where the large electric divo used for the artī was placed. He asked for it to be brought to him. Brahmavatsal Swami handed the divo over, and Swamishri carefully felt its weight in his hands.

Swamishri then remarked, "Only then do we realize how much weight devotees have to lift when they perform the artī."

In that simple moment, it became clear that Swamishri notices even the smallest challenges others face. His care extends to everyone—children, youths, and elders alike—reflecting his constant concern for the well-being and comfort of all who come before him.

title: A Small Connection
text:
Today was a rest day. As per Swamishri's wish, when he went for darshan, he first went to the sabha hall of the Sant Ashram. Then he proceeded to Shastriji Maharaj's room for darshan, where he noticed a cabinet containing items sanctified by Yogiji Maharaj. Inside it, Swamishri spotted a loto (a small metal pot). Pointing to it, he said to Uttamyogi Swami, "That was my loto. I used to keep it when I was a parshad. Yogi Bapa saw it and liked it. So Yogi Bapa asked for it from me."

In this simple moment, Swamishri lovingly recalled a memory of his Guru, showing how deeply he treasures even the smallest connections to Yogiji Maharaj as he keeps those memories alive with reverence and affection throughout his life.

title: Simple Messages
text:
Today was Prabodhini Ekadashi, so various vegetables had been arranged around Swamishri. After his puja, a special question-and-answer session was held on deeper messages from the vegetables.

First, Swamishri picked up potatoes and was asked, "Just as potatoes mix well with everything, what should we do so that we too can blend in with everyone?"
Swamishri answered, "Become simple."

Then Swamishri picked up parvar (pointed gourd) and was asked, "Parvar is known as the king of vegetables, so in Satsang, which one practice is considered like a king?"
Swamishri replied, "Divyabhav!"

Next, Swamishri took broccoli and was asked, "Broccoli is considered a symbol of unity. So how can unity remain among us?"
Swamishri said, "By following all the commands of Maharaj."

title: Lessons in Devotion
text:
Today was Prabodhini Ekadashi, so various vegetables had been arranged around Swamishri. Continuing with the question-and-answer session that explored deeper spiritual messages through these vegetables, the atmosphere remained light yet full of insight.

Swamishri then lifted a bottle gourd (dudhi). Even though it was heavy, he raised it straight up. Remembering Yogiji Maharaj, he said, "When dark clouds gathered, Yogiji Maharaj would lift a dudhi and spin it in front of Viveksagar Swami. If it was about to rain, he would say, 'Go away!'"

Next, Swamishri picked up radishes and was asked, "The belch of radish always comes. Similarly, what should we do so that the 'belch' of Akshar-Purushottam's knowledge always arises within us?"
Swamishri replied simply, "Follow all the commands of Maharaj."

title: The Smallest of Acts
text:
After completing evening arti and ashtak inside Akshardham, Swamishri returned to the sant ashram and had dinner. Afterwards, Manovijay Swami gave a report about the volunteer sabha. He shared, "We decided to maintain a positive attitude; to treat everyone with love. For example, when entering the sabha hall, shoes were not being placed in an orderly line. We didn't say anything, but for two or three sabhas, the volunteers arranged the shoes neatly themselves. Everyone noticed, and from then on, people began placing their shoes in a straight line without being told."

Hearing this, Swamishri said, "Even if the shoes are new, if they are all in a pile, they will look dirty. And even if the shoes are old, when placed properly, they will look good."

Through calm guidance and personal conduct, Swamishri showed that even the smallest acts reflect inner discipline.

title: The Gift He Asks For
text:
Today was Swamishri's 86th birthday celebration. After Swamishri finished his breakfast, Yogimanan Swami asked, "Swami, since it is your birthday today, what can we do to ensure your health remains well?"

Swamishri replied simply, "Niyam–dharma."

With these two words, Swamishri revealed what truly pleases him. More than any external gesture, he asks us to live with firm niyam and dharma. By doing so, we remain connected to him, support his wish, and walk the path he wants us to follow.

title: The Quiet Power of Seva
text:
At 9:16 p.m., the Suryapur Katha-Mangal program began, beautifully portraying the history of satsang in Surat. Around 10:15 p.m., Swamishri returned to his residence, Madhuram Vila, where Suketubhai Sadhak had remained behind to perform seva.

Noting this, Swamishri expressed his happiness and said, "You stayed here and did not watch the program, but everything is included in doing seva. Whatever seva you receive, do it [wholeheartedly], and it will lead you to Akshardham."

Swamishri reminded everyone that sincere seva, even when unseen or unnoticed, holds immense spiritual value. When seva is performed wholeheartedly, it becomes a direct means of pleasing Bhagwan and progressing toward Akshardham.

title: Taking Thakorji Along
text:
Today, Swamishri was scheduled to travel to Jamnagar. As he was seated in the helicopter, Divyapurush Swami stood outside holding Thakorji. Uttamyogi Swami approached to take Thakorji from him, but Divyapurush Swami did not hand Thakorji over and said to Swamishri, "Now we will keep Thakorji here."

At that moment, Swamishri firmly shook his head and insisted that Thakorji must be taken along. He then expressed a profound truth, saying, "Thakorji is present everywhere."

Through this simple yet powerful moment, Swamishri reminded everyone that while Thakorji is all-pervading, our devotion is expressed through care and reverence. By ensuring Thakorji was taken along, Swamishri showed that Bhagwan accompanies us in every journey.

title: Thinking About Thakorji
text:
Swamishri woke around 2:30 a.m. and asked Uttamyogi Swami to call Santcharit Swami, Thakorji's attendant. Uttamyogi Swami inquired, "Swamishri is asking if you have given Akshar-Purshottam Maharaj a warm blanket?"

Santcharit Swami replied, "We have given individual blankets to Maharaj and Swami and have placed a common blanket on top." Still, Swamishri expressed his wish that a warm blanket be properly offered.

Earlier that night, around 2:00 a.m., Swamishri had woken to use the restroom and felt the cold. Due to this, his thoughts immediately turned to Thakorji. The next day, Swamishri shared, "I felt cold last night, and so I remembered Thakorji."

Even a moment of personal discomfort became a reminder to care for Thakorji, revealing a heart that instinctively places Bhagwan first.

title: Reverence Above Comfort
text:
In the morning, Swamishri performed arti and did darshan of the murtis in the mandir. It was then time for him to take his medicine. However, out of deep respect for Thakorji, Swamishri refused to take it there. The attendants suggested alternatives: "Swami, you can sit between the two sanctums," or "You can move a little farther away." None of these were acceptable to Swamishri.

Swamishri then offered his own solution: "[Let's take it] in the pradakshina."

An attendant hesitated, saying, "Swami, it is cold outside."

In his simple, unaffected way, Swamishri replied, "What is cold in that?"

In reality, it was quite cold—around 17°C, with a sharp wind. Yet Swamishri remained firm, choosing respect for Thakorji over personal comfort without a second thought.

title: Unchanged
text:
Today, Swamishri was giving darshan to devotees. Among the devotees was an elderly devotee in a wheelchair named Jodha Bhagat from Gorana. Swamishri saw him, immediately recognized him, and was visibly pleased. He warmly said, "He is my old friend."

In earlier times, Jodha Bhagat had accompanied Yogiji Maharaj, and it was during those days that Swamishri formed a bond of friendship with him. Though many years have passed and circumstances have changed, that feeling of friendship in Swamishri's heart has never faded.

This moment beautifully revealed Swamishri's humility and heartfelt love for devotees. Titles, roles, and time never altered his relationships; he continued to see and cherish devotees with the same warmth and equality as always.

title: Caring for Bhagwan
text:
At 10:30 a.m., arrangements were made to film Swamishri performing the mahāpujā at Akshar Deri. Swamishri arrived and began the pujā with deep focus and devotion. During the ritual, he bathed Shri Akshar-Purushottam Maharaj with pañchāmrut. After Swamishri bathed the murtis with honey, there was a brief pause as the camera angles were adjusted, during which the murtis remained covered in honey.

Sensing Swamishri's intent, Divyapurush Swami bathed Akshar-Purushottam Maharaj with pure water. Swamishri was immediately pleased and expressed his approval. He then said, "Bhagwan had become cold."

Swamishri forever sees Bhagwan as truly present in the murti. His concern was not ritualistic formality, but heartfelt care—seeing, feeling, and serving Bhagwan with the same sensitivity one would show to a living being.

title: Living to Please Others
text:
During a conversation today, someone remarked to Swamishri, "We feel that we are pleasing you, but in truth, you are the one who is pleasing us."

Swamishri agreed, and then, entering a deeply divine mood, said, "My incarnation has occurred solely for the purpose of pleasing [others]."

He further added, "To keep everyone happy, even amidst illness. [I] travel carrying the banner (flag) of pleasing others—to keep everyone happy and to remain happy ourselves."

These words are not merely spoken; they are lived. Swamishri's life consistently reflects a selfless commitment to the happiness of others, revealing a heart that finds its own fulfillment in serving, uplifting, and pleasing everyone around him.

title: Reverence for His Gurus
text:
Swamishri proceeded to the old mud-and-clay house where Shastriji Maharaj and Yogiji Maharaj had resided during the construction of the mandir. He first performed darshan in Shastriji Maharaj's old room and then went to Yogiji Maharaj's room to do darshan there as well.

As Uttamyogi Swami was bringing the wheelchair out of Yogiji Maharaj's room, Swamishri suddenly moved forward, extended his hand, and bent down to touch the threshold of the doorway. However, his hand could not quite reach it. At that moment, Vinaypriya Swami quickly touched the threshold and immediately offered his hand to Swamishri. Swamishri then touched Vinaypriya Swami's hand and bowed in reverence.

His gesture reflected a lifelong humility and love for the Gurus, showing that true devotion sees holiness in every place touched by their presence.

title: Remembered with Love
text:
Swamishri was giving personal meetings to devotees in Sarvasva. Among them was a devotee who had come from Nagpur. Swamishri immediately recognized him and mentioned his home area, saying, "Ingle Chowk."

Indeed, the devotee lived in Ingle Chowk.

This small yet touching moment revealed Swamishri's deep, personal bond with his devotees. Remembering such intimate details was not an act of memory alone, but an expression of genuine love and care. Each devotee lived in his heart, not as a number in a crowd, but as a cherished individual.

title: Bow Down to Everyone
text:
Today, before breakfast, Swamishri was informed about a child named Nilkanth from Mumbai, who is just two years and eleven months old. At such a young age, he has memorized the Satsang Diksha scripture and has become a scholar. Swamishri was deeply pleased.

A photograph of the child was then shown to Swamishri. He folded his hands, gently placed them on the child's head to offer blessings, and then touched the child's feet in reverence. In this way, Swamishri bowed down to him.

After breakfast, Swamishri was asked, "Swami, why did you touch the feet of such a small child?"

Swamishri replied, "He has achieved such a great spiritual feat." He then added, "We must, must, and must bow down to everyone."

Even as the Guru, he joyfully bows before genuine devotion.

title: Process of Becoming Brahmarup
text:
Some makhana (fox nuts) were brought before Swamishri, and the discussion turned to their preparation process. It was explained that makhana become edible and flavorful only after passing through many detailed steps, after which they are finally seasoned.

Hearing this, Swamishri remarked in relation to our spiritual journey, "Only after going through so many steps does it develop its taste. If one does not go through the process, it remains raw. Even if one step is missed, it stays raw. One must go through all the steps."

He conveyed that just as makhana must undergo every stage, a devotee must fully follow the entire process of becoming brahmarup. Victory over maya is not achieved by shortcuts, but through steady, complete, and sincere spiritual effort.

title: Greatness in Humility
text:
During a spiritual discussion with the swamis, the topic of the greatness of attendant swamis arose. At that moment, Swamishri tried to place the hand of an attendant swami who was standing nearby upon his own head. However, realizing Swamishri's intention, the attendant quickly withdrew his hand.

Where can one find such a Guru—one who is ready to receive blessings from his own attendant? Swamishri is truly an ego-free soul. On many occasions, he has performed circumambulations around attendants, bowed at their feet, bowed at the doorway of an attendant's room, bowed even to their dhotiyā, and has offered dandavats to attendants in his dreams.

Though Swamishri sits upon the highest seat as Guru, he lives with the heart of a servant.

title: Seeing Maharaj in Everyone
text:
Today, Swamishri arrived at the sabha held for the swamis. An arrangement had been made for the swamis to perform the artī of Akshar-Purushottam Maharaj together with Swamishri. Accordingly, the stand with Akshar-Purushottam Maharaj was placed in front of Swamishri, with Thakorji facing the swamis, and all the swamis began performing the artī.

As Swamishri observed this, he felt the wish to join in as well. Folding his hands, he began performing the artī. Throughout the entire artī, Swamishri performed it while facing and looking toward the swamis.

After the artī, the swamis asked, "Swami, whose artī were you performing?"
Swamishri simply replied, "Maharaj's."

Wherever Swamishri looks, he sees only Maharaj due to his divine vision.

title: The Manifest Attainment
text:
During his morning blessings, Swamishri shared a profound insight. He said, "Maharaj is manifest through the Sant; truly manifest. His eating, drinking, standing, and sitting appear just like ours. Yet he is divine, beyond this world, and beyond maya, while we remain bound by maya."

He then added, "Even when he stands before us, the thought of our desire for Maharaj's darshan remains unfulfilled. But Maharaj is indeed manifest through the Sant; it is the same here as it is in Akshardham. There is nothing more left to see or attain. We have already attained Maharaj Himself. Everything is encompassed in this darshan—but only if it is understood."

Finally, Swamishri concluded, "If one understands this, they are already seated in Akshardham. If not, they must begin again from the very beginning."

title: Heaven is Akshardham
text:
At night, Swamishri was asked, "Swami, where are we right now?"
Swamishri replied, "Swarg (heaven)."

Uttamyogi Swami then asked, "Not Akshardham?"
Swamishri answered, "We are in Akshardham," and added, "We have attained Maharaj. Therefore, for us, heaven is Akshardham."

At first, one may think of swarg as Indra's heavenly abode. However, the scriptures explain that those who have attained brahmavidya and transcended maya go to heaven, meaning Akshardham itself. Thus, the word swarg is used in the scriptures as a synonym for Akshardham, as clarified in the Karika citing the Kena and Brihadaranyaka Upanishads.

Swamishri revealed heaven is not a distant place to be reached after death, but a state attained through realizing Maharaj in the present. With true prapti, life itself becomes Akshardham.

title: New, New Joy
text:
A two-day Sant Shibir was held with swamis gathering in Sarangpur to participate. During the first session today, Swamishri gave inspiring guidance through an online question-and-answer session.

Although the Zoom call had officially concluded, Swamishri still wanted to share one more thought. He asked for the call to be restarted. Looking at the assembly of swamis on the screen, he said with deep affection, "Seeing all of you brings me so much joy. That is all I wanted to say."

They then asked Swamishri, "Does seeing us (the attendants) bring you joy, or does it feel routine since we are always with you?"

Swamishri instantly replied, "No, no. Seeing you also brings new, new joy."

For Swamishri, seeing his devotees is never old or routine; it is always a source of fresh joy.

title: The Vision of Mahima
text:
After the zoom call with the swamis at the Sant Shibir, the attendant swamis continued their conversation with Swamishri, who shared his divine joy upon seeing the devotees.

Adarshjivan Swami then observed, "That explains why we also get a sense of the new joy on your face when you look at us after cheshta." He continued, highlighting the spiritual principle behind this: "If one has mahima, everything seems new."

Gurumanan Swami added, "In Nenpur, you also told us, 'Every time I see all of you, you look brand new.'"

Moved by this, the swamis prayed, "Please have mercy on us so that we may also feel this way about you."

Swamishri smiled and blessed them, saying, "It will happen."

His constant joy stems from the depth of his understanding, not the novelty of the situation.

title: The Only Ambition
text:
At the Akshar Deri, a question-and-answer session took place between Swamishri and Pujya Bhadresh Swami.

Bhadresh Swami asked Swamishri, "What are your feelings regarding all these child scholars?"

Swamishri replied with deep appreciation, "Wonderful! Wonderful! Everyone has done remarkable work. They have truly surpassed all limits with the amount of effort they have put in. They set everything else aside and immersed themselves in this, so they are truly blessed."

Bhadresh Swami then asked, "What is Gunatitanand Swami telling all these children right now?"

Swamishri replied, "He is simply saying that he wants to make all of you ekāntik in this very life."

His singular goal is to make us ekāntik and grant us Akshardham in this very lifetime.

title: A Prophetic Vision
text:
Continuing the question-and-answer session at the Akshar Deri, Pujya Bhadresh Swami asked Swamishri, "Do you have any other sankalp (wish)?"

Swamishri replied instantly, "My only sankalp is that everyone becomes ekāntik." He then added, "These children are truly blessed!"

Looking toward the future, Bhadresh Swami asked, "Just imagine what it will be like after ten years!"

Speaking prophetically, Swamishri said, "It will become a university!"

Throughout this interaction, Swamishri's face beamed with immense joy, visibly pleased by the children's sincere efforts. His joy reminds us that when we engage in a task that pleases the Guru, he not only blesses our present efforts but ensures a magnificent future for the entire Satsang.

title: The Art of Contemplation
text:
Unable to sleep, Swamishri woke up around 3:30 p.m. and announced, "I want to read."

When Uttamyogi Swami asked if he wished to rest a little longer, Swamishri replied, "How much should I sleep?" He asked for the book Purushottam Bolya Prite and pointed to the chapter on Nirdoshbuddhi and Divyabhav.

He continued reading and thinking while having his afternoon soup and fruit, becoming so absorbed that he did not express a desire to exercise.

When Vednayan Swami asked why he suddenly felt like reading today, Swamishri clarified, "The thought of reading is always there, but I rarely get the time I need."

Swamishri immersed himself until 6:20 p.m. Yet, despite reading for two hours, he did not finish that chapter. He loses track of time diving into the meaning of a single topic.

title: Performing Puja Properly
text:
While taking his bath that morning, Swamishri emphasized the necessity of performing puja properly.

He remarked, "Sleepiness in puja comes from boredom. Bhagwan is present in puja, yet if you doze off, it takes you a mile away from Him."

Uttamyogi Swami asked, "Doesn't sleep also come from a lack of rest?"

Swamishri corrected him, "If the thought, 'I haven't had enough sleep,' remains constantly in your mind, you will never feel fully rested. You perform puja physically, but because your mind isn't engaged, you feel sleepy."

He continued, "Now is the time to improve your puja. If you improve your puja, everything else will automatically fall into place. Puja should be the most precious moment."

title: The Resolve for Samp
text:
In his morning blessings, Swamishri emphasized the foundation of unity: "First, one must decide within oneself that they want to maintain samp (unity)—that is where it begins. Then, one must make an effort for it. This effort requires bowing to one another, compromising, and understanding the other person's mahima (greatness)."

He cautioned, "If one lacks the internal determination that, 'I want to maintain samp,' then no matter how many other spiritual endeavors one performs, they will be in vain."

Swamishri continued, "We often see 'knots' of misunderstanding form between devotees. If such a knot exists, they must drop it immediately and come together. A knot is like dirt; when a knot forms, it turns all your merits to dust."

Unity is a deliberate choice.

title: The Spirit of Equality
text:
After the morning blessings, Swamishri performed the latter half of the arti of the volunteers.

Later, when he woke up in the afternoon, he was asked, "Did you perform half of the arti of the volunteers?"

Swamishri replied, "Yes."

"Why?" the attendant asked.

Swamishri explained, "Their sacrifice and they themselves are just like us. So, just as we bow to one another, [we] performed each other's arti."

He added, "No one is Gujarati or Rajasthani; everyone is the same. All are devotees of Bhagwan."

Swamishri's profound humility shone as he erased regional distinctions and honored the volunteers as his equals. He teaches us to look beyond outer differences and recognize that everyone is a devotee of Bhagwan.

title: Overflowing Love
text:
In the evening, Swamishri arrived at the welcome assembly. Once again, Swamishri performed the arti of the devotees, just as he had done in the morning.

Before dinner, he was asked, "Swami, you performed arti of the devotees again. What was your sentiment behind this?"

Swamishri replied, "Well, this was the first time after such a long time that I was meeting the Rajasthani devotees, so I was filled with strength and divine joy."

Swamishri's heart naturally overflows with love and mahima upon seeing the devotees. It reveals how his strength and energy grow through the joy of connecting with them.

title: Honoring from the Heart
text:
This morning, after waking up, Swamishri expressed a wish: "I want to honor the artisans." It was decided to honor them by tying a pagh (turban), as the turban holds great cultural significance in Rajasthan.

Later, after lunch, Swamishri asked, "When are we going to tie the turbans?" His mind remained focused on the artisans.

He was informed, "The program is scheduled for the 26th. Others will tie the turbans on your behalf while you watch from the cabin."

Swamishri immediately instructed, "Do not do it haphazardly or carelessly. Ensure the turbans are tied properly and respectfully." He emphasized, "How should we view these artisans? They are exactly like us. The only difference is our roles. We must honor them from the heart."

title: The Divine Pull
text:
Before lunch this afternoon, a brief discussion took place regarding small children.

An attendant remarked, "Swami, all these small children have become attached to you. You don't speak much, yet everyone develops love for you. They do so much—mukhpath, austerities. Swami, what is the reason that they all run to you and are ready to do so much?"

Swamishri simply responded, "Bhagwan."
